REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL- R2023-G
Information Technology Consulting Services
Halifax Harbour Bridges (HHB) is seeking proposals from qualified proponents for the provision
of Information Technology Services, as outlined in Section 3.
These services will require a commitment of the resource to be potentially available on-site
minimally 50% to perform any of the roles / services at one of the following locations:
1. 30 Faulkner Street, Dartmouth, NS
2. 125 Wyse Road, Dartmouth, NS
3. 465 Princess Margaret Blvd Dartmouth, NS
Exact effort that will require on-site services will be determined at time of provisioning those
services.
The proposal will be submitted as a pdf by email to dgreenfield@hdbc.ns.ca. Be sure you
receive confirmation of your submitted proposal.
HHB reserves every right to reject any or all proposals and to award the contract partially or
entirely, whichever in its opinion best is suited for HHB.
This agreement in no manner, commits HHB to an exclusive contract for any of these
services. By use of the RFP, HHB intends to obtain the services of various professionals for
projects across the Information Systems department, primarily in the areas of Project
Management, Business Analysis, Change Management, Privacy, Business Architecture and
Technical Architecture.
The RFP is for a three (3) year period from the date of award. HHB reserves the right to
extend beyond the three-year period. HHB does not guarantee any volume of work
associated with the RFP during its term.
David GreenField,
CIO, Tolling & Technology Department

Introduction
About Halifax Harbour Bridges
As a commission of the provincial government, Halifax Harbour Bridges (HHB) was created in
1950 by a statute of the Province of Nova Scotia and reports to the Minister of Public Works
for the Province of Nova Scotia. HHB is a user-pay operation and receives no assistance from
Nova Scotia tax dollars and its loans are not guaranteed by any level of government. All
financing is approved by the Nova Scotia Cabinet and the Nova Scotia Utility and Review
Board approves toll rates set by HHB.
HHB is the forward-thinking, manager of key transportation infrastructure assets in the Halifax
Regional Municipality and maintains and operates the Angus L. Macdonald and A. Murray
MacKay Bridges that span the Halifax Harbour.
With annual traffic volume in excess of 34 million crossings (pre-pandemic), HHB’s mission is
to provide safe, efficient and reliable cross-harbour transportation infrastructure in a cost-
effective manner. At HHB, safety is above all; safety of our employees, safety of our bridges
and safety of the traveling public.
Disclaimer
This Request for Proposals (RFP) is neither an agreement nor an offer. It is only an invitation
by HHB to eligible Proponents to submit their proposals. The purpose of this RFP is to provide
the Proponents with information to assist the formulation of their proposals. The Proponents
are to do their own analysis and investigation for the accuracy and reliability of the RFP.
This is an invitation to join the competition of the selection process. No contractual obligation
shall arise from the RFP process until there is a final formal contract between HHB and the
awarded vendor.

Section 1: Submission Instructions to Proponents
1.1 Basic Instructions
Proponents are required to follow the instructions below.
a. Proponents are to read the Request for Proposal (RFP) thoroughly.
b. Proponents to follow the instructions in Section 4 to respond as a proposal.
c. HHB will assume no liability of any kind of oral instructions or suggestions. All
correspondence regarding the RFP should be directed to David Greenfield, CIO,
HHB using the email dgreenfield@hdbc.ns.ca
d. Proposal must be signed by an authorized signatory of the proponent.
e. Proponent can only withdraw their submission before the deadline. A valid
official letter of explanation must be sent to the contact person.
f. HHB reserves all right to make additional copy of the proposal only for internal
use or any other purpose required by the procurement law.
1.2 Eligibility criteria
Only the proponents who meet the following criteria are eligible to submit the proposal.
a. The proponents shall be registered corporate and legally entitled to do business
in Canada. HHB reserves the right to request supporting documents (Sales Tax/
Registration Certificate) if required.
b. Proponent should comply with Nova Scotia Business Names Registration Act or
similar types of act if proponent(s) are applying from outside Nova Scotia.
c. Prospective proponents shall comply with all the laws in effect in the province
of Nova Scotia, without regard to the conflict of laws rules thereof.
d. Proponents shall comply with Nova Scotia Procurement Policy Act and all
governing law applicable to do business in Nova Scotia.
1.3 Proponents Expenses
Proponents shall bear all the cost associated with the preparation and submission of
the proposal. Proponents will be solely responsible or liable for any costs related to the
preparation of the RFP. HHB will in no case be responsible for any cost related to the
bidding process.
1.4 Late Submission
Any RFP received after the above deadline will be automatically disqualified from the
competition and further evaluation will not be done for that RFP.
1.5 Addenda and Amendments
Addenda may be issued during the proposal period. All addenda shall become part of
the RFP documents. Proponents are responsible for receiving all addenda and including
them in the submitted proposal documents. Proposals that do not reference all
addenda may be immediately returned and the proponent eliminated from further
consideration.
Amendments to the submitted proposal will be permitted if received in writing prior to
proposal call closing and if endorsed by the same party or parties who signed the
original proposal.
Any required addenda will be issued no later than three working days before the
Proposal Call Close. Verbal answers are only binding when confirmed by written
addenda.

1.6 Proprietary Information
Materials submitted in response to this competitive procurement shall become
property of HHB.
1.7 Public Information
The Proponents are advised that HHB is subject to the Freedom of Information and
Protection of Privacy Act (“FOIPOP”), SNS 1993, c.5, s.1. The FOIPOP Act is an “Act
Respecting the Right of Access to Documents of Public Bodies in Nova Scotia and a
Right of Privacy with Respect to Personal Information Held by Public Bodies in Nova
Scotia”.
Subject to limited exceptions, all information under the control of HHB is subject to
public review under FOIPOP, including information related to this RFP. In the event a
Proponent desires to claim portions of his/her proposal as exempt from public
disclosure, the Proponent must identify those portions in the letter of transmittal. Each
page of the proposal claimed to be exempt must be clearly identified as “confidential.”
In the event that an access request is received by HHB for such confidential
information, HHB will notify the affected Proponent, but HHB will determine whether
any or all of the claimed exemptions are protected from disclosure under FOIPOP. The
ultimate decision rests with the courts of Nova Scotia.
1.8 Confidentiality
The proponent agrees not to release or in any way cause to release any
confidential information of HHB without HHB’s express written consent.
1.9 Acceptance of RFP/Proposal Content
By submitting a proposal, the Proponent certifies that the proponent has read,
understood, and agreed to all requirements, terms, and conditions in this
RFP, including any and all attachments, exhibits, and appendices. A proponent
may withdraw his/her proposal prior to the RFP proposal deadline.
1.10 Disqualified for false information
Proponent(s) are required to provide the factual response to this RFP. Proper
justification for the response should be attached (technical, documents) as a part of
response. In case of any inadequate information, HHB holds the rights to ask for
additional explanation. In terms of discrepancy HHB reserves the right to disqualify
the proponent(s) to participate in the competition.

Section 2: Terms and Conditions
It is the expectation that the following terms and conditions will be incorporated into the final
contract agreed to by the proponent and HHB. If the proponent has any concerns with any of
these terms and conditions listed below these are to be outlined in the proponent’s proposal.
2.1 Payment Authority
The payment as per contract will be made by the Tolling & Technology Department on
behalf of HHB. Any payment, related questions and concerns will be forwarded to the
CIO, HHB.
2.2 Force Majeure
Neither party shall be liable for any damages delays or failure in performance under
this agreement caused by acts or conditions beyond its reasonable control or without
its fault or negligence (a “Force Majeure Event”), including but not limited to “acts of
God”, delays caused by governmental authorities, strikes, lockouts and other labour
unrest, delays in obtaining governmental approvals and similar conditions. A Party
shall, in order to avail itself of any of the provisions of this section, forthwith send a
written notice of the Force Majeure Event to the other party, including a description of
the Force Majeure event, its expected duration and a description of the actions being
taken by the party to mitigate the effect of the Force Majeure event.
2.3 Indemnity
The proponent agrees to indemnify and hold harmless HHB, its officers and employees
from and against claims, demands, losses, costs, damages, actions, suits, or
proceeding hereinafter called "claims", by third parties that arise out of or are
attributable to the proponent's performance of the contract provided such claims are
attributable to bodily injury, sickness, disease, or death, or to injury to or destruction
of tangible property and caused by negligent acts or omissions of the contractor or
anyone for whose acts the proponent may be liable. The proponent agrees to indemnify
HHB, its officers and employees against any claims or costs initiated by third parties
as a result of any negligence or wrongful acts of the proponent or its employees.
2.4 Insurance
2.4.1 Professional and General Insurance
Prior to finalizing a contract, the successful proponent will be asked to provide
confirmation of insurance coverage for review by HHB. HHB will require the successful
proponent to obtain the following coverages:
1. Professional liability insurance – not less than $5 million
2. General liability insurance – not less than $1 million
2.4.2 Workers’ Compensation
If required by the applicable legislation, the proponent shall register as an employer
under workers' compensation legislation in Nova Scotia, and covenants that it shall
maintain such registration in good standing at all times that the proponent is providing
services hereunder.
2.4.3 Proof of Insurance
At any time, HHB may require proof of such insurance policies in the form of certificates
of insurance, which shall be provided by the proponent at its expense.

2.13 Termination
2.13.1 Termination on Default
If HHB is of the view, acting reasonably, that the proponent has not performed or

2.13.2 Termination for Convenience
HHB may terminate the signed agreement, in whole or in part, whenever it

2.13.3 Insolvency

Section 3: Scope of work and Deliverables
3.1 Project Background
HHB manages critical infrastructures on both the Angus L. Macdonald Bridge (ALMB)
and the A. Murray MacKay Bridge (AMMB). This includes a surveillance system, traffic
management system, toll collection and payment system, different Internet of Things
(IoT) systems and internal corporate servers and applications.
The purpose of this Request of Proposal (RFP) is to invite prospective service providers
to submit a proposal to HHB’s Tolling & Technology Department who require consulting
services to support numerous project work identified the five-year Strategic Plan. HHB
engaged all business lines in lengthy planning exercises to produce this plan and have
identified several projects that will require staff augmentation, primarily in the areas
outlined in this Section. These are roles where HHB has identified long term initiatives.
There will be other Tenders and RFPs over the duration of this RFP for other initiatives
requiring other unique skills and materials. Those requests will be tendered separately.
The initial term length will be three (3) years, with options to renew yearly for up to
two (2) additional one (1) year terms. Renewals are not guaranteed and will be solely
at HHB discretion based on provider performance of the contract and current market
conditions. The maximum contract will be five (5) years before a full market renewal
will be undertaken.
3.2 Scope of Work
HHB will contract with a qualified service provider for the roles listed in Section 3.
HHB will endeavor to provide an equal opportunity for firms to respond, bearing in
mind that some firms have specific experience and/or skills in particular areas that
may limit the opportunity for other firms to submit proposals.
Successful proponents will be expected to enter into a Professionals Services
Agreement outing the specific work tasks and terms and conditions as required.
3.3 Services
HHB will require professional consulting services for the following roles:
3.3.1 Project Manager (up to three)
This requirement is for project management professionals (PMP) with a minimum of
five (5) years of experience delivering projects for other government organizations.
Work may include carrying out project initiation (production of project charters and
stakeholder registers), planning (production of project management plans, including
plans for each knowledge area), executing (ensuring work is issued and being acted
upon), monitoring & controlling (keeping the project on track and making plan
adjustments and change requests as required) and closing (orderly shutdown of
contracts, recording of lessons learned, possibly reviewing related future phases).
3.3.2 Business Analyst (up to two)
This requirement is for business analyst professionals to perform a structured method
of bringing about and identify existing and new business processes within HHB. Such
experience will include facilitating business process reviews in terms of current
situation and future situation mapping, gathering business requirements, creating
documentation (process models and descriptions), identifying trouble areas, providing
Information Technology Consulting Services
Page: 18
solution recommendations and communicating changes needed/shortfalls. Preference
will be given to certified individuals (CBAP or PMI-PBA) with three (3) years of
experience in delivering projects for other government organizations.
3.3.3 Privacy Analyst (up to two)
This requirement is for privacy analyst professionals that will support HHB’s
organization's privacy programs and policies. The privacy analyst will reinforce
business and data management processes and procedures that comply with privacy
laws and regulations while providing remediation processes. The privacy analyst will
also assist in coordinating and delivering privacy training programs, communications,
and training materials. Additionally, the privacy analyst will conduct research, analysis,
and reporting on the impacts of new legal changes or of potential policy changes.
Preference will be given to candidates with at least three (3) years of experience in
delivering projects for other government organizations.
3.3.4 Technical Architect (maximum one)
This requirement is for technical architect professionals who are capable of designing,
implementing, and overseeing technical roadmap development for HHB IT systems.
The technical architect will have responsibility for designing the structure of new
technology systems and liaising with the software development team. Preference will
be given to candidates with at least five (5) years of experience in a technical architect
role delivering projects for other government organizations.
3.3.5 Business Architect (maximum one)
This requirement is for business architect professionals who are capable of performing
a strategic role to allow HHB to adapt the business processes to be more agile and
productive. The business architect will champion the structuring of the HHB’s business

Dear ,
On behalf of CGI, I would like to thank you for giving us the opportunity to provide you with a proposal for the R2023-G – Information Technology Consulting Services RFP.

CGI is a global information technology leader with headquarters in Canada. As a Canadian company we are invested in the success of Canada, and by extension each of the provinces.  The Atlantic Business Unit of CGI is eager to build on our relationship with the Halifax Harbour Bridges (HHB) and provide top quality resources to help HHB achieve success in their initiatives.

When HHB chooses CGI to trust as their partner to deliver the Professional Services, we will approach the relationship as a true partnership with HHB. For more information about Pivot Consulting, please refer to Appendix C. With our combined expertise and innovative approach along with a high quality local and larger talent pool, we can offer HHB a comprehensive range of expertise and services. This will not only meet HHB needs but also exceed the expectations while providing increased efficiencies and cost savings on this five-year strategic journey. Understanding of the Requirements

CGI understands that Halifax Harbour Bridges (HHB) manages and maintains the critical cross Harbour infrastructure that allows Halifax to be the preeminent economic centre in Atlantic Canada, this includes the infrastructure of both the Angus L. Macdonald Bridge (ALMB) and the A. Murray MacKay Bridge (AMMB). Managing the bridges entails the management and operations of surveillance systems, traffic management systems, toll collections, payment systems, IoT (Internet of Things) and other internal infrastructure.

HHB’s Tolling and Technology department is in the need of consulting services to support work on numerous projects that is emanating from the long term 5-year strategic plan that HHB put together recently and is currently in the process of undertaking. This strategic plan will serve as a blueprint for HHB in its mission of providing safe, efficient, and reliable cross harbour infrastructure in a cost effective manner. The primary goals and outcomes of this strategic plan are following:
Goal 1 – Improve safety, efficiency and environmental stewardship in operations and maintenance
Goal 2 – Provide customer value through seamless, reliable and safe bridge crossing
Goal 3 – Demonstrate financial sustainability
Goal 4 – Create a workplace where employees thrive
Goal 5 – Establish a culture and practice of innovation

The two bridges are critical pieces of transportation infrastructure in the HRM (Halifax Regional Municipality) and in the province of Nova Scotia and with increasing traffic demands and age of the infrastructure itself, it is critical that HHB, as the custodian of the bridges, continues to monitor and evaluate and undertake the necessary capital projects to ensure the safe operation of the bridges through the use of technology, both, for the short and long term. The additional support required as part of this RFP is primarily in the areas of IT Project Management, Business Analysis, Privacy Analysis, Business and Technical Architecture, and Change Management as these are roles where HHB has identified key long-term initiatives ready to begin under the 5-year strategic plan.

The team members chosen to work alongside HHB will be well supported by the expertise CGI has in this transportation market. One of the early ways the team will contribute to the success of this transformational work is to quickly integrate with HHBs internal teams and understand what considerations, and factors impact the smooth operation of the bridges. As an example, we can extrapolate that with the ever-increasing population of HRM, the amount of bridge use must be increasing. Of course, this can be contrasted with what we expect was a significant drop in flow during the Pandemic, and with the work from home model/hybrid adopted by a lot of organizations, the flow still has not returned to pre-pandemic levels. We suspect the latter (Pandemic) has a bigger impact on the flow, than the former (Population Growth). Understanding various key indicators along with current and forecasted use metrics will enable our team to deliver value to HHB quickly and efficiently, minimizing consultant onboarding time.

The team understands that some of the technologies that are used need updating, and some of this has already been announced publicly. Replacement of the MacPass transponder system with a more automated service will benefit both the traveling public and HHB. The traveling public will potentially have a slightly faster commute, and less delays at the toll plaza, while HHB will see a reduction in incidents at the toll plazas. No one wants to see trucks in the wrong lane more than HHB we expect.

Additional safety improvements can also be a benefit to HHB, with the use of automated ticketing for excessive speed, or unsafe driving on the bridge. This will help drive revenues, but more importantly as a safety measure, will hopefully lower collisions, and result in smoother traffic flow. As a team CGI Is invested in being a part of the HHB legacy and assisting the organization to be the most technically agile it can be as it looks to future decades.

1. INTRODUCTION
1.1. NSLC Overview
The Nova Scotia Liquor Corporation (NSLC) is one of Nova Scotia’s largest retailers. For
almost 100 years, the NSLC has been managing the safe and responsible sale of beverage
alcohol in Nova Scotia, returning 100% of its profits to government to help fund key public
services. In 2018, the NSLC was given an additional mandate as the only authorized retailer
of cannabis in the province.
Operating more than 100 retail stores across the province, the NSLC also provides service
to more than 60 Agency Stores, four Private Wine & Specialty stores, and 2,100 licensed
establishments. The NSLC and its employees touch virtually every community in Nova
Scotia.
The Information Technology Business Unit (ITBU) within the NSLC plays a key role in
enabling the strategic direction of the business and in supporting day to day operations.
There are 2 teams within the ITBU: The Business & Technology Solutions team is involved
on the project delivery side, providing solutions to business needs that merge business
process and software configuration. The IT Services team supports the NSLC’s
Infrastructure & Cybersecurity landscape and provides overall hardware & application
support to the organization.
The NSLC is seeking a strategic partner to establish and operate a Microsoft Centre of
Excellence (CoE) that will serve as a catalyst for digital transformation across the
organization. With limited internal IT capacity and a rapidly evolving Microsoft ecosystem,
NSLC requires a managed service model that not only supports day-to-day operations but
also drives long-term innovation.
The result of this RFP will be the negotiation of a multi-year master services contract
support, maintenance, enhancements and further strategic evolution of the Microsoft
platform. The initial focus will be the managed service and building a roadmap for
transformation.
1.2. RFP Purpose
This RFP invites proposals from experienced Microsoft service providers who can deliver a
flexible, scalable, and insight-driven CoE. The selected partner will work closely with the
NSLC to optimize licensing, enhance governance, prepare for AI capabilities like Microsoft
Copilot, and ensure alignment with provincial regulatory frameworks.
Our goal is to build a sustainable technology foundation that improves operational
efficiency, and build a roadmap for ongoing modernization.

Cybersecurity is out of scope (handled separately), but basic compliance (and use of tools

1.3.2. Technology Approach and Adoption Profile
The NSLC has an established approach of purchasing packaged software from reputable
vendors and then maximizing the use of platform supported functions, minimizing custom
coding. Given this tenant, the NSLC expects the successful proponent to bring knowledge
and best practices to ensure we remain as standard as possible.
The NSLC utilizes a corporate Technology Adoption profile which places us behind the risky
forefront of new technologies. The NSLC will generally prefer proven technologies, including
those for which skill sets have achieved some degree of maturity in the industry.
The NSLC will continue to evolve the use of its Microsoft systems over the coming years.

Letter of Introduction
CGI is proud to present NSLC with our proposal for SR-18-FY26 – Microsoft: Centre of Excellence Partner.

NSLC is seeking a strategic Microsoft Centre of Excellence partner to support three core objectives: reliable day-to-day operations, strong governance and cost control, and a structured path to future innovation. CGI’s proposed Microsoft CoE has been designed explicitly to align with these objectives, balancing operational stability, fiscal discipline, and long-term sustainability within a regulated retail environment.

CGI is uniquely positioned to support NSLC through a delivery model that combines local executive leadership in Atlantic Canada with proven Microsoft platform expertise delivered through our Canadian Centres of Excellence. Our engagement with NSLC will be led by senior CGI leadership based in Atlantic Canada, providing direct accountability, executive engagement, and a deep understanding of regional public-sector and retail operating contexts. This local leadership is complemented by CGI’s Microsoft 365 Centre of Excellence in Quebec City, which delivers enterprise-scale managed services and governance capabilities to large, regulated organizations across Canada. This combination of proximity and depth distinguishes CGI from providers that rely on offshore delivery or fragmented subcontracting models

CGI is proudly Canadian, founded and headquartered in Canada, with decades of experience supporting public-sector and regulated clients nationwide. All services proposed for NSLC will be delivered within Canada, ensuring no corporate risk arising from international data storage and full alignment with NSLC’s security, privacy, and regulatory requirement

CGI’s proposed CoE emphasizes Year-1 operational stability, focusing on Microsoft 365 support, SharePoint stabilization, DevOps enablement, identity management, and license optimization—aligned with NSLC’s stated priorities and budget guidance. From this stable foundation, the CoE provides a phased roadmap toward stronger governance, automation, and innovation, enabling NSLC to adopt capabilities such as Power Platform and Microsoft 365 Copilot when organizational readiness and business priorities align.

Our delivery model is built on partnership, transparency, and accountability. Services are delivered through a block-hours managed service aligned to NSLC business hours, supported by defined governance and escalation mechanisms. CGI remains end-to-end accountable for service delivery and acts as NSLC’s single point of coordination for Microsoft-related escalation

In choosing CGI, NSLC gains a trusted Canadian partner with local leadership, national delivery depth, and a proven ability to operate and evolve mission-critical Microsoft environments at a measured, low-risk pace.
Thank you for the opportunity to submit this proposal. We appreciate your consideration and look forward to the possibility of partnering with NSLC.
Mandatory Conditions
Laws of Nova Scotia

CGI explicitly confirms and agrees that any agreement(s) resulting from this Request for Proposal will be governed by the laws of the Province of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable therein.
Corporate Capabilities and Experience

CGI confirms that it possesses the required corporate capabilities and experience to deliver both Project Implementation and Managed Services for Microsoft solutions. CGI has extensive expertise in implementing, managing, and supporting Microsoft technologies across complex enterprise environments, ensuring high-quality service delivery aligned with industry best practices.
Data Storage Protection

CGI acknowledges and fully adheres to the ’s data residency requirements. CGI confirms that no  data will be stored in the United States. All data associated with the delivery of services under this RFP will be stored and managed exclusively within Canada, in accordance with ’s data protection policies and the sensitive nature of the products it sells.
Data Protection Agreement (Schedule A)
CGI agrees to NSLC’s Data Protection Agreement.
Corporate Suitability
Corporate Overview
Corporate Expertise

Founded in 1976, CGI is Canada’s largest independent IT services firm and the world’s fifth largest, with approximately 95,500 professionals operating in more than 40 countries. CGI has a strong presence in Nova Scotia, with over 350 professionals based in Halifax, supported by approximately 800 resources across Atlantic Canada and an additional 11,000 professionals throughout the rest of Canada.

Partnership and quality are central to CGI’s values, and disciplined quality processes have long been a cornerstone of our operations. In 1994, CGI became the first IT services company in North America to achieve ISO 9001 certification for its Project Management Framework. CGI has since achieved ISO 9001 quality certification across all three of its stakeholder management frameworks, covering clients, members, and shareholders.

CGI’s Microsoft services and expertise are delivered through a global practice comprising more than 25,000 Microsoft professionals across 40+ countries. This practice is supported by 12 dedicated Microsoft Centres of Excellence, including centres located in Canada, the United States, India, France, and other regions.
Our current percentage of employee turnover within the area of CGI that will support ’s Centre of Excellence is 12%.

CGI has substantial experience working with Canadian retailers, Canadian government organizations, and liquor jurisdictions. We are currently providing Azure project and support services to Ontario’s The Beer Store (see Reference #4 in Section 4.4). In addition, CGI has several IT and business consulting engagements underway with Quebec’s Liquor Corporation (SAQ – Société des alcools du Québec) and with the Nova Scotia Provincial Government.

CGI has successfully executed more than 50 projects with the Province of Nova Scotia, utilizing the AMANDA software platform for regulatory applications and licensing, demonstrating our ability to manage complex government initiatives. Our experience with the Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission included the modernization and enhancement of regulatory applications, further showcasing our expertise within liquor jurisdictions. We have also worked with the Saskatchewan Liquor and Gaming Authority (SLGA) to deliver an ERP financial system upgrade, including enhancements to the General Ledger, Accounts Payable, Asset Management, Accounts Receivable, Billing, and Purchasing modules.
Evidence of CGI’s up-to-date business liability insurance can be found in Appendix A.
Partner Location
CGI’s primary business location in Nova Scotia is located at 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1007, Halifax, NS B3L 2C2. This office serves as a key hub for our IT and consulting services in the region.

For the  contract, the remote services location will be CGI’s M365 CoE in Quebec City. All services will therefore be delivered within Canada with seamless support enables through strong collaboration practices and full alignment to NSLC standard business hours (Atlantic time) and no international data storage risk.
Subcontracting

CGI does not use subcontractors for this engagement. CGI’s preference is to provide  with CGI staff for the contract requirements ensuring continuity, accountability and longe term retention for NSLC-specific knowledge while reducing overhead and maintaining a high standard of services quality.
Data Storage Protection

CGI acknowledges and fully adheres to the ’s data residency requirements. CGI confirms that no  data will be stored in the United States. All data associated with the delivery of services under this RFP will be stored and managed exclusively within Canada and in accordance with ’s data protection policies and the sensitive nature of the products it sells.
No production, development or test data will be stored outside of ’s Microsoft 365 tenant. No  data will be stored in CGI data centres.
Business Continuity Plan

CGI maintains a mature, enterprise-wide Business Continuity and Resilience framework designed to ensure consistent, uninterrupted service delivery for mission-critical public sector systems, including justice and court environments. This framework addresses both workforce continuity and technology or service interruptions and is regularly reviewed and tested.
Employee Turnover Continuity

CGI ensures resource continuity through a structured approach that combines skilled workforce management, comprehensive documentation, and a scalable resourcing model. New resources are selected based on proven expertise and relevant experience and are integrated seamlessly into existing teams through standardized onboarding and formal knowledge transfer processes. Leveraging up-to-date documentation and cross-functional collaboration across skillsets, CGI enables rapid skill alignment, consistent service quality, and uninterrupted delivery even when onboarding new team members. This approach ensures operational stability, minimizes knowledge loss, and maintains productivity across all service and project engagements for the client.
Additional workforce continuity measures include:
Low Turnover and Workforce Stability: CGI maintains low turnover within its justice and public sector practices, supported by long-tenured professionals and active retention programs.
Role Redundancy and Cross-Training: All critical roles have designated backups, with cross-training to reduce reliance on individual resources.
Centralized Knowledge Management: Project documentation, configuration assets, operational procedures, and code repositories are centrally maintained to support rapid onboarding and continuity.
Standardized Delivery Frameworks: Established CGI delivery models, governance structures, and quality controls ensure consistency regardless of team composition.
Succession and Transition Planning: Proactive resource planning and structured handover processes ensure continuity during planned or unplanned staff transitions.
Technology and Service Interruption Continuity
CGI’s continuity strategy for technology and service interruptions includes:
Resilient Infrastructure: Use of highly available, cloud-based platforms including Microsoft Azure with built-in redundancy, automated failover, and geographic resilience.
Disaster Recovery and Backup: Regularly tested backup and disaster recovery procedures with defined Recovery Time Objectives and Recovery Point Objectives aligned to service criticality.
24x7 Monitoring and Incident Management: Continuous system monitoring and a formal incident response process ensure rapid detection, escalation, and resolution of service disruptions.
Controlled Change and Release Management: Structured change, testing, and deployment processes minimize the risk of service outages.
Business Continuity Testing: Periodic continuity and disaster recovery exercises validate readiness and drive continuous improvement.
Assurance of Uninterrupted Service Delivery

Through workforce stability, scalable resourcing, comprehensive documentation, and resilient technology operations, CGI ensures consistent, uninterrupted service delivery. These measures enable CGI to meet service level commitments, minimize operational risk, and support the ongoing availability of critical court and justice services.
Corporate Capabilities & Experience
Technical Qualifications
Microsoft Partner Status

CGI and Microsoft share a vision for innovation. Using Microsoft’s technology, CGI delivers enterprise services and solutions that drive enterprise agility, collaboration, and innovation. CGI is a globally-managed Enterprise Solutions Integrator partner. Under Microsoft’s new Microsoft AI Cloud Partner Program, CGI is a Microsoft Cloud Partner that has achieved all six Solutions Partner designations. CGI is also a member of the Microsoft Intelligent Security Association (MISA) with Microsoft-verified Managed XDR (Extended Detection and Response) solution status.

CGI’s service offering and expertise with Microsoft is a global offering, with more than 25,000 Microsoft professionals in 40+ countries, as well as 12 dedicated Centres of Excellence for Microsoft practices in countries like Canada, USA, India, France and more.

CGI has a dedicated partner manager at the corporate level who helps to coordinate relationships with Microsoft’s local partner and account teams to develop solutions for specific clients. CGI is a regular participant at Microsoft Ignite where partners learn about Microsoft’s roadmap for the upcoming year, network and build connections, share best practices, experience the latest product innovations, and learn new skills and techniques.

CGI has achieved the status of Solutions Partner for Modern Work in the Microsoft Cloud Partner Program. This designation demonstrates our competency in implementing Microsoft 365 and assisting clients during their deployment of Microsoft 365 services and subsequent operation of the platform.
This designation is highly relevant since  requires a partner that has the expertise to manage the Microsoft 365 platform and to provide extended services.

CGI is one of Microsoft’s top Canadian partners invited to participate in Modern Work market accelerators in 2025/26: Jumpstart for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Jumpstart for Secure AI Productivity. We would be happy to hold workshops on these themes with  representatives at no cost to .

CGI has received multiple partner of the year awards from Microsoft in different geographical locations around the globe including Canada, the United Kingdom and Sweden. As part of our close relationship, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has spoken about CGI innovations in IoT and augmented reality at major Microsoft events.

We have a strong commitment to training and certification for employees working with Microsoft 365. CGI’s approach to professional development includes ongoing training, participation in major industry events such as Microsoft Ignite, and continuous alignment with Microsoft’s product roadmap and release cadence. This ensures that CGI’s consultants remain at the forefront of innovation, best practices, and compliance standards in Microsoft 365.

Within our key personnel, the M365 SME-Subject Matter Expert who will be assigned to the  contract (Mr. Laurent Grados) is Microsoft-certified as an Identity and Access Administrator. He also holds the Security, Compliance and Identity Fundamentals and Azure Fundamentals certifications.
Experience Delivering M365 Services

Our Canadian M365 CoE has been delivering M365 services for the last 9 years and consists of around 40 members. We created a permanent M365 team in Sept. 2016 for our first project which was a 330-user migration project from on-premise services to M365 for a client in France called Butachimie. Since that time, we have successfully delivered M365 projects involving more than 255,000 users in client organizations based in Canada (SNC Lavalin, Yellow Pages, VIA Rail, Industrial Alliance, Quebec Provincial Government, Canadian Federal Government), in the US (KinderCare Learning Centers, CSL Behring, Miraclon) and in France (TOTAL Energies, Michelin).

The largest project that our M365 CoE has delivered was a migration of 76,500 users in 130 countries to Microsoft 365 for TOTAL Energies, one of the largest energy companies in the world. This project included the migration of 90,105 mailboxes, user training, post-migration support and the administration of all M365 services for a 12-month period.
Power Platform Centre of Excellence Expertise

CGI has several Power Platform Centers of Excellence around the world. Our CoE in the Quebec province has been delivering Power Platform services for the last 8 years and consists of around 50 members, including architects, analysts and developers. We offer clients the following services:
Governance: oversight of citizen developer activities and application lifecycle management
AMS: Application development and management services for Power Apps, Power Automate and Power BI
Industrialized software engineering: Factory-like custom software development on-demand
Integration: implementation of services and platform connections as reusable components
Consulting: Supporting innovation and initiatives through our experience and technical know-how

We bring proven, repeatable expertise in Power Platform governance and Center of Excellence implementation—both with our clients and within CGI—so innovation scales with control. Using our “Runway” framework to implement best practices and proper management and thus ensuring velocity, we establish pragmatic guardrails (environment strategy, DLP-Data Loss Protection policies, role-based access, and solution ALM-Application Lifecycle Management) that balance speed with safety. We deploy and tailor the Microsoft Power Platform Center of Excellence application to instrument the tenant end to end—inventory, telemetry, and dashboards for applications, flows, makers, and connectors. This foundation accelerates adoption while keeping data secure, costs transparent, and compliance auditable across client business units.

Our CoE in the Quebec province has successfully delivered Power Platform projects for client organizations based in Canada (VIA Rail, Quebec Provincial and Municipal Government, Rio Tinto Alcan, Cree Schoolboard, Hydro-Quebec, Technical Safety BC, Bell, Legislative Assembly of Manitoba, Fondaction), in the US (City of Austin, SCP Health) and in Europe through our global CGI partnerships (EDF, Airbus, SNCF).
Microsoft 365 Copilot Implementation Experience

CGI has extensive experience in implementing Microsoft’s generative artificial intelligence tool - M365 Copilot. Our Canadian M365 CoE is responsible for assisting clients in the adoption of the tool.

CGI is a qualified Microsoft Partner to assist  since we hold the second highest level in the Microsoft Jumpstart program for M365 Copilot: "Ready Tier". This level demonstrates that CGI has an established M365 Copilot practice. Our M365 Center of Excellence in Canada is currently engaged in an audit with Microsoft in order to graduate to the highest level: "Prioritized Tier".

CGI has successfully supported several public and private-sector organizations with the deployment and adoption of M365 Copilot and cloud-based AI capabilities. Our M365 CoE leverages repeatable, field-tested methodologies, training materials, templates, technical frameworks and governance models refined through multiple M365 Copilot engagements. Our standard framework called “12-weeks to M365 Copilot Adoption” enables CGI to deliver:
Comprehensive readiness assessments
Structured pilot planning and execution
Technical configuration aligned with security and governance requirements
User onboarding, training, and adoption support

Onboarding Methodology and Approach

Based on the scope of services requested by NSLC and CGI’s experience delivering similar managed service engagements, we are confident that a four-week transition (onboarding) period is appropriate and provides sufficient time to establish a strong operational foundation, gain a thorough understanding of the current environment, and minimize risk to NSLC.

The onboarding approach is designed to ensure continuity of service, clear operational readiness, and effective knowledge transfer. The transition period is structured into three phases, bookended by formal milestones, as outlined below.

Transition Kickoff meeting (Week 1): A formal transition kickoff meeting will be held to introduce the CGI and NSLC teams, confirm scope and objectives, review the transition approach, and initiate the Microsoft CoE Services onboarding activities.

Phase 1 – Transition Discovery (Week 1): This due diligence phase focuses on establishing a clear and validated understanding of NSLC’s current-state environment. Activities include reviewing NSLC-provided documentation related to Microsoft 365, Access databases, and DevOps configurations, as well as understanding NSLC’s operational processes, organizational structure, and support tools. During this phase, CGI will begin developing the Operational Framework document that will govern service delivery throughout the contract.

Phase 2 - Transition Planning (Week 2): During this phase, CGI will design the detailed transition plan, develop the associated work breakdown structure (WBS), and define Go-Live acceptance criteria. These criteria will address both NSLC and CGI prerequisites and are intended to ensure operational readiness and reduce transition risk prior to service takeover.
Phase 3 - Transition Execution (Weeks 3 to 4): This phase will be executed across multiple coordinated workstreams:
Operational framework stream: Finalization, validation, and approval of the Operational Framework sections related to Microsoft managed services.
Knowledge transfer stream: Structured knowledge transfer workshops to facilitate effective transition of operational knowledge between NSLC support agents and CGI support agents.
Tools stream: Specification, implementation, and validation of reporting and access required for CGI within the NSLC ticketing system.

Support and administration onboarding stream: Phased onboarding of CGI resources, including shadowing of NSLC support agents by CGI, followed by reverse shadowing to validate readiness and reduce operational risk.

Go-Live meeting (end of Week 4): A Go-Live meeting will be held to review and validate that all transition acceptance criteria have been met. NSLC approval is required prior to confirming the Go-Live date and commencing billing for CGI support services. The Go-Live date typically occurs at the beginning of Week 5.

This onboarding approach is aligned with NSLC’s Year 1 priorities, which focus on operational stability. Upon Go-Live, CGI will assume responsibility for SharePoint Online operations and ensure ongoing stability of the Access database environment. The setup of DevOps services will be initiated once a separate statement of work is developed by CGI and approved by .

DEFINITIONS
Throughout this Request for Proposals, the following definitions apply:
a) “Artificial Intelligence” or “AI” refers to a set of digital technologies that enable systems to
perform cognitive functions such as learning, problem-solving, and decision-making. AI
may be used to augment or automate processes.
b) “Generative AI” refers to a subset of AI technologies designed to produce new content
such as text, images, simulations, audio or code based on patterns learned from data.
c) “HPEI” refers to Health PEI
d) “Contract” means the written agreement resulting from this Request for Proposals
executed by Health PEI and the Contractor;
e) “Contractor” means the successful Proponent to this Request for Proposals who enters
into a written contract with Health PEI;
f) “must”, or “mandatory” means a requirement that must be met in order for a proposal to
receive consideration;
g) “Proponent” means an individual or a company that submits, or intends to submit, a
proposal in response to this Request for Proposals;
h) “Request for Proposals” or “RFP” means the process described in this document; and
i) “Should” or “desirable” means a requirement having a significant degree of importance to
the objectives of the Request for Proposals.

PART 1 – INVITATION AND SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS
1.1 Invitation to Proponents
This Request for Proposals (the “RFP”) is an invitation by Health PEI (“HPEI”) to prospective proponents
to submit proposals for the provision of a Health PEI Data Roadmap as further described in;
• The RFP Mandatory Criteria (Appendix C) (the “Mandatory Criteria”);
• The RFP Rated Criteria (Appendix D); and
• The RFP Pricing (Appendix E).
HPEI is the single health authority for the Canadian province of Prince Edward Island. It delivers medical
care on behalf of the Government of Prince Edward Island's Department of Health and Wellness (DHW),
and is governed by a board of directors appointed by the Minister of Health and Wellness. Health PEI is
responsible for the delivery of publicly funded health services; the agency operates hospitals, health
centres, public long-term care nursing facilities and community-based programs and services.
Health PEI has embarked on a coordinated effort to rapidly advance health system transformation.
Foundational to the advancement and sustainability of this work is ensuring that appropriate and
reliable health data, analytical capacity, policies, processes, and technologies are in place to meet the
health system’s objectives.
Health PEI is seeking a consultant to create a data roadmap that focuses on using data to drive health
system performance, healthcare delivery, healthcare access, and innovation. The roadmap must help
Health PEI to realize a future in which:
• heath system performance is measured consistently and in alignment with national
standards, such as those from the Canadian Institute for Health Information (CIHI);
• strategic outcomes and targets are measured and reported consistently;
• appropriate legal/ legislative, technological, and administrative measures are in place to
support data governance, data accessibility, and high-value uses of data;
• all staff in Health PEI have tools to use data to drive impact and a baseline level of data
literacy;
• data visualization and analytics capacity are decentralized and technology-agnostic,
empowering business units to access and use data in operations and healthcare delivery;
and
• highly skilled analytics staff perform more complex data analyses that derive actionable
insights, creating enhanced value from data.
Development of the data roadmap is being led by HPEI’s Transformation and Strategy Office (TSO). The
TSO supports functions and initiatives that span across the healthcare system. Under the TSO, the
Performance and Innovation division supports Health PEI’s information needs by providing: quality
health information to inform decisions and manage system-level performance; operational support to
electronic health information systems used by Health PEI; strategic and operational decision support;
system and program/service planning, implementation, and evaluation; and policy development,
research, analysis and coordination. Through the Transformation Office, the TSO leads project and
change management for health system transformation, accelerating progress and ensuring initiatives
move forward at pace; coordinating across the health system; and monitoring, tracking and reporting on
Page 5 of 45
progress. The roadmap will therefore be strategically positioned to support health resource allocation
and service improvement.

For the purpose of this procurement process, the “RFP Contact” shall be:

PART 2 – EVALUATION AND NEGOTIATION
2.1 Stages of Evaluation and Negotiation
HPEI will conduct the evaluation of proposals and negotiations in the following four stages:
Stage I: Mandatory Submission Requirements
Stage II: Evaluation
Stage III: Pricing
Stage IV: Ranking and Contract Negotiations
2.2 Stage I – Mandatory Submission Requirements
Stage I will consist of a review to determine which proposals comply with all of the Mandatory

the Proponent a rectification notice identifying the deficiencies and providing the proponent an
opportunity to rectify the deficiencies. If the Proponent fails to satisfy the Mandatory Requirements
within the Rectification Period, its proposal will be excluded from further consideration. The
Rectification Period will begin to run from the date that HPEI issues a rectification notice to the
Proponent.
2.3 Stage II – Evaluation

3.3.4. If a Proponent fails to satisfy the Mandatory Requirements, its proposal will be excluded from

2.5 Stage IV – Ranking and Contract Negotiations
2.5.1 Ranking of Proponents
After the completion of Stage III, all scores from Stage II and Stage III will be added together and each
Proponent will be ranked based on its total score. The top-ranked Proponent will receive a written
invitation to enter into direct contract negotiations to finalize a Contract with HPEI. Upon finalization of

provided in its proposal or to confirm the conclusions reached in the evaluation, and may include
requests by HPEI for improved pricing, performance terms from the proponent, or modifications to the
proposed solution.
2.5.3 Time Period for Negotiations
HPEI intends to conclude negotiations and finalize an agreement with the top-ranked proponent during
the Contract Negotiation Period, commencing from the date HPEI invites the top-ranked proponent to
enter negotiations. A proponent invited to enter into direct Contract negotiations should therefore be

2.5.5 Notification to Other Proponents

3.1.1 Proponents not to change terminology

3.1.2 Proponents to Follow Instructions
Proponents should structure their proposals in accordance with the instructions in this RFP. Where

to access and use data in operations and healthcare delivery; and

creating enhanced value from data.

D.2.1 Strategic Alignment
Health PEI’s 2025-2028 Strategic Plan1 identifies data as an important asset that must be leveraged to
support continuous improvement, evidence-informed decision-making, innovation, health system
performance, resource allocation, and collaboration with regional partners.
1 https://www.princeedwardisland.ca/en/information/health-pei/health-pei-2025-2028-strategic-plan

PEI’s Digital Health Strategy (DHS) 2024-20292 is a guiding document for improving the availability and
usage of health information and investing in secure digital health technologies. A key theme identified
during strategy consultations was that “there is an opportunity to make better use of the information
captured by our digital health technologies, (and to do that) the appropriate supports must in place (e.g.
specialized resources, governance, policies, education, cybersecurity practices, etc.).” Goal #4 of the DHS
sets key priorities to achieve data-driven health decisions:
• Establish a provincial framework for managing health information;
• Ensure appropriate infrastructure is available to use health information; and
• Increase capacity to use health information.
To realize these key priorities, Department of Health and Wellness (DHW) and Health PEI will:
• Develop a Health Information Management framework (Governance, Policy, Resource Model)
that aligns with the Government of PEI information management legislation (including the PEI
Health Information Act), policies and practices; and addresses the needs, concerns, and
expectations of health system stakeholders and Island residents. Activities will include:
o Engaging health system stakeholders and residents to get an understanding of health
data needs, concerns (e.g., resource capacity, processes/structures, quality, trust with
accessing/use of health data), and expectations.
o Identifying opportunities to maximize the use of health data to support clinical decision
making and overall health system performance.
Another guiding document concerning the use of data is the 2024-2026 IT Shared Services (ITSS)
Strategic Plan. Within this document, data and information are seen as “assets to be protected and
leveraged appropriately.” ITSS therefore shares the goal of supporting evidence-based decision-making
by “enhancing data governance, data stewardship, and information management”.
Further, Health PEI’s Data Roadmap must align with the Pan-Canadian Health Data Stewardship
Framework3 developed by CIHI. The framework includes four Hallmarks of Health Data Stewardship,
which are intended to guide organizations and their staff on how to effectively and safely manage health
data. These hallmarks are:
• Making quality data accessible and usable for those who need it;
• Safeguarding data against misuse;
• Advancing and adhering to relevant laws, policies, and ethical standards; and
• Being transparent about how data is used and shared.

Health PEI’s goal is to have a data roadmap that enables the organization to optimize the way it uses
data to drive health system performance and deliver healthcare. The roadmap that is produced must be
technology-agnostic and must address capacity building/ bridging the following areas:
• Organizational Culture: Health PEI must have an organizational culture that values and uses
data—where data is demanded and drives decisions.

efficiently and maximizing the value gained from data. The roadmap should address legal,
administrative, and technological measures that are needed to develop and operationalize a
framework for data management.
o Work pertaining to data/information management and data governance that is
underway in other parts of the broader PEI public service must be considered and
integrated into the roadmap when appropriate.

• Data Visualization: Data visualization enables the use of data for decisions by transforming
complex information into easily digestible visual formats. This improves understanding,
communication, pattern recognition, decision-making, and data analysis. The roadmap should
address administrative and technological measures that are needed to enable the use of data
visualization software to create products like dashboards.

and using dashboards must be considered.

predictions and forecasting to improve care delivery, and early intervention and health

extent possible.

implementation of the roadmap, data-related duties for staff, and training/ upskilling for staff.

1 Executive Summary
Provide a 1–2-page summary of your technical response, highlighting the key features of your proposal. It should allow the evaluation
team to quickly gain an overall perspective of your proposal, prior to reviewing it in detail.
CGI is pleased to submit this proposal in response to Health PEI's Request for Proposals for the development of a Data
Strategy and Roadmap. We understand that Health PEI stands at a pivotal moment in its transformation journey, where the
organization is seeking to evolve from a state where data exists in silos serving primarily retrospective reporting needs, to a
future where data actively drives decision-making at every level of the organization. CGI is uniquely positioned to be Health
PEI's partner in this transformation, bringing the combination of deep local presence, world-class healthcare data expertise,
and innovative methodologies required to deliver a roadmap that is not just strategically sound, but genuinely implementable
within PEI's specific context.
Understanding Health PEI's Requirements
CGI recognizes that this engagement requires more than a document, it requires a strategic partner who understands both
the art and science of health data transformation. Health PEI's vision, as articulated in the 2025-2028 Strategic Plan and PEI's
Digital Health Strategy 2024-2029, is clear: data must become a strategic asset supporting continuous improvement,
evidence-informed decision-making, and better health outcomes for Islanders. What distinguishes CGI's understanding is our
recognition that Health PEI's path forward must be context specific. Solutions designed for larger provincial health authorities
with dedicated analytics departments will not translate directly to PEI's reality. The roadmap must be feasible and designed
for an organization that must maximize value from existing investments while building capacity incrementally.
Our Approach: Data First Philosophy with AI-Enabled Discovery
CGI proposes a proven three-phase methodology aligned with Health PEI's required six-month timeline:
Phase 1: Current State Assessment & Target State Definition (Months 1-2): We will conduct comprehensive discovery
using AI-enabled analysis tools to accelerate documentation review while engaging key stakeholders through structured
interviews and collaborative workshops. The target state will be co-developed with Health PEI stakeholders, ensuring
alignment with the Quintuple Aim, Pan-Canadian Health Data Stewardship Framework, and PEI's Digital Health Strategy.
Phase 2: Gap Analysis & Recommendations (Months 3-4): CGI will conduct rigorous gap analysis with embedded root-
cause analysis, applying Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) with stakeholder-validated criteria to prioritize solutions
based on impact, feasibility, and alignment with Health PEI's context. Recommendations will address change management,
data literacy, and culture transformation.
Phase 3: Data Roadmap Development & Validation (Months 5-6): The final roadmap will be clear, phased, costed, and
context-specific to PEI. It will include a Target Operating Model with roles, competencies, and responsibilities feasible within
Health PEI's resources, along with knowledge transfer to ensure Health PEI can maintain and evolve the roadmap as priorities
shift.
Our Data First approach treats data as a strategic asset from day one, ensuring the roadmap addresses foundational elements
of governance, quality, and accessibility before layering on analytics capabilities. Our methodology delivers additional value
by accelerating discovery and analysis (work that would traditionally consume weeks) while reducing the burden on Health
PEI's limited staff resources. Critically, AI finds things; our experts validate. Every insight is reviewed by senior CGI consultants
before presentation, and nothing moves forward without Health PEI's sign-off. All AI usage aligns with Pan-Canadian AI for
Health (AI4H) Guiding Principles, with data processed within Canada using enterprise-grade security.
Right-Sized for PEI
While CGI is a global organization, our approach is deliberately scaled for Health PEI's context not imported from larger
jurisdictions. Our track record with comparable organizations including Fife Council (370,000 residents), Life Sciences Nova
Scotia, and Island Health demonstrates our ability to deliver practical, implementable roadmaps for resource-constrained
organizations. This is a data strategy engagement, not an AI project. CGI's AI-enabled tools simply accelerate our internal
discovery work; the roadmap itself will be technology-agnostic, specifying requirements rather than prescribing solutions.
Every recommendation will be grounded in PEI's reality leveraging existing investments, defining roles achievable within PEI's
workforce, and providing cost estimates aligned with provincial fiscal constraints. Health PEI retains full control over scope,
approach, and any future-state capabilities identified.

CGI also understands that Health PEI's data roadmap must be developed within an increasingly complex regulatory and
ethical landscape. The Pan-Canadian Health Data Stewardship Framework from CIHI establishes clear expectations for
making data accessible while safeguarding against misuse. PEI's Health Information Act is undergoing comprehensive review
to align with evolving provincial, federal, and international principles on health information privacy. The Pan-Canadian AI for
Health (AI4H) Guiding Principles set expectations for any use of generative AI in healthcare contexts principles that CGI's

Clinical Delivery of Care and Health Analytics Communities for Canada Health Infoway as well as being currently engaged in
the federal AI Task Force and co-chairing the Strategic AI Council, positioning CGI at the forefront of national conversations

federal connection brings insights into federal investments in relevant infrastructures and research which may be pertinent to
PEI Health. This expertise ensures that the roadmap we develop will not only meet today's requirements but anticipate
tomorrow's opportunities and regulatory expectations.
Building the foundations for a data-driven organization
Beyond compliance, CGI understands that the deeper challenge Health PEI faces is cultural transformation. The RFP's
emphasis on organizational culture as one of five areas of focus reflects a mature understanding that technology and
governance alone do not create a data-driven organization. Staff across Health PEI, from frontline clinicians to administrative
personnel must see data as a tool that helps them do their jobs better, not as an additional burden or a mechanism for
surveillance. Building data literacy, creating demand for data-informed decisions, and fostering trust in data quality are
fundamentally human challenges that require thoughtful change management, not just technical solutions. CGI's methodology
addresses this directly through communications planning, training programs, and cultural change roadmaps that recognize
transformation happens one conversation, one dashboard, one decision at a time.
A multi-stakeholder landscape
Finally, CGI appreciates that Health PEI does not operate in isolation, and that some health services for Islanders are
delivered across Atlantic regional partners. The requirement to consult with Atlantic regional partners, New Brunswick, Nova
Scotia, and Newfoundland and Labrador, reflects a pragmatic recognition that smaller provinces can achieve more through
collaboration than competition. Interoperability work already underway with regional partners should be incorporated, not
duplicated. CGI's experience facilitating consensus across multiple organizations with competing priorities from our work

1 Proposed Approach and Project Plan
1.1 Approach and Plan
Outline the proposed approach and project plan that will be followed to address the RFP requirements as set out in D.1.
CGI's proven data consulting methodology, enhanced by our proven best practices, Data First philosophy, and leveraging AI-
enabled tools where approved and where it makes sense to increase efficiencies in analyzing data, positions us uniquely to
deliver a comprehensive, actionable, and context-specific Data Strategy and Roadmap for Health PEI. We bring the right
combination of global healthcare expertise, local presence, and innovative approaches to help Health PEI realize its vision of
using data to drive health system performance, healthcare delivery, healthcare access, and innovation.
We are committed to co-developing this roadmap with Health PEI stakeholders, ensuring alignment with your strategic
priorities and the Quintuple Aim, while delivering practical recommendations feasible within PEI's specific context. Our tested
collaboration approach and focused deliverables ensures that Health PEI will have not just a document, but a clear path
forward, designed based on immediate and extended needs, with the organizational capacity to sustain and evolve the
strategy over time. CGI will also deliver knowledge transfer to ensure adjustments and realignment of the roadmap and
implementation plan are understood so that PEI can continue to evolve the longer-term goals using the same templates and
methodology and priorities shift over time.
1.1.1 CGI’s Data First Approach to Transformation
CGI proposes a proven three-phase methodology for developing Health PEI's Data Strategy and Roadmap, enhanced by our
Data First Approach and AI-enabled discovery tools. This approach has been refined through successful engagements
with healthcare organizations across Canada, including BC's Provincial Health Services Authority (CST project), Alberta
Health (Data Strategy and Roadmap), and Island Health (Data and Corporate Reporting Strategy), and has been specifically
tailored to meet Health PEI's timelines, deliverables and unique context as a smaller, integrated provincial health authority.
Our Data First methodology aligns directly with Health PEI's required timeline of six months and addresses each of the five
areas of focus: Organizational Culture, Data Management/Governance, Data Visualization, Data Analytics, and Human
Resources. The approach is grounded in the IHI Quintuple Aim Framework and Pan-Canadian Health Data Stewardship
Framework, ensuring alignment with national standards while remaining context-specific to PEI.
CGI's Data First Approach represents a fundamental shift in how data strategies are developed. Rather than beginning with
technology solutions and working backward, we start by deeply understanding the organization’s strategic priorities in concert
with the data ecosystem itself, its sources, flows, quality, governance, and most importantly, its potential to drive value across
the entire data value chain.
Core Principles of Data First:
• Data as a Strategic Asset: Treating data with the same rigor as financial or human capital assets, ensuring proper
stewardship, governance, and investment.
• Value Chain Orientation: Examining data through the lens of collection, processing, analysis, distribution, and use,
identifying opportunities to increase quality, capture metadata, identify sources of truth and increase value at each stage.
• Outcome-Driven Discovery: Connecting every data initiative to measurable health outcomes aligned with the Quintuple
Aim enhanced care experience, improved health outcomes, reduced costs, staff wellbeing, and health equity.
• Technology-Agnostic Requirements: Defining what data capabilities are needed before prescribing specific tools,
ensuring recommendations leverage Health PEI's existing investments while addressing genuine gaps.
CGI has embedded AI into our methodology, not as an experiment, but as standard practice which will be reviewed and
approved by PEI Health to ensure alignment with how information is captured, synthesized, and validated to protect
information while ensuring efficiencies are achieved. While all discussions will be led by our health data experts, our AI-
enabled approach dramatically accelerates the team to conduct the discovery and analysis phases, reducing overall timeline
by 40-60% compared to traditional methods while delivering more comprehensive and deeper insights, all validated by PEI
Health stakeholders.
CGI uses secure, enterprise-approved data and AI tools that operate within controlled environments, with data encrypted in
transit and at rest, strict access controls, and audit logging enabled. All information assets are assessed for sensitivity prior
to use, and only data explicitly approved for AI-assisted processing is permitted. No client data is used without formal
authorization, and usage is governed by CGI security policies, privacy standards, and applicable regulatory requirements.

Health PEI | HPEI-1382 - Health PEI Data Roadmap
In section 3.2.1 we will go into more detail about CGI’s Data First Approach and why it is so suitable for this project.
1.1.2 Three-Phases
Our methodology is structured in three distinct phases, directly aligned with Health PEI's required timeline and deliverables.
Each phase builds upon the previous, with iterative stakeholder validation ensuring continuous alignment and buy-in.
1.1.2.1 Phase 1: Current State Assessment & Target State Requirements Definition
(Months 1-2)
The assessment phase establishes a validated understanding of Health PEI's current data landscape and co-
develops the target state vision and requirements with key stakeholders.
Collaborative Discovery Through AI-Accelerated Analysis and Expert Insight
CGI's approach to the Current State Assessment begins with a structured discovery sprint that combines the speed and
comprehensiveness of AI-enabled tools with the irreplaceable judgment of seasoned healthcare data experts.
During the first weeks of engagement, our team will deploy a combination of human reviews and safe and secured AI
discovery tools, that contain all data to PEI Health approved stakeholders, to conduct a rapid, systematic inventory of Health
PEI's existing data assets (focused only on the descriptive data architecture and metadata and not the data itself), policies,
system documentation, data dictionaries, and approved process workflows across clinical, financial, HR, and operational
domains. These AI tools will synthesize thousands of pages of documentation, work that would traditionally consume weeks
of analyst time into organized findings that surface patterns, redundancies, data lineage relationships, and potential
governance gaps across Health PEI's fragmented data landscape. Combining this automated cataloging with ‘human’ analysis
the team will be able to accelerate the categorization of assets, overlap in process and opportunities for efficiencies at the
outset of the engagement, increasing the time to valuable collaboration with PEI Health stakeholders, Critically, this AI-
generated foundation becomes the starting point for deep collaboration: CGI's subject matter experts, drawing on decades of
combined experience in Canadian healthcare data strategy, will validate, contextualize, and enrich these findings through
structured working sessions with Health PEI's internal teams.
Our SMEs will bring analytical frameworks grounded in the Data Management Institute’s DMBOK principles and the Pan-
Canadian Health Data Stewardship Framework, while Health PEI's staff contribute the institutional knowledge, operational
realities, and organizational nuances that no external analysis can fully capture. This collaborative model ensures that the
current state assessment reflects not just what exists on paper, but how data flows, who uses it, what barriers they encounter,
and where the greatest opportunities for value creation reside.
Data Capability Maturity Assessment: Establishing a Focused Baseline
© 2026 CGI Inc. Confidential 2
Health PEI | HPEI-1382 - Health PEI Data Roadmap
CGI's Phase 1 current state analysis employs a structured Data Capability Maturity Assessment to establish Health PEI's
baseline across six core capability dimensions, assessed in sequence: (1) Data Governance & Stewardship, policies, roles,
and decision rights; (2) Data Quality & Metadata Management, standards, definitions, and data lineage; (3) Data
Architecture & Integration, how data flows across systems; (4) Analytics & Visualization, reporting capabilities and self-
service maturity; (5) Data Literacy & Culture, organizational appetite for data-driven decisions; and (6) Privacy, Security &
Compliance, alignment with legislative and regulatory requirements.
For each dimension, we engage targeted stakeholders: Executive Leadership and the Data Governance Sub-Committee for
governance; Health Analytics and eHealth for architecture and analytics; Privacy and Information Management for
compliance; and HR and Operations for culture and literacy. Each capability is rated on a five-level maturity scale (Ad Hoc →
Optimized), producing a heat map that visualizes strengths and gaps.
This approach intentionally focuses on maturity sensing and gap analysis, not exhaustive data inventories, or deep technical
assessments. It manages scope by measuring organizational readiness across defined dimensions, providing the structured
foundation for current state findings, and ensuring the gap analysis in Phase 2 addresses the right priorities.
The maturity model and data risk assessments also provide a baseline for PEI Health for incremental improvement. The tool
will be provided with knowledge transfer to PEI Health stakeholders to measure the improvements at each stage of
implementation.
CGI will leverage existing capabilities and services framework as a starting place, and will adapt based on PEI Health priorities
and capabilities, to conduct the current state assessment. By leveraging visuals similar to the image below the summary of
current state can be shared as a heat map for current state with a drill down to capabilities below.

Health PEI | HPEI-1382 - Health PEI Data Roadmap
Beyond internal engagement, our team will conduct targeted consultations with Atlantic regional partners in New Brunswick,
Nova Scotia, and Newfoundland and Labrador to identify opportunities for collaboration on business intelligence, analytics
capacity, and cross-provincial data sharing recognizing that Health PEI's small scale can be transformed from a constraint
into an advantage through strategic regional partnerships.
CGI will help Health PEI further enrich the target state vision by drawing on our global healthcare practice's direct experience
with comparable transformations: from NHS Wales Clinical AI Acceleration initiative, NSW Health Australia's centralized
analytics program, BC’s CST, provincial Health Data Platform, and Vancouver Island Health data platform initiatives, to Alberta
Health's Provincial Health Analytic Network redesign, to Fife Council Scotland's AI-enabled workforce planning initiative. CGI
will facilitate connections with similar relevant stakeholders if desired.
These cross-jurisdictional and cross-industry insights will be carefully filtered through the lens of PEI's specific context its
integrated provincial model, existing IT infrastructure, workforce realities, and legislative environment under the Health
Information Act, ensuring that the target state is aspirational yet achievable, grounded in what has worked elsewhere but
tailored to what will work here. The result will be a validated target state vision and requirements that stakeholders recognize
as their own, aligned with the Quintuple Aim and PEI's Digital Health Strategy, and ready to serve as the foundation for
meaningful gap analysis.
Phase 1 deliverables are:
• Validated Project Charter with governance structure and communication plan.
• Current State Assessment Report covering all five areas of focus.
• Target State Vision, co-developed with stakeholders.
• Stakeholder Requirements Documentation.
Phase one will include several key activities to be able to complete a current state assessment and define the target state
requirements with key stakeholders within Health PEI.
