1.1.2.2 Phase 2: Target State Definition, Gap Analysis & Recommendations (Months 3-4)
This phase translates the current-to-target state gap into prioritized, actionable recommendations with
embedded root-cause analysis.
Phase 2 begins with the critical work of translating the target state requirements gathered in Phase 1 into a comprehensive,
validated Target State Definition that will serve as the strategic north star for Health PEI's data journey. CGI's team will
facilitate a series of collaborative design sessions with Health PEI stakeholders to synthesize the requirements, aspirations,
and constraints identified during discovery into a coherent future state architecture spanning all five areas of focus,
Organizational Culture, Data Management/Governance, Data Visualization, Data Analytics, and Human Resources. CGI will
demonstrate the power of AI assistance in these workshops, with the approval of PEI health, by demonstrating how
information collected through collaboration can be synthesized into actionable insights as part of the workshop saving time
while increasing opportunities for validation and collaboration.
This target state will be explicitly grounded in the Quintuple Aim Framework,
ensuring every element can be traced to improved care experience, health
outcomes, cost efficiency, staff wellbeing, or health equity. The Target State will
also include an identification of intended benefits so that the KPIs are defined
early in the process to ensure value and the expected return on investment is
achieved. With both current state and target state now clearly defined, our team
will conduct a systematic gap analysis using a structured capability maturity
model and data risk assessment tool that assesses Health PEI's current
positioning against target state requirements across each dimension of the data
value chain – see sample analysis framework below. CGI will leverage our
existing tool to allow maturity to be assessed along with the future vision as well
as a comparison to relevant industry peers.
Co-Developing the Target State Vision and Requirements Through Stakeholder Engagement and Cross-
Jurisdictional Learning
The target state definition will be co-developed through a deliberate stakeholder engagement process designed to build
ownership and consensus while incorporating proven practices from healthcare organizations facing similar challenges.
CGI will facilitate a series of structured interviews, focus group sessions and interactive workshops with the full spectrum of
Health PEI stakeholders (i.e. Executive Leadership, Operations, Health Analytics, eHealth Clinical Operations, Policy
Planning & Evaluation, Privacy and Information Management, the Transformation Office, HR Analytics, Finance, and Medical
Affairs) using proven facilitation techniques that surface both explicit requirements and underlying concerns about data
accessibility, quality, and governance. The team will work with the PEI Health lead to determine the best engagement
approach for each group to minimize the impact of current workloads and maximize the collaboration opportunities. This may
include virtual interviews, leverage existing team meetings, or conduct scheduled focus groups and workshops.

Developing Prioritized, Context-Specific Recommendations
The gap analysis findings will be transformed into a prioritized set of recommendations through a rigorous Multi-Criteria
Decision Analysis (MCDA) process, with evaluation criteria co-developed with Health PEI stakeholders to ensure
organizational buy-in and contextual relevance.
Criteria will span multiple dimensions including strategic alignment with the Quintuple Aim, feasibility within PEI's resource
constraints, implementation complexity, time to value, dependencies on other initiatives, and financial sustainability,
recognizing that recommendations must be practical for a smaller, less-resourced provincial health authority rather than
aspirational best practices imported from larger jurisdictions.
CGI will develop a comprehensive options analysis for closing each significant gap, presenting Health PEI with alternative
pathways that articulate trade-offs between speed, cost, risk, and capability outcomes.
Recommendations will address not only technical and process changes but also the critical enablers of successful
transformation: change management strategies including a communications plan to build organizational awareness and
support, a training plan to increase data literacy across the organization, and a cultural change roadmap to foster the data-
driven decision-making culture that Health PEI seeks to create.
All recommendations will be stress-tested for financial feasibility and validated through focused working sessions with a
designated stakeholder sub-group before being considered final, ensuring that what emerges from Phase 2 is not a theoretical
wish list but a pragmatic, prioritized, and stakeholder-endorsed foundation for the implementation roadmap to be developed
in Phase 3.
Phase 2 deliverables are:
• Target State Definition, co-developed with stakeholders.
• Gap Analysis Report with root-cause analysis.
• Prioritization Framework and MCDA Results.
• Draft Recommendations validated with stakeholder sub-group.
• Change Management Strategy including communications plan, training plan, and data-driven culture roadmap.
Phase two will include several key activities to be able to define the target state, gap analysis, and recommendations for the
data roadmap.

1.2.1 CGI’s Data First Approach to Modernization
CGI's Data First Approach is uniquely suited to address Health PEI's fragmented data landscape and ambitious six-month
timeline by starting with the data itself rather than prescriptive technology solutions. This methodology directly aligns with
Health PEI's requirement for a technology-agnostic roadmap that leverages existing investments while addressing genuine
capability gaps.
By examining data through the lens of the data value chain collection, processing, analysis, distribution, and use, CGI can
systematically identify opportunities to increase value at each stage across Health PEI's patient/resident, clinical, financial,
HR, and operational systems. This outcome-driven approach ensures every recommendation connects to measurable health
outcomes aligned with the Quintuple Aim Framework, addressing Health PEI's strategic priorities for enhanced care
experience, improved health outcomes, reduced costs, staff wellbeing, and health equity. The Data First philosophy treats
data as the strategic asset Health PEI envisions in its 2025-2028 Strategic Plan, establishing the governance, stewardship,
and investment framework needed to support evidence-informed decision-making and health system transformation.
CGI's AI-enabled discovery tools safely and dramatically accelerate the comprehensive stakeholder consultation and
documentation analysis that Health PEI's roadmap requires, reducing discovery and analysis timelines by 40-60% while
delivering deeper insights across the five areas of focus. AI rapidly processes Health PEI's existing policies, procedures,
system documentation, and data dictionaries work that would traditionally require weeks of manual review enabling CGI's
experts to spend more time on validation, root-cause analysis, and co-development of solutions with Health PEI stakeholders.
Pattern recognition capabilities identify data relationships, redundancies, and gaps across Health PEI's fragmented
landscape, while AI-assisted synthesis of stakeholder interviews ensures no insight is missed from consultations with
Executive Leadership, Operations, Health Analytics, eHealth, Privacy and Information Management, and regional partners.
How AI Enhances Discovery for Health PEI:
• Comprehensive Documentation Analysis: AI processes existing policies, procedures, system documentation, and
data dictionaries, compiling and synthesizing information that would traditionally take weeks to manually review.

requirements. CGI’s methodology is intentionally flexible, allowing Health PEI to retain full control over tools, techniques, and
data usage without impacting on the quality or integrity of the resulting data roadmap.

1 Reporting and Documentation
1.1 Approach to Deliverables and Reporting
Outline how you will provide the Current State Assessment and Target State Definition, Analysis and Recommendations, and Data
Roadmap mentioned in D.1.
CGI understands that Health PEI operates with limited resources and that every hour of stakeholder time is valuable. Our
approach is designed to deliver high-quality, implementable outputs while minimizing the burden on Health PEI staff, ensuring
we do the heavy lifting so your team can focus on validation and decision-making rather than document production.
Current State Assessment and Target State Definition (Months 1-2)
CGI will conduct a comprehensive discovery process using our AI-enabled analysis tools to accelerate documentation review
and identify patterns across Health PEI's data landscape. We will engage key stakeholders (Executive Leadership, Health
Analytics, eHealth Clinical Operations, Privacy and Information Management, and others identified in the RFP) through
structured interviews and collaborative workshops. Our assessment will be guided by the five areas of focus (organizational
culture, data management/governance, data visualization, data analytics, human resources) and the data value chain
concept. We will co-develop the target state vision with stakeholders, ensuring alignment with national frameworks including
the Pan-Canadian Health Data Stewardship Framework, CIHI standards, and the Quintuple Aim. Regional partner
consultation with New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, and Newfoundland and Labrador will inform collaboration opportunities.
The Current State Assessment and Target State Definition will be considered complete when:
• Health PEI’s current data and analytics environment has been documented across the five areas of focus and the data
value chain, reflecting people, process, governance, technology, and data considerations.
• Stakeholder input, documentation review, and data asset analysis have been synthesized into a clear summary of current
capabilities, challenges, and dependencies.
• A clear and achievable target state has been defined, outlining future capabilities, governance, roles, and ways of working
aligned with Health PEI’s strategic priorities and organizational context.
• The target state reflects relevant national frameworks and best practices and incorporates applicable regional partner
insights.
• Visual summaries comparing current and target states are included and consistent with the narrative.
• The deliverable has been reviewed, validated, and formally endorsed by Health PEI’s designated governance and
approval authorities.
Once these conditions are met, the deliverable will be considered complete and formally approved, enabling progression to
the next phase of the engagement.
Analysis and Recommendations (Months 3-4)
CGI will conduct a rigorous gap analysis with embedded root-cause analysis to identify why gaps exist between current and
target states. Using Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) with stakeholder-validated criteria, we will prioritize solutions
based on impact, feasibility, and alignment with Health PEI's context. Recommendations will address change management,
data literacy, and culture transformation, including communications and training plans. All recommendations will be validated
with key stakeholders before finalization.
The Current State Analysis and Recommendations will be considered complete when:
• Gaps between the current and target states have been clearly identified across all areas of focus, supported by structured
analysis and evidence-based findings.
• Root causes of identified gaps have been assessed and documented, informed by capability maturity assessments and
dependency analysis.
• A transparent and repeatable prioritization approach (e.g., Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis) has been applied, with
prioritization criteria co-developed and validated with key stakeholders.
• Recommendations have been clearly documented, prioritized, and linked to identified gaps, including rationale,
dependencies, sequencing considerations, and change management implications.

Health PEI | HPEI-1382 - Health PEI Data Roadmap
• Change management considerations related to communications, data literacy, and fostering a data-driven culture have
been incorporated at a planning level.
• Visual summaries (e.g., capability maturity heat maps, gap severity charts, and prioritization matrices) are included and
consistent with the narrative findings.
• Findings and recommendations have been reviewed, validated, and formally endorsed by Health PEI’s designated
governance and approval authorities.
Once these conditions are met, the deliverables related to the analysis and recommendation will be considered complete and
formally approved, confirming readiness to proceed to the next phase of the engagement.
Data Roadmap (Months 5-6)
The roadmap will be clear, phased, costed, and context-specific to PEI, not based on best practices from larger jurisdictions.
It will include a target operating model with roles, competencies, and responsibilities feasible within Health PEI's resources.
Initiatives will be prioritized and sequenced with cost estimates and resource requirements. The roadmap will be technology-
agnostic, identifying requirements rather than specific solutions, and will address privacy-by-design, security, and data
residency considerations throughout.
The Data Roadmap will be considered complete when:
• A clear, phased, and costed roadmap has been developed that defines a practical path from the current state to the
target state across all five areas of focus and each step of the data value chain.
• Prioritized initiatives are clearly documented with associated timelines, dependencies, sequencing, cost estimates, and
resource requirements.
• The roadmap is technology-agnostic and reflects Health PEI’s existing IT infrastructure, data and digital health
architecture, security practices, and hybrid centralized/decentralized service model.
• A future-state data and analytics operating model has been defined, including roles, competencies, and accountability
structures aligned with Health PEI’s organizational capacity.
• The roadmap demonstrates alignment with the Quintuple Aim, Health PEI’s Digital Health Strategy, and pan-Canadian
data stewardship principles.
• Visual representations (e.g., phased roadmap, initiative sequencing, dependency views, and target operating model
schematic) are included and consistent with the narrative.
• The roadmap has been reviewed, validated, and refined through iterative engagement with key stakeholders and

1.2 Resource Replacement and Continuity Management
Health PEI acknowledges that instances can arise where a proposed resource is no longer employed by or associated with the
Proponent or is otherwise unavailable to the Proponent at the time of the service requirement. In the proposal, describe the process
that would be used for including Health PEI in the selection of replacement resources and for securing Health PEI’s approval of
replacement resources. Describe how changes in the project manager, in particular, would be handled, if this becomes necessary.
As a global organization, CGI has a substantial pool of experts, drawn from diverse fields and specialties. This extensive
network of talent allows us to address any resource requirement or challenge promptly and effectively and ensure that your
project objectives are met without compromising on quality or timelines.
• Proactive Assessment: We will frequently assess the skill sets and performance of each member of our project team
involved in your project. This will enable us to identify potential risks or gaps that might necessitate resource replacement.
• Transparent Communication: We will maintain transparent communication with you. If a resource replacement is
inevitable, we will notify you ahead of time, explain the reason, and provide the plan for replacement to mitigate any
impact. Contingent upon your request, we will provide the opportunity for you to validate the fit of a replacement resource.
• Training and Knowledge Transfer: We will ensure that the replacement resource will undergo a training and onboarding
process to acquaint themselves with the project specifics, culture, and expectations. In addition, we will facilitate a
comprehensive knowledge transfer from the outgoing resource to the incoming one to ensure continuity of work.
• Transition Phase: We will enforce a handover period where both the outgoing and incoming resources work together.
This will help the new resource to adapt faster and ensures a smoother transition.
• Client Approval: We offer you the opportunity to interact with and approve the new resource. This will foster confidence
and preserve the quality of our relationship and partnership.
• Regular Reviews: Post-transition, we will conduct regular reviews with you and the resource. This will allow us to ensure
your needs are being met and the resource feels adequately supported.
Handling Changes in Project Manager
CGI recognizes that the Project Manager role is critical to engagement success, and any transition requires particular care to
maintain momentum and client confidence. As a global organization with a substantial pool of experts across diverse fields,

1.3 Performance Management and Issue Resolution

Proponent is not performing their responsibilities adequately.
CGI is committed to delivering exceptional service on the Health PEI Data Roadmap engagement.
Quality Management Approach
CGI applies an ISO 9001-aligned quality management approach to ensure deliverables meet Health PEI's expectations. Our
methodology incorporates iterative review cycles where draft deliverables are shared with Health PEI stakeholders for
validation before finalization ensuring alignment at every milestone rather than waiting until project ends.
Quality checkpoints are embedded at each phase transition, with acceptance criteria co-developed with Health PEI during
project initiation. Regular status meetings provide opportunities for feedback, and CGI's engagement leadership conducts
periodic quality reviews to assess deliverable standards and team performance.
This continuous feedback loop ensures issues are identified early and addressed promptly, keeping the engagement on track
and Health PEI confident in the outcomes.
In the event that an assigned resource is not performing their responsibilities adequately, CGI will work collaboratively with
Health PEI to address the concern promptly and decisively.
Immediate Response and Performance Improvement
Upon receiving feedback from Health PEI regarding resource performance, CGI will initiate a structured Performance
Improvement Plan (PIP) jointly defined with Health PEI leadership. The focus is on protecting delivery outcomes, maintaining
project momentum, and minimizing any impact to roadmap objectives. Corrective actions are initiated promptly and may
include targeted coaching, adjusted responsibilities, additional oversight, or, where necessary, introduction of alternative
consulting resources from CGI's qualified resource pool.
Resource Transition Process
Where a resource transition is required, CGI provides a minimum of ten business days' notice and manages the transition as
a controlled change. A proposed replacement profile (including curriculum vitae and demonstrated alignment with the role
requirements) is submitted to Health PEI for review and approval before the transition proceeds. To ensure continuity and
preserve institutional knowledge built during the engagement, a formal knowledge transfer and transition plan is developed
and shared with Health PEI for validation prior to the change.

Change management is embedded within our engagement governance model. Stakeholders are kept informed through clear
communication, and impacts are assessed collaboratively. Where appropriate, CGI's engagement leadership facilitates

smoothly.

comprehensive Data and AI Strategy for Provincial Laboratory Medicine Services (PLMS) in
British Columbia. The initiative was designed to help PLMS leverage Artificial Intelligence to
enhance diagnostic precision, clinical efficiency, and patient outcomes, while ensuring ethical,
equitable, and sustainable use of AI technologies. CGI worked closely with PHSA’s technical,
operational, and clinical stakeholders to assess digital pathology systems, review architectural
readiness, and scan the global landscape of AI tools and solutions relevant to the provincial
laboratory environment.

and maturity, built around governance, capability development, and responsible adoption. Key
deliverables included the creation of a Data and AI Centre of Enablement (CoE) to guide
innovation, the design of a Target Operating Model for AI Lifecycle Management, and the
development of standardized AI Governance and Risk Assessment tools. The strategy also
introduced a Computational Pathology Community of Practice, fostering cross-institutional
collaboration and knowledge sharing.

integration across its diagnostic operations. CGI’s approach balanced innovation with governance
and compliance, ensuring that data and AI initiatives are implemented with measurable value,
regulatory alignment, and a sustainable foundation for continued digital transformation.

practices for CGI and our clients globally. In this role Diane has led the design and implementation of standards to ensure
Responsible AI policies and practices across CGI’s 93,000 members globally. Diane is also engaged in advising policy makers
and business leaders in Canada and the United Kingdom, and the EU AI Commission on emerging AI Legislation and Codes
of Conduct for AI developers and implementers. Diane has also been named the co-chair of Canada’s AI Council to the
Federal Government. Diane has also been assigned as an advisor to the Welsh Government Strategic AI Council and most
recently was invited as a member of the 2025 AI Strategy Refresh Task Force for the Canadian Federal Government.
Diane holds a PhD in Information Technology Management where she conducted doctoral research on medical AI/expert
system solution modeling and adoption and has also served as a lecturer at Simon Fraser University as well as having been
engaged in designing and co-delivering material on Data Science in Medicine for the UBC Medical School DASH program.
Diane has over 35 years of experience in the design, development and delivery of highly integrated big data, analytics and AI
solutions, including leading public health surveillance solutions in Canada to drive evidence-based decision making. Diane
is an experienced presenter and author of whitepapers and academic research on responsible use of AI and continues to
extend her knowledge in applied AI and emerging technologies for positive business and societal impacts.

The Canadian Federal AI Council has several key objectives, including fostering the development and implementation of
Responsible AI policies across various sectors in Canada. The Council aims to ensure that AI technologies are developed
and used in ways that are ethical, transparent, and aligned with the values of Canadian society. It is also focused on advancing
AI literacy and skills among the Canadian workforce, promoting innovation and competitiveness in AI, and providing guidance
on the ethical and societal impacts of AI. The Council works closely with policymakers, industry leaders, and other
stakeholders to create a collaborative environment for AI innovation while safeguarding public trust and safety.

level change. These efforts demonstrate a high degree of organizational readiness, and critically, the strategic timing to pursue
a comprehensive data roadmap now.
1. Strategic Alignment Across Multiple Guiding Documents
Health PEI has established clear strategic direction through multiple aligned planning documents that create a coherent
foundation for data transformation. The Health PEI 2025-2028 Strategic Plan explicitly identifies data as an important asset
that must be leveraged to support continuous improvement, evidence-informed decision-making, innovation, health system
performance, resource allocation, and collaboration with regional partners. This strategic recognition of data's value signals
executive-level commitment to transformation.
PEI's Digital Health Strategy (DHS) 2024-2029 further reinforces this direction, with Goal #4 setting clear priorities for data-
driven health decisions: establishing a provincial framework for managing health information, ensuring appropriate
infrastructure to use health information, and increasing organizational capacity to leverage data effectively. Notably, the DHS
consultations identified that "there is an opportunity to make better use of the information captured by our digital health
technologies", demonstrating that stakeholders across the organization already recognize both the need and the opportunity
for change.
The 2024-2026 IT Shared Services (ITSS) Strategic Plan aligns with these health-specific priorities, treating data and
information as "assets to be protected and leveraged appropriately" and sharing the goal of supporting evidence-based
decision-making through "enhancing data governance, data stewardship, and information management." This cross-

Executive Summary

The New Brunswick Liquor Corporation (ANBL) is seeking a modern, automated testing solution to support and protect its Dynamics 365 ecosystem, including Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, Dynamics 365 Commerce (eCommerce and POS), and Power Pages. The solution must provide reliable, end-to-end test automation across integrated systems, reduce manual testing effort, improve release quality, and support ongoing system changes with minimal operational risk. CGI’s proposed solution has been specifically designed to meet these requirements.

CGI is proudly Canadian, founded, headquartered, and continuously operating in Canada for nearly 50 years, with over 40 years of service delivery across Atlantic Canada. Since opening our first Atlantic office in 1991, CGI has grown to employ approximately 800 professionals across New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador. As a long-standing community builder, CGI reinvests in local talent and supports the economic and digital evolution of New Brunswick. Backed by a global network of nearly 100,000 professionals, CGI delivers the combined strength of local accountability and global expertise aligned to ANBL’s long-term digital strategy.

CGI’s proposed approach leverages our proven SimpliTest automated testing platform to deliver comprehensive, end-to-end test automation across ANBL’s Dynamics 365 environment. SimpliTest enables single automated test scenarios that span Finance, Commerce, POS, eCommerce, and Power Pages, ensuring complete business process validation across systems. This mature platform, used extensively by CGI for internal application testing, reduces testing complexity, accelerates release cycles, and improves system stability across ANBL’s integrated retail and enterprise operations.

A key differentiator of CGI’s solution is its configuration-based approach, requiring no customization. SimpliTest aligns with Microsoft’s Dynamics 365 roadmap, ensuring long-term maintainability, seamless upgrades, and reduced total cost of ownership. This approach allows ANBL to adopt future Microsoft enhancements without rework while maintaining consistent and reliable test coverage.

CGI’s delivery methodology emphasizes predictability and risk reduction through structured onboarding and phased rollout of automated testing. High-risk and high-value business processes are prioritized to deliver early value, while ongoing support ensures test assets remain current as configurations and releases evolve. Security, privacy, and compliance are foundational to CGI’s approach, with all services delivered in alignment with provincial and enterprise standards.

In selecting CGI, ANBL gains a trusted partner with deep expertise in automated testing, proven experience supporting Dynamics 365 platforms, and a strong local presence in New Brunswick. CGI offers a low-risk, scalable, and future-ready automated testing solution that supports operational stability, accelerates change, and enables ANBL’s continued digital transformation.
Experience and Qualifications
Company Overview

Share a brief history of your company, including founding year, key milestones, and core business areas. Highlight your company’s unique value proposition and how it distinguishes itself from competitors.

Founded in 1976 by Serge Godin and André Imbeau in Québec City, CGI has grown from a small consulting firm into one of the world’s largest independent IT and business process services companies. From its inception, CGI was built on a client-first philosophy and a partnership-based culture that emphasizes accountability, collaboration, and long-term relationships. This foundation has enabled CGI to scale globally while maintaining a strong focus on predictable delivery and client outcomes.

Over the decades, CGI has expanded its service offerings and geographic footprint through disciplined organic growth and targeted acquisitions. Strategic expansion during the 1980s and 1990s strengthened CGI’s IT consulting capabilities, while continued acquisitions in the 2000s diversified its service portfolio and extended its global reach. In 2016, CGI marked its 40th anniversary by ringing the New York Stock Exchange Closing Bell, recognizing the contributions of its global workforce. Today, CGI operates through more than 30 delivery centers and multiple technology centers worldwide, supporting clients across both public and private sectors with a strong focus on digital transformation, emerging technologies, and sustainable solutions.
Core Business Areas

CGI delivers comprehensive end-to-end IT and business services designed to help organizations modernize operations, improve efficiency, and achieve measurable business outcomes. These services include IT and business consulting, systems integration, application development and management, infrastructure and cloud services, and business process outsourcing. CGI’s integrated service model enables clients to engage a single trusted partner across the full technology lifecycle, reducing complexity and risk while ensuring continuity and accountability.
Unique Value Proposition and Differentiation

CGI distinguishes itself from competitors through a combination of ownership structure, delivery model, and operational discipline. Approximately 85 percent of CGI’s shares are owned by its member-partners, creating a culture of personal accountability and long-term commitment to client success. This partner-owned model aligns incentives toward sustainable relationships and consistent delivery quality rather than short-term financial performance, resulting in lower turnover and deeper institutional knowledge within client engagements.

CGI’s proximity model further differentiates the organization by combining local accountability with global scale. Clients are supported by local CGI teams who understand regional regulations, business environments, and organizational priorities, while also benefiting from access to CGI’s global delivery and technology centers. This approach allows CGI to provide responsive, tailored solutions without sacrificing scalability or cost efficiency, avoiding the common trade-offs seen in purely offshore or boutique consulting models.

Operational excellence is a core strength of CGI. The organization is recognized for disciplined execution, mature governance, and predictable delivery, with consistently high client satisfaction and a strong track record of projects delivered on time and within budget. CGI’s pragmatic approach to consulting emphasizes solutions that fit within a client’s existing environment, prioritizing measurable outcomes over trend-driven or experimental initiatives. Technology-agnostic recommendations ensure that solutions are designed around client needs rather than vendor-driven agendas.

CGI also differentiates itself through deep industry expertise across sectors such as government and public services, financial services, healthcare, utilities, and other regulated industries. This vertical specialization enables CGI to embed industry knowledge directly into delivery teams, ensuring solutions are practical, compliant, and aligned with sector-specific challenges. Growth through targeted acquisitions further strengthens this expertise, with acquired organizations integrated carefully into CGI’s operating model to preserve talent, continuity, and domain knowledge.

Sustainability and responsible business practices are embedded into CGI’s operations and governance. The company is recognized by leading international ESG indices for its environmental, social, and governance performance, reinforcing CGI’s commitment to ethical delivery, inclusive growth, and long-term value creation for clients and communities.
Test Automation Services for New Brunswick Liquor Corporation

Within this broader context, CGI’s Test Automation services are designed to improve quality, accelerate delivery cycles, and maximize return on investment for New Brunswick Liquor Corporation. CGI applies a structured and industrialized approach that includes automation opportunity assessments, strategy development, framework implementation, and scalable execution. Leveraging leading tools such as SimpliTest, Selenium, Appium, UFT, and Tricentis Tosca, CGI delivers reliable and maintainable automation solutions supported by strong governance, transparent communication, and close collaboration with New Brunswick Liquor Corporation stakeholders.
Company Experience

The proposal should provide evidence of comparable company experience by referencing three (3) test automation solution implementation projects completed within the last five (5) years, with organizations of similar size, industry, and complexity (e.g., crown corporations, retail, or other regulated sectors).

Each reference should highlight the proponent’s capabilities and demonstrated success delivering enterprise-grade test automation solutions across Microsoft business applications such as Dynamics 365 (F&O, eCommerce, Power Platform) and integrated environments involving multi-platform, end-to-end testing.
Proponents should clearly describe how their experience demonstrates:
• Proven ability to deliver automated testing frameworks that integrate across systems, including API-level validation, cross-browser, and cross-device execution.
• Experience supporting Canadian clients with confirmed data residency and compliance requirements.
• Effective enablement of business and functional users in contributing to automation creation and maintenance through low-code or reusable components.
• Evidence of reusable test automation assets, accelerators, or onboarding packages that reduced implementation time and improved maintainability for clients.
• Integration of automation within CI/CD pipelines, particularly with Azure DevOps or similar platforms.
• Successful collaboration or integration with RSAT for Dynamics 365 and performance or load testing in enterprise environments.

The following references highlight CGI’s experience delivering quality engineering and test automation solutions, including multiple client engagements leveraging CGI’s SimpliTest solution. These projects demonstrate CGI’s ability to implement acceptance-criteria–driven automation aligned to agile delivery models, while meeting budgetary and schedule commitments and delivering measurable business outcomes. The references span both recent pilot implementations and long-term enterprise engagements, illustrating how SimpliTest and CGI’s broader quality engineering services have been successfully applied to improve release velocity, increase automation coverage, and embed quality as a built-in practice supported by effective onboarding and knowledge transfer.
Team Experience

It is expected that the test automation solution delivery team assigned to the project will have the requisite experience and expertise to ensure a successful implementation, and that these resources will remain engaged for the duration of the project.
The proponent should describe the team composition, identifying key roles and named individuals who will be allocated to the ANBL account. For each proposed team member, provide:

Brief bio highlighting relevant subject matter expertise, certifications, and experience in: test automation frameworks, Microsoft ecosystems (e.g., Dynamics 365, Power Platform), CI/CD integration.
Description of how each individual will contribute to achieving ANBL’s automation objectives and ensuring solution adoption and long-term sustainability.
Clear identification of whether each resource is an employee or a sub-contractor, if applicable.
Role Requirements
For each proposed role, the proponent should clearly outline the role’s purpose and contribution to the test automation solution, and provide:
Description of accountabilities and responsibilities as they relate to the test automation solution project.
Years of experience in the proposed role and with the proponent organization.
Examples of similar automation projects delivered, particularly those of comparable size, scope, or technical complexity.
Details of projects completed in the retail or regulated sectors (e.g., crown corporations or other enterprise environments with comparable compliance requirements).
Evidence of experience on Microsoft platform projects, including Dynamics 365, Power Platform, or related enterprise systems.
Demonstrated ability to work effectively within business-led or cross-functional projects, applying industry best practices for quality assurance, automation design, and stakeholder collaboration.
Relevant certifications, such as: ISTQB, Microsoft Certified Professional, Azure DevOps, Selenium, or equivalent automation tool certifications
Any other relevant experience or qualifications aligned with ANBL’s project scope, objectives, or technical environment.

CGI proposes a delivery team structured to maximize the benefits of SimpliTest’s low-code/no-code automation capabilities while ensuring ANBL achieves sustainable adoption and long-term value. The team combines governance, technical enablement, and quality engineering expertise to deliver a scalable solution that empowers both technical and business users. CGI with it’s proximity model ensures that the team will have continuity through customer engagement from the client account owner and ensuring that the delivery is consistent and team is retained for the length of the engagement. By retaining the resources ANBL will have relationships built with functional stake holders that will ensure that business led and cross functional delivery models will be executable through the automation process.
Team Composition and Role Alignment
Implementation Lead & Solution Adoption Architect
Years of Experience: 25+ years in testing/QA and systems engineering.
Expertise: Test assessments, Agile/SAFe transformations, BDD coaching, DevOps readiness programs for major public-sector and financial services organizations.

Relevant Projects: Agile-at-Scale transformation for large transit authority; BDD enablement for major Canadian bank; test strategy for crown corporations and regulated sectors.

Automation Architect
Years of Experience: 10+ years in automation engineering across financial services, insurance, and federal engagements.
Expertise: Selenium/Java, Jenkins CI/CD, Git, TestNG, visual regression testing (Applitools/VRT), Azure DevOps pipelines.
Certifications: ISO 27001, ITIL v3, SAFe 4 Practitioner.

Relevant Projects: Designed and implemented regression suites with Selenium/Java/Maven; built Jenkins CI/CD pipelines for automated execution and reporting; ran Azure DevOps pipelines to trigger pre-requisite data, smoke, and regression suites; integrated with test management tools (JTMF/ALM/Jira).

Contribution to ANBL: Configures SimpliTest platform; sets up reusable libraries; integrates automation with Azure DevOps CI/CD pipelines; ensures technical scalability, security compliance, and maintainability of the automation framework; provides guidance on best practices for leveraging SimpliTest’s configuration-driven approach.

Contribution to ANBL: Converts ANBL’s critical workflows into executable BDD scenarios using SimpliTest templates; delivers targeted training and enablement for technical and business users; continues to develop additional test scripts throughout the engagement and provides product support for the duration of the project, ensuring automation assets remain current and aligned with evolving business needs.

Role Requirements and Evidence of Capability
How This Team Supports ANBL’s Objectives
Low-Code/No-Code Enablement: Roles are designed to minimize scripting complexity and empower ANBL’s business users to contribute to automation through structured processes and templates.
Sustainable Adoption: Governance and enablement ensure automation practices become embedded in ANBL’s delivery lifecycle.

A = Accountable
R = Responsible
C = Consulted

CGI can also make available additional Quality Engineers on a time and materials (T&M) basis from our Atlantic Global Delivery Centre to scale test creation and pipeline capacity as coverage expands, maintaining continuity with the above model.
Solution Capabilities and Implementation Requirements

CGI’s SimpliTest is a quality-engineering automation accelerator designed to help organizations achieve higher quality, greater stability, and regulatory confidence while simultaneously reducing delivery cost and accelerating time to value. The solution enables a disciplined shift-far-left approach by embedding automated acceptance testing directly into the lifecycle of requirements, development, and delivery.

Unlike traditional test-last or tool-centric testing models, SimpliTest establishes automated acceptance criteria as the single source of truth for expected system behavior. This approach reduces late defect discovery, minimizes rework, and improves predictability across the delivery pipeline.
Core Solution Capabilities
Built-In Quality Through Automated Acceptance Test-Driven Development (ATDD)

SimpliTest operationalizes ATDD and BDD practices by enabling teams to define executable acceptance criteria before development begins. Acceptance tests are written in business-readable Gherkin and automated from the outset, ensuring:
Early validation of requirements and assumptions
Reduced defect injection during development
Faster feedback loops and improved backlog readiness
Clear, auditable traceability from requirement to evidence

This shift-far-left model has demonstrated 25–35% effort reduction per sprint, 60–70% improvement in defect management, and 20–25% faster response to change requests for clients adopting the approach at scale.
Acceptance Criteria as a Single Source of Truth

SimpliTest integrates directly with Application Lifecycle Management (ALM) tools such as Jira, Azure DevOps, or ServiceNow, allowing acceptance tests to live inside the user story itself. This eliminates duplication across tools and ensures that:
Business, development, and quality stakeholders collaborate on the same artifacts
Acceptance criteria remain visible, reviewable, and improvable by all roles
Automated tests do not require specialized access or separate test management systems
This model increases transparency, reduces handoffs, and avoids the anti-pattern of disconnected test assets that drift from actual requirements.
Self-Service Automation and Continuous Testing
SimpliTest enables self-service execution of automated acceptance tests at any point in the lifecycle. Teams can invoke tests locally or via CI/CD pipelines to validate progress continuously.
Key capabilities include:
Fail-first automated acceptance tests used as development readiness signals
Reusable step definitions provided out of the box for rapid automation
Automated capture of test evidence for audit, compliance, and release confidence
Cumulative test suites executed continuously as part of DevOps pipelines
Once acceptance tests pass with evidence, teams can confidently advance work without additional manual test gates, reducing cycle time while maintaining control.
End-to-End Visibility and Evidence-Based Delivery
SimpliTest produces centralized reporting and test evidence across all executed scenarios, enabling:
Objective, data-driven insight into quality and readiness
Early detection of systemic issues rather than late-stage surprises
Reduced reliance on subjective status reporting or anecdotal progress updates
This evidence-based approach supports regulatory, audit, and compliance needs while improving executive visibility into delivery health.
AI-Augmented Scenario Creation (Roadmap Capability)
SimpliTest is evolving to include AI-assisted capabilities that accelerate and improve test creation, including:
Generation of testable Gherkin scenarios from traditional requirements
Expansion of existing scenarios with negative paths and edge cases
Improvement suggestions for clarity, completeness, and testability
These capabilities further reduce manual effort while strengthening coverage and consistency.
Implementation Requirements
Deployment Architecture
SimpliTest is delivered as a fully containerized solution, designed for rapid, repeatable deployment across enterprise environments. The platform is typically deployed using:
Docker or OCI-compliant container runtimes
Kubernetes or managed Kubernetes services (e.g., EKS, AKS, GKE, OpenShift)
CI/CD pipeline–driven deployments for automated promotion across environments
No proprietary infrastructure or specialized hardware is required. The solution aligns with standard enterprise DevOps and platform engineering practices.
Infrastructure and Resource Requirements
SimpliTest has a low resource footprint and is suitable for deployment in shared or constrained environments.
Typical requirements include:
Compute: Lightweight container execution; no GPU or high-performance compute required
Memory: Modest memory consumption suitable for standard container sizing
Storage: Minimal disk usage for runtime and temporary test artifacts; optional persistent storage for test evidence retention
The platform scales horizontally when deployed in Kubernetes, allowing capacity to grow in line with pipeline execution demand.
Connectivity and Integration Requirements
SimpliTest requires network connectivity to the following systems:
Application Under Test (AUT)
HTTP/HTTPS access to APIs, services, or user interfaces under test
Network access consistent with existing test and CI/CD environments
No invasive instrumentation or code changes required in the AUT
Application Lifecycle Management (ALM)
Connectivity to ALM tools such as Jira or Azure DevOps
Authentication via standard enterprise mechanisms (e.g., API tokens, service accounts)
Read/write access limited to user stories, acceptance criteria, and execution results
Acceptance criteria and automated tests remain authored and stored in the ALM, ensuring traceability and avoiding duplication across tools.
CI/CD Integration
SimpliTest is designed to be invoked as part of existing CI/CD pipelines and requires:
Ability to execute containers from pipeline runners
Standard pipeline permissions to access target environments and ALM systems
Artifact storage for automated test evidence and reports
The solution supports fail-first execution models, self-service test invocation, and continuous testing without introducing additional manual gates.
Security and Compliance Considerations
No customer data is embedded in the platform
Credentials are managed using environment variables or enterprise secrets managers
Network access can be restricted to required endpoints only
Supports deployment in isolated, regulated, or air-gapped environments where required
Implementation Effort

Initial deployment is typically completed in hours to days, depending on enterprise security and network approval processes. Ongoing operational overhead is minimal and aligns with existing container and pipeline management practices.
Platform Automation & Cross-Platform Scenarios

Proponents should describe their ability to support automation across D365 F&O, eCommerce, Power Pages, and Commerce POS. This includes the creation of single automated test cases that span multiple platforms, with context switching (e.g., order creation in eCommerce and fulfillment in F&O). Proponents should also demonstrate the use of pre-built accelerators, connectors, libraries, and security/role automation assets to reduce setup and maintenance. Any limitations, prerequisites, or additional configuration requirements for cross-platform automation should be clearly outlined.

CGI’s SimpliTest platform provides comprehensive, end-to-end automation across D365 F&O, D365 Commerce (eCommerce and POS), and Power Pages by enabling single automated test scenarios that span multiple systems with seamless context switching. Through its library of pre-built accelerators, connectors, role-based authentication assets, and reusable step definitions, SimpliTest significantly reduces scripting effort and maintenance while supporting UI, API, and desktop automation within one unified framework. The solution efficiently orchestrates multi-channel workflows such as order creation in eCommerce, fulfillment in F&O, and validation in POS, while ensuring data continuity across platforms. Any required configurations, such as POS automation setup, test-friendly authentication methods, or environment access, are incorporated into CGI’s onboarding approach to ensure predictable and scalable cross-platform automation.

The proposal should also describe scripting and API integration options for advanced test scenarios, including the ability to blend UI and API steps in the same flow. Proponents should address: (i) Reusable automation elements (functions, methods, blocks), versioning, and sharing across teams. (ii) Support for XPath, CSS, AI-driven locators, JavaScript execution, wait/synchronization mechanisms, and cross-browser compatibility. (iii) Data-driven testing support and management of test data sources. (iv) Parallel execution, mobile/responsive testing, and any limitations related to devices, browsers, or environments.

CGI’s SimpliTest platform provides a low-code/no-code automation environment that enables non-technical users to build tests using visual modeling, drag-and-drop reusable components, and recording utilities, while also supporting advanced scripting for complex scenarios. SimpliTest blends UI and API steps within a single flow, and offers extensive reusable automation elements, including functions, blocks, and shared libraries, managed through version-controlled repositories to promote consistency across teams. The platform supports XPath, CSS, AI-driven locators, JavaScript execution, synchronization controls, and full cross-browser compatibility. SimpliTest enables data-driven testing using structured datasets, databases, APIs, and dynamic data generation. The framework supports parallel execution, responsive and mobile validation, and scalable cloud or on-premise execution grids, with only minor environment-specific limitations related to device configurations or specialized browser settings.
Integration & CI/CD

Proponents should describe their approach to integrating automation solutions with CI/CD pipelines, such as Azure DevOps, including triggering tests, publishing results, creating work items, and maintaining traceability. Proposals should also address interoperability with RSAT test suites and other test assets, integration with test management tools (e.g., TestRail), and availability on marketplaces (e.g., Azure Marketplace, D365 AppSource) including deployment and licensing benefits.

CGI’s SimpliTest platform integrates natively with Azure DevOps and modern CI/CD pipelines, enabling automated test execution, results publishing, defect creation, and full traceability from requirements to test outcomes. Pipelines can trigger SimpliTest tests during builds, releases, scheduled runs, or pull-request validations, with detailed logs, screenshots, and analytics stored directly in DevOps. SimpliTest interoperates with existing RSAT test suites for D365 F&O, complementing form-based RSAT tests with end-to-end UI/API flows across Commerce, POS, Power Pages, and integrated systems. The platform also connects with enterprise test management tools such as TestRail and Azure Test Plans to synchronize test assets and maintain a unified testing repository. Deployment options include Azure Marketplace and cloud-ready provisioning models that streamline onboarding, improve scalability, and provide flexible licensing aligned to enterprise DevOps practices.

CGI’s SimpliTest platform provides comprehensive reporting and analytics capabilities, including step-level execution logs, screenshots, video capture, and performance metrics for every test run. SimpliTest consolidates results across multi-platform scenarios, such as tests spanning D365, eCommerce, Power Pages, and POS, into a single unified report that preserves the order of execution, shared context, and data flow between systems. Reports can be exported in multiple formats, published automatically to Azure DevOps, or integrated with enterprise reporting platforms and dashboards. SimpliTest supports results synchronization with ADO Test Plans, automated defect creation with linked artifacts, and sharing via HTML dashboards, PDF exports, or API-based delivery, ensuring complete traceability and visibility for all stakeholders.

Performance & Stress Testing

Proponents should describe their methodology for performance and stress testing across web, API, and D365 platforms. The proposal should include design, execution, and reporting of performance scenarios, including concurrency, transaction mix, and bottleneck analysis. Any limitations, dependencies, or licensing requirements related to performance testing should also be addressed.

ANBL’s primary objective is to ensure confidence in system stability and responsiveness during critical business operations and future upgrades. While full-scale stress testing for Microsoft Dynamics 365 SaaS environments is typically managed through Microsoft-native tools (e.g., RSAT for regression and Azure Load Testing for performance), CGI’s approach focuses on proactive performance assurance integrated with automation and remediation strategies.
CGI's Approach
We deliver targeted performance validation through practical, actionable methods that complement functional automation:
API-Level Performance Validation
Measure response times for critical services (e.g., order processing, inventory updates).
Validate latency thresholds under normal and peak conditions using automated API calls.
Preventive Measure: Establish baseline thresholds and alerting for deviations.
Corrective Measure: Collaborate with ANBL and Microsoft to adjust configurations or scale resources when thresholds are breached.
Batch Job Monitoring & Throughput Checks
Automate monitoring of D365 batch jobs for completion times, queue depth, and error rates.
Preventive Measure: Identify bottlenecks early and recommend scheduling adjustments.
Corrective Measure: Escalate to ANBL’s technical team for job prioritization or resource allocation.
Transaction Volume Simulation via Data-Driven Automation
Execute large-scale, data-driven automated flows to simulate high transaction volumes across eCommerce → F\&O → POS → Power Pages.
Capture execution time and responsiveness metrics during these runs.
Preventive Measure: Validate performance before major releases.
Corrective Measure: Recommend phased deployments or additional capacity if degradation occurs.
Integration Performance Monitoring
Validate end-to-end latency for integrations (e.g., POS → F\&O → Power Pages).
Automate checkpoints for message queues, API calls, and data synchronization.
Preventive Measure: Monitor integration health continuously.
Corrective Measure: Apply retry logic or adjust integration schedules.
Telemetry & Observability Integration
Leverage available telemetry (e.g., Azure Monitor, pipeline logs) for error tracking and trend analysis.
Note: For SaaS environments, Microsoft limits direct SQL access and Application Insights is primarily for error tracking - not full load metrics.
Preventive Measure: Use telemetry for anomaly detection.
Corrective Measure: Trigger incident response and collaborate with Microsoft support for root cause analysis.
Concurrency & Parallel Execution Testing
Use SimpliTest’s automation framework to run parallel test executions across multiple sessions.
Confirms that D365 can handle simultaneous operations without degradation.
Optional Collaboration

For organizations requiring full-scale load or stress testing, CGI offers advisory support and integration with Microsoft’s RSAT and Azure Load Testing tools. This ensures ANBL can leverage Microsoft’s performance ecosystem while maintaining a unified automation strategy.

1 Executive Summary
New Brunswick Power Corporation serves approximately 420,000 customers across one of Canada’s most geographically
challenging service territories, operating the full energy value chain from nuclear generation at Point Lepreau through to
customer delivery. For a vertically integrated Crown utility, continuity failures have direct public safety, financial, and regulatory
consequences. NB Power’s investment in an enterprise BCM program reflects a strategic commitment to operational
resilience. CGI is the right partner to help NB Power build it.
Why CGI: The Right Partner for NB Power
Proven Canadian BCM partner for public utilities. CGI is Canada’s largest independent IT and business consulting firm,
with more than 1,700 cybersecurity and resilience professionals globally and over 350 in Canada. We have delivered end-to-
end BCM programs for organizations that share NB Power’s operating reality: vertically integrated utilities, publicly
accountable Crown corporations, unionized workforces, and environments governed by ISO 22301, NERC CIP, and sector-
specific regulatory obligations. Our recent engagements at Hydro-Québec (IT service continuity maturity uplift across 12
domains), Télé-Québec (full BCM program design and crisis management implementation), VIA Rail (disaster recovery test
coordination), the City of Montréal (IT business continuity exercises and governance), and CDPQ (BIA and resilience
strengthening) demonstrate that CGI does not just advise on BCM, we build programs that clients operate independently after
we leave.
A bilingual team that combines local talent with global expertise. Our bilingual engagement team is led by Arnaud
Mangematin (ISO 22301 Lead Implementer, 13+ years in BCM, crisis management, and cyber resilience) who personally led
the Hydro-Québec and Télé-Québec engagements, supported by Gaby Abou-Haidar (CBCP, 12 years BCM experience
including enterprise BIA delivery at CDPQ and Société Générale), and Patrick Foley, a New Brunswick–based business
analyst with 25+ years in structured requirements management, stakeholder facilitation, and documentation in public sector
and utility environments. This team brings NB Power direct utility BCM experience, certified methodology rigor, and a local
resource who understands the province’s people and institutions. CGI’s proposed team is fully bilingual in English and French,
a key asset in New Brunswick’s bilingual regulatory and stakeholder environment. While English-only deliverables are
acceptable under the RFP, our French-language capability enables interviews and workshops to be conducted in participants’
preferred language, reducing barriers and enhancing the quality and candor of BIA inputs.
A rigorous, efficient methodology that delivers more value in less time. CGI’s four-phase approach - Current-State
Assessment, Business Impact Analysis, BCM Framework and Business Continuity Plans, and Walkthrough and Closeout is

4.2 Understanding of NB Power
Demonstrate your understanding of NB Power’s operations, or similar publicly owned utilities in Canada, or other unionized

CGI has worked with Canadian public utilities long enough to know that BCM is a direct financial, regulatory, and public safety
obligation, with consequences that are highly visible and politically sensitive.
NB Power is a vertically integrated Crown corporation serving approximately 420,000 customers across one of Canada's most
geographically challenging service territories. It owns and operates the full energy value chain, nuclear generation at Point
Lepreau, hydro, thermal, wind, transmission across more than 26,000 km of lines, distribution into rural and coastal
communities, and customer services, while answering to the New Brunswick Energy and Utilities Board (EUB) on rates,
performance, and financial management. This combination of asset diversity, public accountability, and geographic exposure
creates a BCM landscape that is among the most complex in Canadian utility sector.
NB Power’s BCM is currently decentralized, with plans managed at the individual business unit level, varying levels of maturity,
and no enterprise-wide governance framework in place. This is not unusual for a vertically integrated utility that has grown its
continuity practices organically around operational priorities, but it means that the path forward is not simply to write better
plans. The core challenge is to build an enterprise-wide BCM governance structure that connects what individual business
units already know about their operations into a single, coherent program with shared standards, consistent criticality criteria,
coordinated recovery strategies, and accountable leadership. Our methodology addresses this transition: the current-state
assessment establishes a baseline, the BIA creates an authoritative view of criticality and interdependencies, and the BCM
framework provides governance, plan hierarchy, and maintenance cadence.

Key Risk Considerations for NB Power
Based on experience supporting Canadian energy utilities and critical infrastructure operators, the following resilience risks
materially shape NB Power’s operating environment and public accountability.
Generation concentration risk: Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station represents a substantial share of NB Power’s net
generation and is foundational to the province’s clean energy mix. Extended outages require replacement power purchases
from neighboring jurisdictions, creating financial exposure, rate pressure, and regulatory scrutiny. BCM planning must
therefore address single-asset concentration, contingency procurement, interconnection coordination, and decision-making
protocols under generation shortfall conditions.
Extreme weather and climate-driven disruption: New Brunswick’s exposure to Atlantic storms, winter ice loading, coastal
flooding, and spring runoff creates geographically dispersed transmission and distribution risks. Restoration often requires
coordinated field mobilization, remote facility access, and cross-functional prioritization of critical loads. BCM must bridge
emergency response and structured operational continuity planning, particularly for multi-site or prolonged events.
IT/OT convergence and cybersecurity risk: NB Power operates in a converged IT and operational technology environment
where disruption to SCADA, EMS, grid control systems, or enterprise platforms directly impacts generation dispatch and
customer service continuity. Cyber incidents affecting operational systems must be treated as continuity events, not isolated
IT issues. BCM design must align business recovery objectives with IT disaster recovery capabilities and integrate NERC
CIP, CNSC, and broader cybersecurity governance requirements.
Supply chain and specialized workforce constraints: Long lead times for critical infrastructure components such as
transformers, reliance on specialized nuclear maintenance expertise, and the realities of a provincially concentrated skilled
workforce create structural continuity dependencies. Collective agreement provisions, shift coverage models, and contractor
availability must be explicitly reflected in minimum operating resource assumptions and recovery strategies.
Regulatory and financial exposure: As a Crown corporation regulated by the EUB, NB Power’s operational disruptions
carry direct financial, prudency, and reputational implications. Continuity failures can translate into rate impacts, public
scrutiny, and government shareholder concern. BCM governance must therefore produce audit-ready documentation,
defensible recovery objectives, and clearly documented decision pathways.

NB Power has indicated that up to 16 critical business processes will be assessed, spanning generation, nuclear operations,

• A Business Impact Analysis that surfaces cross-functional and cross-domain dependencies, particularly between

minimum operating resource requirements that reflect operational reality.

Respondent Corporate Profile and Experience
Corporate Profile

An overview of the Respondent’s organization including types of services offered, length of time in business and key accomplishments and projects. This description should be comprehensive enough for Halifax Water to understand the full nature of the services provided.

is a Canadian multinational information technology consulting and systems integration company and was established 47 years ago in Quebec City in 1976 by two founders, Sege Godin our current chairman of the board and André Imbeau, a current board member and advisor to the chairman of the board. Globally, CGI generates over $14.3B CAD annually in revenue with around $2B CAD of this coming from Canada and Canadian clients. CGI is one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world. CGI is 100% Canadian owned and a true Canadian success story. With 91,500+ professionals operating in 40 countries, CGI fosters local accountability for clients’ success while bringing global delivery capabilities to clients’ front doors. CGI applies a disciplined delivery approach that has achieved an industry-leading track record of on-time, on-budget projects. CGI is among the largest IT and business consulting firms in the world. CGI delivers an end-to-end portfolio of capabilities, from strategic IT and business consulting to systems integration, managed IT and business process services, and intellectual property solutions. CGI works with clients through a local relationship model complemented by a global delivery network that helps clients digitally transform their organizations and accelerate results.
CGI in Atlantic Canada

CGI opened its first office in Atlantic Canada in 1991 providing systems integration and IT consulting services to commercial and public sector clients. The company has since grown to employ over 750 employees in Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island and Newfoundland and has added business process services and software application management to its services mix.

In 2001 CGI Group Inc., the largest Canadian IT services firm, and Service New Brunswick Inc. (SNB) signed a memorandum of understanding to negotiate an agreement to headquarter CGI's worldwide government service delivery initiative in Fredericton, New Brunswick. Through the agreement, CGI established its "g-Commerce Lab" at its Fredericton Knowledge Park facilities.

In 2004, CGI and Manulife entered into an outsourcing agreement that led to the launch of CGI's Atlantic Global Delivery Center. With the primary center based in Halifax and the first satellite location in Charlottetown, PEI - the AGDC provides application development, maintenance, and outsourcing services to clients from the US, Europe, and other regions in Canada.

Today, CGI is one of Atlantic Canada’s largest IT employer. With numerous local consulting practices, an extensive banking business, a state-of-the-art global delivery center, and a wide range of infrastructure services, CGI delivers a full breadth of services from Atlantic Canada to clients across Canada, the U.S, and around the globe.

Knowing that partnerships extend outside the workplace, CGI local business units embrace and engage in client causes and in the causes that most positively influence their local communities. This grassroots CSR approach ensures that all CGI communities’ benefit in the best possible manner through financial investments as well as through the volunteer involvement of our members. Our primary objective is to develop relationships within these communities, fostering positive and beneficial changes. After all, we are members of these communities, and our commitment reflects our shared desire for collective betterment.
CGI’s Services
As Canada’s largest end to end IT services firm, CGI offers a comprehensive portfolio of services including:
High-end Business and IT Consulting – Expertise to help grow your organization, accelerate your objectives, improve efficiency, and become more agile.
Systems Integration Services – System architecture, system development and implementation of business and technology solutions.
Application Development and Management – Design, development, implementation maintenance and improvement of business applications.
Infrastructure Services – Comprehensive infrastructure management capabilities that adapt to business requirements and service priorities.
Business Process Services – Management of back-office business processes to streamline operations.
CGI Solutions – Portfolio of 150-plus CGI-developed business and IT solutions that reduce costs and create operational efficiencies.

CGI can handle the full life cycle of IT requirements, from conception and design to implementation and ongoing operations, support, and enhancement. In many cases, we can perform business functions for the client as well, such as back-office processes, to update operations and create a higher level of efficiency. We call this our end-to-end approach to IT services, which enables us to meet clients’ current and future needs.

We deliver the full spectrum of services to help clients become digital enterprises. Organizations in many industries, after several years of investment in digital customer touchpoints and related innovations, are now demanding reliable returns from their IT investments, in a faster and more holistic way. CGI helps clients take an enterprise approach to accelerate and maximize their return on technology investments through relevant applied innovation. We leverage our proximity-based client relationships, world-class delivery capabilities, and operational excellence to help clients become digital across their enterprises. Delivering true business value requires that individual digital initiatives are done as part of an enterprise-wide strategy to modernize underlying core systems, enable a data-centric culture, and implement new technology. CGI helps clients pursue an end-to-end model that includes an enterprise digital strategy encompassing change management; systems design, implementation, and integration; and the use of managed IT and business process services to mitigate cost pressures and fund greater innovation. CGI's approach to relevant innovation is to work jointly with clients through our projects, while seeking opportunities to co-invest in repeatable business solutions.

Demonstration of the Respondent organization overall service delivery capacity and experience, including number of employees, number of contractors and collective years of experience by role.
Utility and Public Sector Industry Experience

CGI has been working in the Utilities industry for many years and has many references across Canada. CGI is well acquainted with Halifax Regional Water Commission, working together since January 2014. Greg Duda, Technical Architect, who served as the data architect for the Operational Data Store (ODS) and Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW), which are foundational elements of the Insights program. James Slupsky, another Technical Architect, also contributes to Halifax Regional Water Commission’s projects. Jason MacDonald, Cyber Security Analyst, is working with the Halifax Water Information and Technology team on the cyber security program to build a suite of technology policies, practices, and standards to guide the safe use of technology in all aspects of Halifax Water business and operations. Finally, Prachi Butala, Senior Project Manager, is working with the HW PMO on projects such as the Physical Access Security System, GIS software upgrade, and implementation of Human Capital Management System (HCMS) modules for Recruitment, Health Safety, and Wellness. All are currently working for Halifax Water.
Worldwide, CGI has over 90,000 consultants in 400 locations across 40 countries. Atlantic CGI is home to approximately 750 employees with the following expertise by Service Category:
Project Management Services – over 60 employees.
Business Analysis Services – over 60 employees
Change Management Services – over 20 employees.
IS Systems, Design and Architecture Services – over 20 employees.
Data Management and Data Analysis – over 15 employees.

The advantage of partnering with CGI is our ability to tap into a vast network of expertise, even if a specific resource isn't based in Atlantic Canada. With access to CGI's 90,000 consultants globally, we ensure that the right skills and experience are always available to support any project, no matter the location.
