Project Management Services

CGI has been delivering Project Management services since 1994, using our Client Partnership Management Framework (CPMF) or its predecessor, the Project Management Framework. This long history underscores our deep expertise and commitment to excellence in project management. With more than 1,500 project managers in Canada, CGI offers an extensive pool of highly skilled individuals. Each of our project managers have attended mandatory trainings, pursue continuous training, and benefit from mentorships as needed.
Adherence to Industry Standards:

CGI's Project Management Practice adheres to industry best practices and standards such as PMI-PMBOK, ISO-12207, ISO-9001, IEEE-1074, and SEI-CMM. Our methodologies are inspired by these standards, ensuring high-quality and consistent project delivery.
Methodological Training:

All CGI project managers are trained in the Client Partnership Management Framework (CPMF). New employees receive introductory briefings, while those in leadership roles undergo compulsory, in-depth training leading to certification. Additionally, CGI invests significantly in ongoing professional development and certifications across various relevant fields, including PMP, ITIL, and CMMI.

Our training program represents a significant on-going investment in our members and our clients. Included in this investment is the amount that we have spent on our members attending conferences, in-house training programs, training programs that our members take on their own time and for which CGI reimburses and our per seat cost for SkillPort, our e-learning tool. CGI’s training program has led to certification of members in the following areas:
ITIL V2 and V3
Quality
Security
Privacy
Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence
Oracle Technologies (e.g. RDBMS, RAC, Fusion, OBIEE)
JAVA
Microsoft (e.g. .NET, SharePoint, Dynamics)
Project Management Professional (PMP) Certification
Certified Business Analyst Professional (CBAP)
Document Management and Records Retention
Content Management Systems (e.g. Adobe CQ, Drupal, and Kentico)
Globally, CGI has resources certified in the following areas:
Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI)
ISO 9001:2000 Quality Management System
Information Technology Infrastructure Library (ITIL)
Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK)
ISO 12207 Framework for Software Life Cycle Processes
IEEE-1074 Process Map for Software Life Cycle Processes
The Open Group Architecture Framework (TOGAF)
Control Objectives for Information and Related Technologies (COBIT)

In addition to formal training and certification CGI invests in Practice Groups. The Practice Groups are fully supported by all levels of the executive management team with a CGI Director assigned responsibility to each practice group. The primary goal of the Practice Group is to:
Improve member engagement, participation, and learning opportunities.
Leverage members’ knowledge and ideas, and build upon their good work.
Improve the quality and consistency of our deliverables to our clients.
Execute on our strategic business plan by aligning and empowering our practice groups.
These goals are accomplished by creating a coordinated and collaborative approach to key business and technology areas and include:
Establishing standards, methods, tools, and templates
Identify gaps in our resources and/or skills
Each practice group produces deliverable templates
Strategies for improving service delivery and quality
Lunch and learn sessions where resources are educated in latest trends or concepts
Size of Practice:

CGI's project management practice is supported by a global network of qualified Project Managers. This includes a large pool of experienced professionals managed through a comprehensive database that matches their skills and experience with project requirements. Our PM Practice Council facilitates global and local collaboration, ensuring effective resource utilization and adherence to common guidelines and tools.
Deliverables:

Developing Terms of Reference for a Project: CGI develops detailed project charters, defining high-level requirements, scope, costs, and resource needs. These charters provide clear, actionable foundations for all projects.

Developing Detailed Project Management Plans: We create comprehensive project management plans that outline cost, schedule, and resource allocations. These plans are integral to our structured approach to project execution.

Managing All Phases of a Project: Our project management approach covers all phases from initiation to post-implementation review. We ensure rigorous resource and schedule management, facilitating successful project completion.

Implementing and Monitoring Quality Assurance and Control: Quality assurance and control processes are embedded within our CPMF, ensuring projects meet the necessary standards and satisfy client needs.

Delivering Services in Line with PMI Standards: Our services align with the PMI’s standards as detailed in PMBOK. The CPMF, which is ISO 9001 certified, provides a robust framework for managing all critical project areas, ensuring compliance with industry standards.

Developing and Implementing Communications Plans: We develop and implement effective communications plans that include progress reports and timely information distribution to stakeholders, ensuring transparency and engagement throughout the project lifecycle.

Identifying, Documenting, and Analyzing Risks: Risk management is a key component of our project management practice. We identify, document, and analyze risks, facilitating issue resolution and mitigating potential project impacts.
Establishing and Implementing Change Control Processes: Our change control processes are designed to handle project changes efficiently, maintaining project integrity and alignment with client goals.

Managing Project Budgets: We manage project budgets meticulously, establishing cost baselines and providing regular reports on actual versus budget forecasts, ensuring financial control and transparency.

Comprehensive Project Management: Our end-to-end project management services ensure all aspects of the project are handled professionally and effectively. We leverage the CPMF to deliver projects on time, within budget, and to the highest standards of quality.

Agile Deliverables: Deliverables in agile project management are crucial for ensuring transparency, communication, and project progress. By showcasing product demos, progress reports, bug fix lists, and completed task lists, agile teams are better equipped to handle challenges and deliver high-quality products. Ultimately, the deliverables of an agile sprint guarantee efficiency and consistency in executing complex, evolving projects.

With our extensive experience, certified methodologies, and detailed framework, CGI is well-equipped to deliver high-quality project management services that consistently meet and exceed client expectations.
Business Analysis Services

Since 1976, CGI’s Business Analysis Services are designed to support clients in achieving their business objectives through detailed process optimization and requirements definition. Our team adheres to industry standard methodologies, with staff certified in PMI-PBA or CBAP, ensuring that we deliver high-quality, consistent results.
Key Offerings:

Business Process Analysis and Design: We analyze, define standards, and optimize business processes to improve performance measures. This includes designing new processes and redesigning existing ones to enhance efficiency and effectiveness.

Business Requirements Definition: We discover, analyze, define, and document the requirements related to specific business objectives, ensuring that all needs are comprehensively understood and addressed.

Business Architecture Analysis and Design: Our services analyze and develop the design, structure, and behavior of the current and future states of your organization, providing a common understanding of its framework.

Methodological Adherence and Training: All our practices are in line with the standards set out by the Project Management Institute (PMI) and the International Institute of Business Analysis (IIBA). Our staff undergoes rigorous methodological training to stay updated with the latest industry practices.
Additional Services: We also offer project management, change management, and quality assurance services specific to project deliverables, ensuring a comprehensive approach to business analysis.
Our Approach:

Assess: We conduct a thorough analysis of your business data and processes to identify gaps, risks, and opportunities for efficiency. Stakeholder mapping and engagement are critical at this stage to ensure successful adoption of new processes or systems.
Plan: Collaborating with your project team and stakeholders, we develop a detailed plan that outlines deliverables, timelines, methodologies, techniques, and tools necessary to achieve your goals.

Perform: Our analysts support all phases of the project lifecycle, from viability research to change adoption and benefits realization. We utilize various business analysis tools and techniques to ensure comprehensive and effective solutions.

Sustain: We ensure that stakeholders take ownership of changes, and that knowledge transfer is complete. Continuous service improvement is supported through metrics and monitoring tools like key performance indicators (KPIs).
Benefits of Our Services:
Knowledge Transfer and Skills Development: We share expertise and best practices with your teams, enabling continuous service improvement.
Bespoke Solutions: Our services are tailored to your specific business needs, providing custom technology, processes, and enterprise architecture.
Cost Efficiencies: By offering business analysis for the required duration, we help reduce long-term overheads.
Flexibility and Scalability: Our services can be scaled up or down based on your business needs or project phase.
Change Management: We assist stakeholders, users, and customers in embracing new processes or systems, ensuring successful adoption and realization of business benefits.

Through our comprehensive Business Analysis Services, we ensure that your organization is equipped with the tools, knowledge, and strategies necessary to navigate change and achieve sustainable improvements in performance and efficiency.
Change Management Services

CGI has over 30 years of experience providing global change management services. Our Change Management Practice includes applying change management processes and tools to create strategies for adoption, supporting the design, development, delivery, and management of communications, conducting impact analyses, assessing change readiness, and identifying key stakeholders. We provide input, document requirements, and support training program design and delivery. Our practice involves completing change management assessments, identifying and managing anticipated resistance, consulting and coaching project teams, and creating actionable deliverables for communication plans, sponsor roadmaps, coaching plans, training plans, and resistance management plans. We support and engage senior leaders, coach managers and supervisors, support organizational design and define roles and responsibilities, coordinate efforts with other specialists, and integrate change management activities into project plans. Additionally, we evaluate and ensure user readiness, manage stakeholders, track and report issues, define and measure success metrics, monitor change progress, support change management at the organizational level, and manage the change portfolio. CGI’s CM approach is adaptable and aligns with Halifax Water's preferred methodology. There are 20+ Change Management/Organizational Change Management (OCM) resources in Atlantic Canada. Globally, we have 4,100 OCM resources worldwide, with 766 located in Canada.
Methodology:

Our change management approach combines Prosci's ADKAR method, with many of our consultants certified, and the expertise of our advisors, enhanced by best market practices from our extensive experience. We focus on people through these key levers:
Support for Leaders: Strengthening the leadership of your managers and ambassadors of change.
Co-construction and Mobilization: Engaging managers, superusers, and change agents to achieve a transformation that they understand and find inspiring.
Personalized Pathways: Developing personas and associated pathways (mobilization, communication, skills development) tailored to each user profile for an optimal user experience.
Additionally, our approach ensures smooth transitions, maintains business continuity, aligns stakeholders, and fosters a culture of adaptability and innovation.
Phase 1: Plan for Change

With a current-state understanding, our experience, and a vision of the future state, we solidify the approach, techniques, timelines, and leadership responsibilities for the change process. Activities include documenting business drivers and objectives, assessing current culture, aligning sponsors and leaders, developing stakeholder engagement plans, conducting change impact analyses, and assessing organizational readiness. We also create the change strategy and develop communication and training plans. Deliverables are a vision document, culture assessment, sponsor agreement, stakeholder engagement plan, change impact analysis, organizational readiness report, change strategy, and a learning roadmap/training plan.
Phase 2: Engage the Organization

Our OCM lead works with your project lead to understand the change's impact on roles, structure, and performance metrics. Activities include establishing a change network, coaching leaders, implementing readiness plans, setting up OCM systems, communicating the need and benefits of the change, identifying benefits metrics, establishing KPIs, ensuring feedback mechanisms, and developing communication and training materials. Deliverables are a change toolkit, coaching materials, change readiness tracker, KPIs, a feedback process, a benefit register, and communication and training materials.
Phase 3: Enable People

This phase ensures that affected individuals have the skills, knowledge, tools, and motivation needed for the change. Activities include deploying training, monitoring engagement and adoption, evaluating change status, assessing training effectiveness, implementing new policies and procedures, rewarding performance, and celebrating success. Deliverables include a training and communication report, change status review, organizational design services, and reports from design stage plans.
Phase 4: Achieve Success

We verify that the steps taken reinforce the behavioral shifts necessary for sustaining the change. Activities include transitioning change management roles to internal teams, updating performance metrics and rewards programs, creating measurement and tracking capabilities, establishing ownership of KPIs, and reviewing the benefits register. Deliverables are a knowledge transfer plan, benefits realization plan, measurement and tracking plans, and updated performance management metrics.
Training for Members:

Specific to Change Management, we are in the process of developing a Change Consulting Acadacemy which will meet the requirements for IACMP. We also offer Prosci training throughout the year. CGI encourages our staff to continually improve their skills by providing ongoing training opportunities (including computer-based training, classroom training, special interest groups, and practices), which enables us to have the most qualified resources available to provide services to our clients. Our Target 24 learning program encourages training with goals to build necessary skills for client needs, diversify our talent pipeline, acquire new skills and certifications in emerging technologies and leadership, leverage the CGI Academia training site, and empower members to take charge of their career development. As a full-service provider, we offer the global resources, industry expertise, stability, and dedicated professionals needed to achieve results.
IS Systems, Design and Architecture Services

CGI has been providing IS Systems, Design and Architecture Services in Atlantic Canada for over 25 years and to Halifax Water for 10 years. Our local practice includes 12 enterprise, solution and cybersecurity architects, all of whom have access to CGI’s Enterprise Architecture Center of Excellence (EACOE) and our global Enterprise Architecture (EA) team which collectively provide a comprehensive and pragmatic approach to enterprise and solution architecture.

Our hands-on experience encompasses a wide range of EA frameworks and methodologies, including TOGAF (The Open Group Architecture Framework), EA 2.0, Zachman Framework, Gartner's EA methodology and ArchiMate. This diverse expertise allows us to tailor our approach to meet the specific needs and contexts of our clients.  Furthermore, our enterprise architecture practice is designed to support digital transformation initiatives, ensuring that organizations can leverage technology to achieve their strategic goals. We also emphasize sustainability, helping institutions integrate sustainable practices into their IT and business processes.

In addition to architecture services, CGI has provided expertise to Halifax Water in system integration design, development and testing; data analysis, design, extraction-transformation-load and conversion; and report design, development and testing.
Data Management and Data Analysis

CGI has extensive experience in the end-to-end processes required to strategize, design, develop, and implement successful data and analytic programs. With our deep understanding of the differences between analytic design and traditional software development, CGI quickly identifies the current state of analytic and BI capabilities, the desired future analytic program vision, and then facilitates a strategy session with stakeholders to identify quick wins and a long-term roadmap for moving to a data-driven organization, including leveraging Open Data solutions.

CGI has experience in the structure of data warehouses and advanced analytical modeling and is expert in end-to-end data science. CGI can quickly develop and implement proofs of concept and pilots to ensure our clients get the answers they need while developing an analytic program, including organizational governance, skills and capabilities, data management and governance, and technical infrastructure.

CGI’s Analytics, A.I and Machine Learning practice comprises of over 10,000 members across all relevant disciplines: analytics strategy, data governance, technology selection, artificial, visualization, implementation (big data and traditional DW in cloud and on-premise environments), and ongoing sustainment. Through CGI’s Delivery Manager the Internal Audit Centre will have access to over 4,500 BI specialists in Canada and many more worldwide.

Our Analytics, A.I and Machine Learning team is comprised of members who have also worked with the Microsoft BI stack including (Reporting Services, Integration Services, and Analysis Services) since 2000, with Power Query, Power Pivot and Power View since 2013, and Power BI since 2015.
Data Management:
Experience and Expertise:
Years of Experience: CGI has been providing Data Management services for over 15 years, consistently delivering high-quality solutions to our clients.
Industry Certifications: Our staff hold certifications such as Certified Data Management Professional (CDMP) and other industry-recognized qualifications.
Size of Practice: Our team comprises a substantial number of employees, all skilled in various aspects of data management.

Data Governance: Developing data governance principles to meet business and regulatory requirements.
Database Standards and Policies: Creating and maintaining database standards and policies.
Database Design and Testing: Supporting database design, creation, and testing activities.
ETL Processes: Designing and developing Data Extraction, Transformation, and Loading (ETL) processes from multiple systems into a data warehouse environment.
Backup and Storage Strategies: Designing database backup, archiving, and storage strategies.
Database Performance Management: Managing database availability and performance, including optimization (tuning), backup, recovery, incident, and problem management.
Data Analysis:
Our Data Analysis Services provide comprehensive solutions to help organizations harness their data for strategic decision-making and operational efficiency.
Experience and Expertise:
Years of Experience: We have over 15 years of experience in delivering Data Analysis services, working with a wide range of clients to provide actionable insights.
Industry Certifications: Our analysts are certified in industry-standard methodologies such as Six Sigma, and our team undergoes regular methodological training.
Size of Practice: Our Data Analysis practice includes a significant number of skilled employees and contractors dedicated to various analytical tasks.
Service Offerings:
Data Collection and Analysis: Collecting and analyzing data to identify patterns, trends, insights, and solutions.
Focus on Analytics Needs: Working closely with project teams to understand and maintain focus on data analytics needs, including critical metrics and KPIs.
Data Strategies: Creating data strategies that support data acquisition, integration, and data modeling.
Data Presentation: Data collection, examination, and presentation, including data mining, data visualization, statistical analysis, predictive modeling, and dashboards.
Reporting and Decision Support: Generating reports and presenting findings to aid decision-making.
Methodology:
CGI employs a structured and comprehensive approach to data management and analysis, leveraging our extensive experience and industry best practices.
Data Management Methodology:
Governance and Compliance: Developing and implementing data governance frameworks to ensure compliance with business and regulatory requirements.
Standardization: Establishing and maintaining database standards and policies to ensure consistency and quality.
ETL Development: Designing robust ETL processes to ensure seamless data integration from multiple sources.
Performance Optimization: Continuously monitoring and optimizing database performance to ensure high availability and reliability.
Data Analysis Methodology:
Strategic Alignment: Aligning data analysis efforts with organizational goals to ensure relevant and impactful insights.
Advanced Techniques: Utilizing advanced analytical techniques, including data mining, predictive modeling, and statistical analysis, to uncover valuable insights.
Visualization and Reporting: Presenting data in clear and actionable formats, such as dashboards and detailed reports, to support informed decision-making.
Data Warehouse and Business Intelligence Architecture:

Our approach will involve designing and implementing a scalable and flexible data warehouse architecture that meets the organization's current and future needs. We will adhere to industry best practices and standards to ensure data integrity, security, and accessibility, while also enabling efficient data integration and analytics.
Early Adoption: CGI believes in early adoption of modern data technologies to enable scalable and efficient solutions.
Comprehensive Data Governance: Ensuring quality and compliance throughout the lifecycle, empowering organizations to harness the full potential of their data.
Data Analytics and Reporting:

With over a decade of expertise in Data Analytics and technology enablement, CGI has successfully led numerous enterprises through the processes of evaluation, strategy development, and implementation of advanced analytics solutions. CGI's comprehensive approach ensures that clients are well-equipped with the necessary tools and strategies to maximize the potential of their data, driving informed decision-making and achieving significant business outcomes.

We employ advanced data analytics techniques to derive actionable insights from the organization's data. This will involve data mining, statistical analysis, and predictive modeling to uncover patterns, trends, and correlations. Additionally, we develop customized reporting solutions to present key findings in a clear and concise manner, tailored to the needs of different stakeholders.
Customized Analytics Solutions: Empower informed decision-making.
Intuitive Dashboards: Facilitate ease of interpretation for clients, ensuring they can quickly and effectively derive insights from their data.
Data Science:

Our data science approach focuses on leveraging machine learning, artificial intelligence, and other advanced analytics techniques to address complex business problems and drive innovation. This will involve data exploration, hypothesis testing, and iterative model development to deliver predictive and prescriptive analytics capabilities that add significant value to the organization.
Cutting-Edge Techniques: Drive meaningful insights.
Continuous Iteration: Achieve continuous improvement.
Expertise in Data Science: Ensures actionable outcomes from data analysis.
Visualization:

We utilize cutting-edge visualization tools and techniques to transform complex data into intuitive and interactive visualizations. This enables stakeholders to gain deeper insights, identify trends, and make data-driven decisions more effectively. Our approach prioritizes user experience and accessibility to ensure that visualizations are informative, engaging, and easy to interpret.
Visually Appealing Dashboards: Enhance understanding and engagement.
Knowledge Sharing: Ensure clients can maintain and support visualizations independently.
Data Quality:
Ensuring data quality is a top priority. We implement data quality management processes to cleanse, standardize, and validate data, ensuring its accuracy and reliability.
Strong Emphasis on Data Quality: Ensures integrity and reliability.
Rigorous Measures: Maintain high standards of data quality.
Continuous Monitoring: Maintain data quality standards.
CGI’s Expertise and Commitment:

CGI has more than 7,200 Data and Artificial Intelligence specialists around the globe. We are a leading end-to-end data provider with a comprehensive catalogue of services specially tailored to handling the issues being faced by Halifax Water. We have established strong partnerships with data and artificial intelligence market leaders to ensure we offer our clients an agnostic approach to solutioning their AI transformations.

On July 24, 2023, CGI announced the planned investment of $1 billion over the next three years to support the continued expansion of its Artificial Intelligence (AI) services and solutions. Over the last two decades, CGI has delivered intelligent automation and AI technologies as part of our services and solutions, notably in our IP where we can test and train new models with speed and security—and then apply the learnings across our end-to-end offering’s portfolio.

Today, our consultants can draw upon proven AI use cases and pre-built, industry-focused solutions powered by trusted domain data sets to help clients navigate the hype and make the best-return investments. As the next generation of AI evolves and client demand rises, we are committed to expanding our talent base and capabilities in line with our Build and Buy profitable growth strategy. We believe that we are at the beginning of a new wave of innovation and that the business value of AI will be achieved through the combination of human expertise and ethical use of technology.

Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning: At CGI, we believe that organizations must embrace AI quickly and responsibly. CGI works with our customers to explore and evaluate ROI-led use cases that achieve the highest returns on their investments, while following "responsible use" governance. CGI's Responsible AI Framework (RAI) ensures that AI services and solutions that CGI designs, builds, or operates follow three key principles, ensuring AI solutions are robust, ethical, and trustworthy.

Generative AI: For early-stage and rapidly evolving technologies like Generative AI, CGI has excellent experience implementing and driving value throughout the process. CGI’s proven Art of the Possible Framework addresses clients’ objectives by leveraging our best practices and expertise to identify the most suitable areas of opportunity for AI/Gen AI-driven solutions and establish organizational procedures for ongoing use case identification, assessment, and implementation.

NL Health Services Innovation Strategy
As the provincial health authority in Newfoundland and Labrador, we want to provide the
best possible care to our patients, clients and residents; however, we are challenged by
growing health concerns and budgetary constraints. This requires us to think outside the
box and to find creative solutions to improve patient outcomes and quality of care. An
innovation strategy enables us to formally articulate a path to achieve our vision – one
that positions us to harness innovation to improve patient care and to elevate NL Health
Services as a leader in the Canadian health innovation sector.
Goals
➢ to advance health-care services and programs in NL Health Services
through the application of innovative solutions.
➢ to maximize health systems efficiencies and minimize associated costs by
leveraging the innovation ecosystem to build partnerships and generate
revenue; and
➢ to generate economic development in the province.
Mission
Our mission is to create a supportive environment that fosters innovation so that we
may meet the expectations of our stakeholders:
➢ current and future patients, who depend on NL Health Services for care, expect
access to the best quality of care possible, in a timely manner.
➢ the broader health system, including health-care providers and health-care
organizations, expect leadership, support and open collaboration as we create a
health system of the future.
➢ the residents of the province expect appropriate, accountable use of resources;
and,
➢ partners, who team up with us to improve health-care technologies, expect
open, timely collaboration and adoption of the most promising technologies.
Strategy
The four pillars of our innovation strategy are:
➢ Continued application of a value-based lens in decision-making
➢ Development of a Health Innovation Acceleration Centre
➢ Cultivation of an innovation culture
➢ Building local, national and international partnerships across and within the
innovation ecosystem
Opportunity
NL Health Services is seeking proposals for the development of artificial intelligence (AI)
strategy that provides an approach to identifying (or intake) and evaluating opportunities
where AI may help resolve an issue within NLHS. The strategy should also address
Page 3 of 8
Limited Call - RFP # 2025-5090(A)
AI Strategy
sourcing AI solutions and executing pilots and limited trials to prove the value, and how to
decide viability of candidate solutions. Healthcare organizations across Canada and
internationally are experiencing increased challenges in responding to the needs of
clients, patients, and community stakeholders. Populations are ageing, many individuals
live with multiple comorbid conditions, and we are currently in a global health human
resources crisis. The potential for AI technologies to help solve healthcare challenges and
provide value regarding patient outcomes and cost efficiencies is undeniable. However,
the adoption of AI in healthcare is currently limited as regulatory, integration,
standardization, training, and reimbursement requirements are navigated. As a Living lab
and Testbed for new technologies and ideas, NL Health Services is seeking a partner to
help with a strategy that enables the successful navigation through AI opportunities in this
environment.
List of requirements:
1. Proposal must outline the process to be utilized for development of the AI
Strategy.
2. Proposal must outline how the AI Strategy may be implemented within
current Innovation practices and policies.
3. Proposal must outline an Implementation Plan that highlights the path to executing
the proposed strategy.
4. Proposal must outline how the AI Strategy will address solution post-
implementation benefits realization.
5. The scope of the AI Strategy to be developed would encompass a project
life cycle from opportunity ideation up to implementation and post-
implementation benefits realization. It should be lightweight, flexible and
easy to navigate.
6. The partners should collaborate with NL Health Services and develop a
good understanding of the ask and the unique environment of the
organization in order to ensure the final deliverable meets the intended
objectives.
7. Partners should ensure that proposal is aligned to NLHS Innovation
strategy, and the Living Lab goals for proving new technology and ideas.
8. Partners should have demonstrated expertise in the area of business
development and strategic operations and be familiar with the Newfoundland
and Labrador healthcare public sector.
9. NL Health Services policies, practices, and other applicable regulations
must guide potential solutions.
10. The proposal should demonstrate how to avoid algorithmic bias and the risk
mitigation strategy of the proponent.
11. The proposal must have a financial proposal of not more than $120,000.
12. NL Health Services will schedule an information session with the partners to
answer any questions about the opportunity.
Experience and Similar Projects:
Page 4 of 8
Limited Call - RFP # 2025-5090(A)
AI Strategy
Proponent(s) must include details of experiences and similar projects where the bidder has
developed an AI strategy that helped the client successfully navigate AI potential in their
organization. The detailed experiences must include the client’s name, go-live date for the
solution and name and contact number for the person responsible for managing the
relationship with the bidder.
IT Requirements
General Privacy Requirements
➢ Any collection, use, or disclosure of personal health information by the vendor
software must be in compliance with the Access to Information and Protection of
Privacy Act (ATIPPA, 2015) and the personal health information act (PHIA) and
all regulations.
➢ Vendor must identify a designated/appointed contact person(s) for privacy.
➢ Vendor must have an established and implemented Privacy Program that can
demonstrate compliance with NL provincial legislation, including:
o established and implemented security, privacy and IM policies and
procedures for collection, storage, transfer, copying, modification, use and
disposition of PI and PHI; and
o an established and implemented privacy breach and incident management
protocol relevant to the solution proposed, that includes immediate
notification of any data breaches.
➢ Vendor must provide, for solutions that process PI or PHI, a third party privacy
impact assessment.
➢ Any custom solution that that is required to collect, use or disclose PI or PHI, is
subject to a privacy impact assessment. Vendor must cooperate and assist with
NLHS in completion of privacy impact assessments.
General Security Requirements
➢ All vendors are expected to provide assurance to the NLHS of their solution and
operational compliance to security best practices. This can be demonstrated with
related certifications (e.g. SOC2, ISO).
➢ Vendor COTS solutions are expected to have been subject to periodic third party
security assessments (vulnerability assessment, penetration testing, threat risk
assessment), of which, the executive summary and subsequent risk action plan
will be provided to the client upon request.
➢ Vendor must have an established risk management policy and related procedures,
that address risks associated with solution being provided, and any subsequent
support provided to client for solution operations;
➢ Vendor has a documented incident response plan, that includes timely notification
to client of any security breach, and subsequent activities required to respond
(periodic communications to client, compliance with client change management
procedures, submission of post mortem report for client review);
Page 5 of 8

➢ Vendor must provide training on privacy and security to all staff that may be exposed
to client data;
➢ Vendor staff have taken an oath of confidentiality that includes access to client data,

Data Security

➢ Vendor solution includes a capability to completely delete/return all client data (in

➢ Vendor has capability to segregate client data and processing from other third

➢ All access to solution resources must logged; and

Access and authentication

Memory)
➢ CrowdStrike Falcon is utilized for endpoint protection and is required to be

Databases and Storage Standard

1 Executive Summary
From "We Don't Have a Playbook" to "We Can Deploy AI Confidently"
Newfoundland and Labrador Health Services (NL Health Services) has invested significantly in Epic as its enterprise EHR and
has bold plans to maximize the suite of capabilities that Epic offers, including its leading AI modules and functionality. At the
October 17 bidder conference, Dan Bond captured the central challenge: “We don’t have a playbook—how do we get from an AI
idea to an executed product?”
This question lies at the heart of what NL Health Services needs. The organization already has a strong foundation through its
Value-Based Procurement model and proven eight assessment criteria (Strategic Alignment, Patient Outcomes, System
Performance, Economic Value, Resources, Service Scope, Value, and Capacity). The challenge is not the governance model
itself, but translating it into AI-specific frameworks, processes, and tools that enable confident evaluation, adoption, and scaling
of AI solutions.
CGI’s approach is built to close this gap by aligning people, process, and technology. With the right decision framework, talent,
and tools, NL Health Services can confidently govern, manage, and implement AI innovations across its system.
Our Proposed Approach
CGI’s solution is designed to work within NL Health Services’ existing governance processes—not to replace them. Our approach
has three pillars:
1. Refinement of Governance and Solution Assessment: We operationalize your eight assessment criteria specifically
for AI, creating concrete decision-making tools grounded in evidence and aligned to your organizational values. Rather
than introduce a new framework, we translate what already works into an AI-ready evaluation model.
2. Building Capabilities, Talent and Tools: We define the key enablers and develop ready-to-use playbooks and
templates for intake, evaluation, vendor selection, and decision documentation. These empower NL Health Services to
manage AI governance and adoption independently.
3. Epic-First and Value-Based Focus: We emphasize a pragmatic, Epic-first approach that leverages the AI capabilities
already embedded in your EHR before pursuing external vendors. Up to five high-value Epic AI pilots will be selected
and business-cased for measurable ROI, ensuring early success stories to build confidence and momentum.
The Strategic Advantage of Epic-First Approach
An Epic-first strategy maximizes that existing investment while reducing risk and accelerating time to value compared to layering
in new AI vendors when capabilities already exist within Epic. CGI recommends prioritizing Epic's native AI capabilities such as
Velocity predictive models, Care Navigator population health, and analytics before pursuing external vendors. This approach is
supported by real-world evidence from health systems of comparable size and complexity.
Health systems that have pursued Epic-first strategies report consistent results: 15–25% readmission reduction using Epic
Velocity models, 30–50% sepsis mortality reduction with the Sepsis Protocol bundle, and 5–10% OR efficiency gains through
duration prediction1. These outcomes were achieved within 4–12 weeks of model activation, significantly faster than developing
custom AI solutions or implementing external vendor platforms, which typically require 12–24 weeks and substantial custom
integration work2. The Cleveland Clinic, Kaiser Permanente, and Intermountain Healthcare have all demonstrated that Epic's pre-
built models, which are peer-reviewed and continuously refined by Epic across thousands of health systems, deliver measurable
clinical and operational value rapidly.
Strategic Analysis and Planning Are Essential
AI success is not automatic. CGI’s experience shows that activating AI models without proper planning leads to low adoption,
alert fatigue, and disappointing ROI. The difference between success and failure lies in addressing key readiness factors before
deployment.
1 See Appendix Section 4.2 for Epic Results Statistics & Healthcare AI Implementation
2 Actual outcomes will depend on NL Health Services-specific factors and implementation readiness.
© 2025 CGI Inc. Confidential 1
NL Health Services | RFP # 2025-5090(A) – AI Strategy: Schedule A – Proposal
Our methodology ensures each success factor is integrated into the 16-week engagement and the engagement deliverables:
• Data Quality Validation: Ensuring 12–24 months of clean historical data in Epic.
• Workflow Readiness: Defining how alerts integrate into clinical and operational processes.
• Governance Structure: Establishing decision authority, review cadence, and escalation paths.
• Measurement Framework: Setting baseline metrics and defining success thresholds before pilot launch.
• Change Management: Engaging champions and building adoption capacity across teams.
Through this preparation, NL Health Services will be ready to activate AI confidently and achieve measurable outcomes within
months of pilot execution.
What CGI Will Do
Over 16 weeks, CGI will collaborate with NL Health Services to deliver a practical, operational AI Strategy that aligns directly with
your Value-Based Procurement and Reverse Partner Pitch frameworks.
By the end of the engagement, NL Health Services will have:
• A clear, usable AI Strategy that fits within your existing Value-based Procurement and Reverse Partner Pitch Processes
• Ready-to-use templates for evaluating AI opportunities
• Up to five priority AI use cases identified and ready to pilot
• Detailed playbooks for intake, evaluation, vendor selection, and pilot management
• Definition of first-wave pilots that can be launched within 4-6 months from Epic go-live3, with measurable outcomes by
6-9 months post-launch4
What Makes This Approach Different
Operationalizing What You Already Have: The existing eight-criteria evaluation model works. The strategy translates that
proven approach into an AI-ready framework—elevating, not replacing, what’s already effective within NLHS.
Epic First: The first priority is your existing Epic investment, not new vendors. A tailored decision tree ensures maximum ROI on
the EHR, keeps data under NLHS control, and reduces integration complexity from day one.
Delivering Immediately Usable Artifacts: Playbooks, templates, and evaluation tools are built for immediate use—practical
resources NLHS teams can apply the next working day. Leadership gains a consistent, ready-to-use evaluation process for every
AI opportunity.
Derisking First-Wave Pilots: Each pilot is backed by a detailed business case, success metrics, and clear go/no-go criteria. The
result: fast-moving, measurable outcomes within 6–9 months that demonstrate real value and guide future scaling.5
Balancing Strategy and Pragmatism: The framework delivers the strategic direction NLHS needs to scale AI confidently while
staying grounded in simplicity, values alignment, and immediate actionability.
A Blend of Global and Local Expertise: Our approach delivers a blend of local AI talent to build playbooks with senior strategic
thought leaders to help guide NLHS in its strategy to boldly and confidently scale AI over a longer horizon.
3 This is dependent on data quality and availability as well as user adoption. If the required data or data quality are not achieved
by Epic go-live or user adoption is not sufficiently high, the timeframe for achieving results may change.
4 Timelines are estimated based on an Epic-first approach dependent on the Epic solution being live and availability of the
required modules.
5 This is dependent on data quality and availability as well as user adoption. If the required data or data quality are not achieved
by Epic go-live or user adoption is not sufficiently high, the timeframe for achieving results may change.
© 2025 CGI Inc. Confidential 2
NL Health Services | RFP # 2025-5090(A) – AI Strategy: Schedule A – Proposal
Strengthened by Expert and Strategic Partnerships
In addition to a strong core team, CGI is proud to be able to bring the expertise of global experts in AI, like our Dr. Diane Gutiw,
Vice-President and Global AI Research Lead, who has been appointed to the Government of Canada’s Artificial Intelligence (AI)
Strategy Task Force, a select group of 26 experts guiding the country’s renewed approach to artificial intelligence.
We are also proud to include Dr. Stephen Czarnuch, PhD, P.Eng., as a key advisor on this engagement. Dr. Czarnuch is the
Director of MUN’s Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Special Advisor on AI and Medicine. He also serves as Emergency Medicine
Research Chair within the Faculty of Medicine and Associate Professor in both the Department of Electrical and Computer
Engineering and the Discipline of Emergency Medicine. Through this partnership, NLHS benefits from cutting-edge expertise at
the intersection of AI, clinical research, and health systems engineering, ensuring all proposed AI solutions are both technically
sound and clinically grounded.
In addition, CGI’s partnership with Epic provides access to specialized Epic Platform and Velocity Analytics expertise that will
support the confirmation of pilot AI modules and use cases, as well as the development of robust business cases to guide
implementation.
Why CGI
1. We understand your innovation process. We're not imposing a new framework; we're operationalizing the process you
already have.
2. We know Epic. CGI and Epic have a unique relationship. Epic doesn’t typically partner with implementing partners, but they
are a partner of ours and we have worked closely with them, particularly in EHR implementation in Alberta. We have
knowledge of the AI capabilities already embedded in Epic—such as readmission prediction, sepsis detection, population
health risk assessment—that can be activated quickly with clear ROI.
3. We think execution first. We deliver playbooks and templates you can immediately use, not abstract strategy documents
that sit on shelves.
4. We know Canadian healthcare. We understand provincial health systems, budget constraints, regulatory requirements
(PHIA, ATIPPA), and the importance of keeping data under Canadian control.
AI Strategy: Timeline & Investment
CGI will deliver a complete, operational AI Strategy in 16 weeks, progressing through four phases:
1. Discovery and Governance Assessment (Weeks 1 to 4): Stakeholder interviews, Epic readiness assessment, and
alignment to Value-Based Procurement.
2. Framework Development (Weeks 5 to 8): Operationalization of the eight-criteria model and creation of the Epic-First
Decision Tree.
3. Playbooks and Pilot Design (Weeks 9 to 14): Development of AI intake, evaluation, and vendor selection tools, and
detailed business cases for pilot use cases.
4. Validation and Launch Preparation (Weeks 15 to 16): Final governance and capability validation, readiness review,
and transition to execution.
By Week 16, NL Health Services will possess a board-ready AI Strategy, complete governance toolkit, and validated first-wave

3.1.3 How This Strategy Operationalizes Value-Based Governance Model
The Strategic Advantage of Epic-First Approach
An Epic-first strategy builds on the strategic foundation and investments of NL Health Services, maximizing your existing
investment while reducing integration risk and accelerating time to value. CGI recommends prioritizing Epic’s native AI capabilities,
such as Velocity predictive models, Care Navigator for population health, and built-in analytics, before engaging external vendors.
Comparable health systems have demonstrated consistent success with this approach. Epic Velocity models have achieved 15
to 25% reductions in readmissions, Sepsis Protocol bundles have reduced sepsis mortality by 30 to 50%, and surgical duration
prediction has improved operating room efficiency by 5 to 10%.8 Leading organizations such as the Cleveland Clinic, Kaiser

and operational improvements quickly and reliably. These results were achieved within 4 to 12 weeks of activation, far faster and
less resource-intensive than external solutions, which typically require 12 to 24 weeks or longer and significant custom integration.

AI without strategic planning often face adoption failure, alert fatigue, and limited ROI. The difference between success and failure
lies in addressing key readiness factors before and during deployment.

This diversity helps in addressing various aspects of AI deployment, from legal and compliance issues to technical and ethical considerations, ensuring a holistic approach to AI governance and diversity can also help in the design and deployment of other programs, services and technologies.

Specialized Knowledge: Acquiring and developing specialized knowledge in AI ethics, bias, and societal impacts is crucial to successful AI adoption. This expertise ensures that AI systems are designed and implemented responsibly, minimizing risks and maximizing benefits for citizens. Typical IT organizations do not have this kind of specialized knowledge, and they must work with business units that do. This is also true of AI adoption, but it is also true of other initiatives and therefore special knowledge assets need to be identified, inventoried, maintained and utilized in decision-making related to a variety of programs, services and technologies.

Risk Management: Integrating AI risk management into existing frameworks helps identify and mitigate potential risks associated with AI systems, such as biases and privacy concerns. Being proactive in the identification and mitigation of risks ensures that technologies are safe and reliable. Too often, organizations track project and operational risks but fail to identify, manage and measure social, environmental, ethical and other governance risks that affect people’s lives.

Transparent Decision-Making: Establishing transparent decision-making processes for AI-related decisions builds accountability and trust. Clear documentation of AI model development, testing, and deployment ensures that decisions are made transparently and can be audited if necessary. This is also true of other business and technology decisions. As the public demands greater transparency and accountability, organizations of the future are cultivating greater transparency across the board.

Continuous Monitoring and Adaptation: Continuous monitoring and adaptation of AI systems ensure that they remain compliant with evolving regulations and technological advancements. This is also true more broadly in terms of cyber security, privacy and data use, but can be applied to the processes of maintaining and continuously modernizing processes and technologies to ensure that services are achieving their intended objectives and understanding any unintended outcomes as they arise. Regular audits and updates to policies help maintain the integrity and effectiveness of governance.

A modern operating model to deliver innovation and transformation is essential for driving value creation and effectively executing strategy in today’s fast-paced, complex business environment. It outlines how various functions within an organization should work together to deliver value to customers and stakeholders. An effective innovation model integrates the organization’s structure, culture, processes, technology, and decision-making frameworks to meet key objectives such as efficiency, scalability, innovation, and adaptability.
CGI’s Directed Enterprise Evolution approach envelopes innovation within the elements of sound transformation management, which include:
Strategic Planning: Developing a clear vision and roadmap that aligns with the organization’s goals and objectives.
Change Resilient & Innovation Culture: Developing a vision and strategy for cultivating a culture and workforce that is resilient to change and embraces innovation.
Process Optimization: Streamlining business processes to improve efficiency and reduce costs.
Data-informed Decision Making: Optimizing data collection, management and usage to support decision making.
Technology Integration: Seamlessly incorporating new technologies into existing systems to enhance functionality and performance.
Change Management: Ensuring that all stakeholders are on board and that the transition is smooth and minimally disruptive.
Continuous Improvement: Regularly assessing and refining strategies to adapt to new challenges and opportunities.

This approach enables organizations to evolve in a directed and controlled manner, leveraging the latest advancements in technology while maintaining stability, continuity, and a focus on outcomes over outputs. Our approach is complementary to the emerging trend in healthcare towards new models of care, and particularly value-based care modalities. For this reason, we feel our capabilities are aligned well to support NLHS with Pillar #1 – continued application of a value-based lens in decision making.

Our expertise in Innovation Management, as well as our experience mentoring and coaching innovators and partners, also means we are well equipped to support Pillar #2 - Development of the Healthcare Innovation Acceleration Center (HIAC) in terms of strategic and operational support to the HIAC as well as through support to incubation and acceleration initiatives targeting innovators.

Internally and with our clients and partners, CGI promotes a culture of innovation and change resilience. We have developed our own model, called Business Agility, a combination of industry leading practice from SAFe, PROSCI and Design Thinking, which we train, coach and support our clients to cultivate. This will allow us to support NLHS in Pillar #3 - Cultivation of an Innovation Culture.
For more about CGI and Innovation Management: Innovation management | CGI.com

For innovation to succeed, it needs to be led, managed and governed effectively, as we addressed in this section.  In the next section we demonstrate how we also support our clients and partners to design and develop innovative solutions.
Design and Develop Solutions

CGI operates 12 innovation centres across North America and Europe that serve as hubs with a dual aim: to showcase CGI’s leading cross-industry innovations from around the world; and, to work with clients to accelerate their digitization by offering unique facilitated co-innovation capabilities that focus on applied and tangible innovations.

Our partners and clients don’t have to visit one of our innovation centres to experience our innovation offerings. CGI has a variety of services to support our partners to innovation through transformations as well as through smaller “sprints.”

CGI works with a variety of client and community partners to build local, national, and international partnerships across and within the innovation ecosystem (Pillar #4), which we will speak to in more detail below in section 4.5. Our repertoire of offerings to enable the innovation journey is large and we are not able to cover all of them here, so we have focused on several that are aligned with the objectives under Development of the Healthcare Innovation Acceleration Center (HIAC) (Pillar #2). We use a variety of approaches to turn the creativity of your experts into customer-focused innovation.
Figure 2: CGI Service Offerings to Enable Innovation

CGI has been selected as an innovation partner of both the Canadian Space Agency, Alberta Innovates, Alberta Health and the British Colombia Ministry of Health. Here is a snapshot of some of the innovative solutions that have emerged from these partnerships.

AI is transforming the landscape of business and technology, offering unprecedented opportunities for innovation, efficiency, and improved decision-making. The same principles being applied in the emerging AI governance realm can be applied across all business and technology decision-making processes as we steer and accelerate evolutionary processes towards truly human-centered health services.

CGI has pledged to invest over $1B in AI by 2028, which includes expansion of the company’s AI-related consulting services, responsible and ethical-use delivery platforms and accelerators, intellectual property AI-enablement, global employee hiring and training, and operational excellence efficiencies.
CGI is already a leader in AI governance and innovation, and we have an industry-leading AI Innovation Framework that we use to help clients at any stage in their AI adoption journey.

CGI’s Responsible Use of AI methodology and consulting framework addresses a wide range of potential risks and opportunities, supporting CGI’s business and strategic IT consultants as they partner with clients to design and build a solid foundation for the deployment of AI within their enterprises. The framework complements CGI’s AI Design Sprint Workshops which were recently cited as a key strength by clients who participated in the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide Artificial Intelligence Services 2023 Vendor Assessment:

“According to customers, CGI's strengths are the company's ability to conduct workshops that improve their awareness of AI and its value for their business; apply functional- or industry-specific methodologies and assets to solve their issues; create quality, trusted data sets and pipelines for AI model training; and provide knowledge transfer and training to internal IT and development teams.”
Here are just a few examples of engagements where CGI worked closely with healthcare clients to innovate with AI:

CGI’s emerging technology team in the UK has been exploring in the realm of using Augmented and Virtual Reality (AR/VR) in medical rehabilitation and have found innovation often springs from the desire to make therapy more engaging and motivating for patients. This is precisely what drove the development of "Limbsync," a CGI-developed gamified application.

Limbsync is essentially an interactive application designed to enhance hand-eye coordination and fine motor skills in individuals undergoing hand mobility rehabilitation. We developed the current version as a pilot to demonstrate capability, the look and feel and that it works based on requirements. We continue to work with the client to update this and further extend features. Developing Limbsync has been a rewarding experience; it's an engaging rhythmic solution that gamifies Mirror Therapy—a method used to treat stroke victims with motor impairments.

Another area the CGI emerging technology teams have explored is the area of navigation or wayfinding through buildings and facilities. Several prototypes have been developed and tested in educational and business environments. The phone app overlays a live image on your screen with directional cues and arrows. This could easily be adapted for a healthcare setting to support patients and hospital staff with ensuring people get to where they need to be.

CGI has a large portfolio of successful innovation work with health clients and skilled talent to support NLHS in their innovation journey. In addition to our consulting services, we also own a large portfolio of SaaS offerings (CGI Intellectual Property) as described in more detail in the next section.
CGI’s Innovative Solutions
CGI’s portfolio of Intellectual Property is large. The image below is a snapshot of some of the most relevant SaaS offerings we have to support healthcare clients.
Figure 3: A snapshot of CGI's Healthcare SaaS Intellectual Property (IP)

CGI’s SaaS solutions are developed to meet the highest industry, privacy and security standards (i.e. Information Technology (IT) Specifications *page 10 of the RFP.)  While we can’t showcase them all here, we would like to introduce OMNI360, a proprietary product that provides a next-generation service platform and product family designed to support health and social services with a customer-oriented approach. We have a variety of platform solutions as well as smaller interoperable modular products that might be relevant to NLHS and the Development of the Healthcare Innovation Acceleration Center (HIAC) (Pillar #2).

OMNI360 is more than just a customer and patient-information system. OMNI360 is a suite of easy-to-use, modular tools designed to optimize operations in the healthcare and social-services fields. The solution guides professionals in patient and customer interactions, supports self-service and integrates affordably and flexibly across all open customer and patient-information systems. The Finnish health and social-services model is one of the most advanced in the world. Developed in Finland, OMNI360 now stands ready to benefit health organizations in the 40 countries where we operate. Developed in close cooperation with doctors and other medical experts, OMNI360 clarifies and facilitates the planning, implementation and evaluation of patient care, streamlines work and frees up time for interactions that improve the patient and customer experience.
OMNI360 modules include:

OMNI360 Share collects disparate patient data in one place, making it easily and securely available and sharable across organizational boundaries. Better data access enables health professionals to more accurately evaluate patient care and free up time for interactions that enhance the patient experience.

Self-service Registration is a digital workflow management system for the health and social services sectors. The solution allows the patient or customer to check in and receive information in a more efficient and automated manner. It also enhances and automates the process for calling in a medical professional.

Speech Recognition quickly and easily produces text, providing your organization with a more efficient workflow that saves time and money while creating a better user experience. This solution includes vocabulary for specialized medical care, basic healthcare and social services, updated as new vocabulary is created. Artificial intelligence allows the application to constantly evolve—even adapting to the user’s style of speaking.

Merlot Medi is a management system for doctors in charge of emergency medical services (EMS), EMS supervisors and consulting physicians. The system transmits real-time data from the ambulance unit to hospitals and other emergency treatment facilities. With it, paramedics can make swift and correct decisions about a patient’s treatment at the site of an accident without a doctor being physically present. Merlot Medi is strongly integrated with emergency-care center and hospital information systems.

CGI PulseAI is an advanced hyper-automation platform designed to enhance efficiency and reduce costs through intelligent process automation (IPA). It leverages artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to automate and streamline business processes across various industries. Key features of CGI PulseAI include:
Intelligent Document Processing: Automates the extraction, classification, and processing of data from documents, reducing manual effort and errors.
Predictive Analytics: Provides insights-driven decision-making by analyzing data patterns and predicting future trends.
Conversational AI: Enhances customer interactions through AI-driven chatbots and virtual assistants.
Seamless Integration: Easily integrates with existing systems to ensure smooth implementation and operation.
CGI PulseAI helps organizations achieve greater operational efficiency and improved decision-making capabilities.

CGI TrustedFabric Health Interoperability Platform is an innovative solution designed to enhance data sharing and interoperability within the healthcare ecosystem. Here are some key features and benefits:
Secure Data Sharing: It uses a distributed ledger technology (DLT) to ensure secure and trusted data transactions across various healthcare entities.
Data Ownership and Control: The platform allows healthcare organizations to maintain control over their data, sharing it on a need-to-know basis rather than a want-to-have-it basis.
Improved Coordination: By enabling seamless data sharing among providers, clinicians, and patients, it supports better coordination of care and improved patient outcomes.
Flexibility and Integration: CGI TrustedFabric integrates with existing technical infrastructures, eliminating the need for costly new systems or complicated data warehouses.
Transparency and Auditability: The platform provides real-time dashboards for monitoring data access and transactions, ensuring full transparency and auditability.
CGI TrustedFabric helps healthcare organizations achieve a connected and interoperable ecosystem, enhancing efficiency and patient care.
CGI ProperPay is a comprehensive payment integrity solution designed to help healthcare payers identify, prevent, and recover improper payments. Here are some key aspects of CGI ProperPay:
Advanced Analytics: Utilizes predictive analytics and machine learning to detect hidden patterns and anomalies in claims data, identifying high-potential claims for recovery.
Fraud, Waste, and Abuse Prevention: Helps prevent fraudulent activities and reduces waste by providing tools to easily identify and audit suspicious claims.
Customizable Rules Management: Features a library of cognitive business rules that can be tailored to specific reimbursement policies and methodologies.
Workflow Management: Offers a comprehensive workflow solution that streamlines the audit process, from screening claims to conducting detailed audits.
Real-Time Communication: Facilitates real-time interactions between payers and providers, enhancing the efficiency of medical records requests, audit findings, and appeals.
Proven Results: CGI ProperPay has helped healthcare insurers recover over $3 billion in improperly paid medical and pharmacy claims.
Overall, CGI ProperPay is designed to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of claims processing, ensuring that healthcare funds are used appropriately and effectively.
CGI has a vast portfolio of IP to draw from. For more information on CGI IP, see our website: CGI - Solutions | CGI.com.

PART 1 – INVITATION AND SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS
1.1 Invitation to Proponents
1.1.1 Invitation
This Request for Proposals (the “RFP”) is an invitation by Newfoundland Labrador Hydro (“Company”)
to prospective proponents to submit proposals for Reporting and Data Analytics Solution, as further
described in Section A of the RFP Particulars (Appendix B) (the “Deliverables”).
Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro (Hydro) is part of a group of utility companies which own and operate
facilities for the generation, transformation and distribution of electricity to utility, industrial and residential
customers in the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador. Hydro is a body incorporated pursuant to the
laws of the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador, and having its head office at the City of St. John’s,
in the Province of Newfoundland and Labrador.
Hydro is the people’s Crown utility – providing safe, cost-effective, reliable electricity that our customers
can count on. We have operations across the province including major generation and transmission
assets. Our provincial transmission system spans thousands of kilometers, and includes dozens of high-
voltage terminal stations and lower-voltage distribution stations. We power our families, friends, and
neighbours in 200+ communities across the province, and approximately 80 per cent of our provincial
energy comes from clean hydroelectric generation. Hydro harnesses energy opportunities to benefit the
people of Newfoundland and Labrador.
Our organization, after much consultation, recently launched our new strategic plan which is defined by
three overarching themes – Serving Our Province, Working Together, and Enabling Sustainable Growth.
These represent the foundational principles on which our organization will deliver for the people of the
province.
Further information about Hydro can be attained at https://nlhydro.com
Hydro is issuing this Request for Proposal (RFP) to identify and implement a Reporting and Data
Analytics solution that will replace the existing IBM Showcase Reporting platform and potentially other
reporting and analytics tools currently in use at Hydro (ie. Spreadsheet Server, IDEA Analytics). This
initiative is part of Hydro’s broader strategy to enhance data accessibility, analytical capabilities, and
insight-driven decision-making across the organization.
Hydro currently operates on the JDE Enterprise One ERP system, hosted on-premise. While this system
serves as a central repository for operational and financial data, the current reporting tools present
limitations in flexibility, scalability, and user experience. Showcase, the legacy reporting solution, lacks
the advanced features required to meet evolving business needs and support timely, data-informed
decisions.
The proposed reporting and data analytics solution must address the following core objectives:
• Data Integration: Seamlessly connect to JDE Enterprise One utilizing JDE security model and
other internal and external data sources. The solution should support a wide range of data formats
and enable the consolidation of large, complex datasets.
Page 3 of 42
• Advanced Analytics: Provide robust analytical capabilities including filtering, searching, trend
analysis, and visualization tools that empower users to explore data intuitively and extract
actionable insights.
• Comprehensive Reporting: Offer a broad suite of reporting features such as customizable
dashboards, scheduled reports, ad hoc queries, and export options. The solution should support
both operational and strategic reporting needs across departments.
• User Accessibility and Experience: Ensure ease of use for a diverse user base, including non-
technical staff. The interface should be intuitive, responsive, and support self-service reporting
where appropriate.
• Performance and Scalability: Handle high volumes of data efficiently, with minimal latency. The
solution should be scalable to accommodate future growth in data volume and user demand.
• Security and Governance: Comply with Hydro’s data governance policies, including role-based
access controls, audit trails, and secure data handling practices.
Hydro is committed to selecting a solution that not only meets current requirements but also positions the
organization for future innovation in business intelligence and reporting. Proponents are encouraged to
demonstrate how their solution aligns with Hydro’s strategic goals and supports long-term value creation.
1.1.2 Proponent Must Be Single Entity
The proponent must be a single legal entity that, if selected, intends to negotiate and enter into the
contract with Company. If the proposal is being submitted jointly by two (2) or more separate entities, the
proposal must identify only one (1) of those entities as the “proponent”. The proponent will be responsible
for the performance of the Deliverables.
1.1.3 Bidding System Registration
All proponents must have a vendor account with Company’s electronic bidding system at
https://nlhydro.bidsandtenders.ca/Module/Tenders/ and must be registered as a plan taker for this
opportunity. This will enable the proponent to download the solicitation document, to ask questions, to
receive addenda email notifications, download addenda, and submit their proposal electronically through
the bidding system.
1.2 RFP Contact
To contact Company in relation to this RFP, proponents must initiate the communication electronically
through the bidding system. Company will not accept any proponent’s communications by any other
means, except as specifically stated in this RFP.
For the purposes of this procurement process, the “RFP Contact” will be:
Mark Green – MarkGreen@nlh.nl.ca
Proponents should only contact the RFP Contact where specifically instructed to in this RFP. All other
communication in relation to this RFP, up to and including the submission of the proposal, must be
through the bidding system, as described above.
Page 4 of 42
Proponents and their representatives are not permitted to contact any employees, officers, agents,
elected or appointed officials, or other representatives of Company, other than the RFP Contact,
concerning matters regarding this RFP. Failure to adhere to this rule may result in the disqualification of
the proponent and the rejection of the proponent’s proposal.
Communications from sources other than the RFP Contact shall be considered as unofficial and not
binding. Company shall not be responsible for any information provided by or obtained from any other
source.
1.3 Contract for Deliverables
1.3.1 Type of Contract
The selected proponent will be requested to enter into direct contract negotiations to finalize an
agreement with Company for the provision of the Deliverables. The terms and conditions found in the
Form of Agreement (Appendix A) are to form the basis for commencing negotiations between Company
and the selected proponent.
1.3.2 Term of Contract
The terms of the agreement will be in effect until the completion of the Deliverables
1.4 RFP Timetable
1.4.1 Key Dates
Issue Date of RFP [March 9, 2026]
Deadline for Questions [March 20, 2026 11:59:59 PM local time

If a Public Opening is applicable, the proposals will be opened at 9:00 a.m Newfoundland island time on
the following business day. The public opening will be virtual only. Proponents can attend the public
opening by phone. The list of proponents that submitted proposals will be posted to Company’s website.
Public Opening Call-In Details: 1-844-426-4405; Access Code 160 776 4210#
1.5 Submission Instructions
1.5.1 Submission of Proposals
Proposals must be submitted electronically through the bidding system at:
https://nlhydro.bidsandtenders.ca/Module/Tenders/
Submissions by other methods will not be accepted.
In the event of any technical issues, proponents should contact support@bidsandtenders.ca. For
questions pertaining to a specific bid opportunity, contact the RFP Contact for this procurement.
1.5.2 Proposals to Be Submitted on Time
Proposals must be finalized and fully uploaded in the bidding system on or before the Submission
Deadline. The time of receipt of proposals shall be determined by the bidding system web clock. Late
submissions will not be accepted by the bidding system and will be disqualified as late.
Proponents are cautioned that the timing of submission is based on when the proposal is received by the
bidding system, not when a proposal is submitted by a proponent. As transmission can be delayed due
to file transfer size, transmission speed, or other technical factors, proponents should plan to submit
proposals well in advance of the Submission Deadline to avoid submitting late due to technical issues.
Proponents submitting near the Submission Deadline do so at their own risk.
The bidding system will send a confirmation email to the proponent advising when the proposal was
submitted successfully. If you do not receive a confirmation email, contact the bidding system’s technical
support immediately.
1.5.3 Proposals to Be Submitted in Prescribed Format
Proposal materials should be prepared and submitted in accordance with the instructions in the bidding
system, including any maximum upload file size.
Documents should not be embedded within uploaded files, as the embedded files may not be accessible
or evaluated.
1.5.4 Amendment of Proposals
Proponents may amend their proposals prior to the Submission Deadline. However, the proponent is
solely responsible for ensuring that the amended proposal is received by the bidding system by the
Submission Deadline.

1.5.5 Withdrawal of Proposals
At any time throughout the RFP process until the execution of a written agreement for provision of the
Deliverables, a proponent may withdraw a submitted proposal. Prior to the Submission Deadline,
proponents may withdraw a submitted proposal through the bidding system. To withdraw a proposal after
the Submission Deadline, a notice of withdrawal must be sent to the RFP Contact and must be signed
by an authorized representative of the proponent.
