PART 2 – EVALUATION, NEGOTIATION, AND AWARD
2.1 Stages of Evaluation and Negotiation
Company will conduct the evaluation of proposals and negotiations in the following stages:
a) Stage I – Mandatory Submission Requirements
b) Stage II – Evaluation
c) Stage III – Pricing
d) Stage IV – Concurrent Negotiations and BAFO
a. Initial Ranking of Proponents
b. Concurrent Negotiations
c. Submission of BAFO
d. Evaluation of BAFO and Final Ranking of Proponents
e) Stage V – Contract Negotiations
a. Ranking of Proponents
b. Contract Negotiation Process
c. Time period for Negotiations
d. Failure to Enter into an Agreement
e. Notification of Negotiation Status
2.2 Stage I – Mandatory Submission Requirements
The mandatory submission requirements are set out in Section C of the RFP Particulars (Appendix B).
2.2.1 Determination of Compliance
Stage I will consist of a review to determine which proposals comply with all of the mandatory submission
requirements. Company reserves the right to review and revise Stage I compliance results at any
subsequent stage in the evaluation and/or negotiation process.
Proposals that do not contain all mandatory submission requirements, prepared in accordance with the
instructions provided in this RFP, will be deemed non-compliant and cannot be evaluated. Non-compliant
proposals will be subject to a rectification process, whereby proponents are provided an opportunity to
rectify the identified non-compliances.
2.2.2 Rectification Notice
In response to a non-compliant proposal, Company will issue a rectification notice via email to the
proponent. The rectification notice will present a list of identified non-compliances, a reference
substantiating each non-compliance; and procedures for rectifying the proposal, including a deadline.
2.2.3 Rectification Period
The Rectification Period referenced in RFP Timetable will begin to run from the date and time that
Company issues the rectification notice. The proponent will have a single Rectification Period to revise
and submit a rectified proposal. A rectified proposal received after the Rectification Period deadline will
be excluded from further consideration.
2.2.4 Scope of Rectification
Page 8 of 42
Rectification is limited to the specific list of non-compliances presented on the rectification notice. A
rectified proposal must address only the non-compliances presented in, and only through procedures
prescribed by, the rectification notice. For greater clarity, proponents shall not make other revisions, or
submit additional information, outside these parameters.
A rectified proposal prepared and submitted accordance with the requirements of this RFP, and the
applicable rectification notice, will replace, in full, only those parts of the original proposal identified by
the rectification notice as non-compliant. A rectified proposal submitted with changes beyond the scope
of the rectification notice may be disqualified.
2.2.5 Compliance of Rectified Proposals
If a proponent submits a rectified proposal during the Rectification Period which does not address all of
the non-compliances according to the procedures prescribed by the rectification notice, that rectified
proposal will be excluded from further consideration.
If, through rectifying its proposal, a proponent creates new non-compliances, outside those presented in
the rectification notice, those additional non-compliances will not be subject to further rectification
processes and the rectified proposal will be excluded from further consideration. If a proponent submits
a rectified proposal in a manner inconsistent with the procedures prescribed by the rectification notice
that rectified proposal will be excluded from further consideration.
Where a rectified proposal is deemed compliant by Company, it will move forward to technical evaluation.
2.3 Stage II – Evaluation
Stage II will consist of the following two (2) sub-stages:
a. Mandatory Technical Requirements
b. Non-Price Rated Criteria
2.3.1 Mandatory Technical Requirements
Company will review the proposals to determine whether the mandatory technical requirements as set
out in Section D of the RFP Particulars (Appendix B) have been met. All mandatory technical
requirements will be evaluated as pass or fail. Questions or queries on the part of Company as to whether
a proposal has satisfied the mandatory technical requirements will be subject to the verification and
clarification process set out in Part 3. If a proposal fails to satisfy the mandatory technical requirements
it will be excluded from further consideration.
Eligible proposals that satisfy all mandatory technical requirements will move forward to the evaluation
of rated criteria
2.3.2 Non-Price Rated Criteria
Company will evaluate each qualified proposal on the basis of the non-price rated criteria as set out under
Evaluation Criteria in Section F of the RFP Particulars (Appendix B).
Proposals must meet or exceed the specified minimum performance threshold for each rated criterion.
Proposals that fail to meet any minimum performance threshold will be excluded from further
consideration. Proposals that meet all minimum performance thresholds will move forward.
Page 9 of 42
2.4 Stage III – Pricing
Stage III will consist of a scoring of the submitted pricing of each qualified proposal in accordance with
the price evaluation method set out in Section G of the RFP Particulars (Appendix B). The evaluation of
price will be undertaken after the evaluation of mandatory requirements and rated criteria has been
completed.
In the event that a proponent’s pricing appears to be abnormally low in relation to the Deliverables,
Company may require the proponent to provide a detailed explanation of the pricing information to
account for the low level of price and confirm that all requirements in respect of the Deliverables have
been taken into account. If the proponent is unable to satisfactorily account for the abnormally low pricing,
Company may reject the proposal. Company may also reject any proposal that contains unbalanced
pricing. Pricing may be considered unbalanced where nominal or significantly understated prices are
proposed for some elements of the Deliverables and inflated prices are proposed for other elements of
the Deliverables. Unbalanced pricing includes, but is not limited to, “front-loaded” pricing which contains
inflated pricing for Deliverables to be provided or completed at the beginning of the contract, offset by
understated pricing for Deliverables to be provided or completed later in the contract.
2.5 Stage IV – Concurrent Negotiations and BAFO
2.5.1 Initial Ranking of Proponents
After the completion of Stage III, all scores from Stage II and Stage III will be added together and the
proponents will be initially ranked based on their total scores.
2.5.2 Concurrent Negotiations
Company intends to invite the top - ranked proponents to enter into concurrent negotiations. During these
concurrent negotiations, Company will provide each proponent with any additional information and will
seek further information and proposal improvements from each proponent.
During this stage, Company will schedule a commercially confidential meeting (“CCM”) with each of the
top-ranked proponents to engage in direct dialogue with the proponents for the purposes of clarifying and
coming to a common understanding of Company’s requirements and the proponent’s proposal. Additional
details and instructions in respect of the CCM process will be provided to the top-ranked proponents.
[During this stage, proponents may be required to present a demonstration of their solution via
teleconference session at their own expense.
• Proponent representatives at the teleconference session will include key representatives of the
proponent.
• This is NOT to be viewed as a sales presentation. Company will use the session to validate the
proponent’s Proposal.
• Proponents will receive further instructions upon invitation to attend the teleconference session.
• Company reserves the right to determine the extent of the presentation required.
• Company reserves the right to terminate a presentation that fails to address the specific
requirements and instructions.
Page 10 of 42
2.5.3 Submission of BAFO
After the expiration of the concurrent negotiation period, each proponent will be invited to revise its initial

APPENDIX B – RFP PARTICULARS
A. THE DELIVERABLES
Hydro is continuing to evolve toward a more data driven and metric based performance model.
This requires the merging, restructuring, and reporting on large amounts of data from a variety of
systems, data sets, and sources.
Hydro relies on multiple reporting solutions, as none alone meets all functional needs. Some tools
analyze corporate transactional data for business intelligence, while others enable direct data
analysis in Excel. However, these solutions do not fully address Hydro’s changing reporting
requirements, and some existing solutions are nearing end of life and must be replaced.
Hydro intends to implement a centralized, Commercial off the Shelf (COTS) reporting and data
analytics solution designed to replace existing reporting platforms such as Showcase and
Spreadsheet Server. The objective is to enhance reporting and business intelligence capabilities.
The proposed solution should enable data import from multiple sources, support query
generation, facilitate data search and filtering, produce comprehensive reports, integrate
seamlessly with business systems, and maintain compatibility with existing JDE E1 security
protocols.

We appreciate the opportunity to submit our proposal and look forward to participating in the next stage of the process.

Executive Summary

CGI will deliver a modern, secure, and scalable reporting and data analytics platform that replaces NL Hydro’s legacy reporting tools, reduces manual effort, and enables faster, data-driven decision-making across the organization.

The proposed solution establishes a single, governed analytics platform that integrates JD Edwards EnterpriseOne and other enterprise data sources into a unified, trusted source of truth. Business users will be able to access intuitive dashboards, perform ad hoc analysis, and generate insights independently reducing reliance on technical teams while improving accuracy and responsiveness.

CGI’s approach is designed to deliver immediate value while minimizing implementation risk. We will take a structured, phased approach to implementation and report transition, working with NL Hydro stakeholders to prioritize critical reporting needs and ensure continuity of business operations. This approach enables a smooth evolution from legacy tools while supporting long-term simplification and improved usability.

A key advantage of CGI’s proposal is its strong value profile. By leveraging NL Hydro’s existing Microsoft 365 E5 investment and aligning with Microsoft Fabric and Azure-native services, the solution minimizes incremental software costs and reduces total cost of ownership. At the same time, it improves productivity by reducing manual data preparation and enabling self-service reporting across the organization.
CGI brings a combination of local delivery, deep technical expertise, and proven experience in utility environments that reduces delivery risk and ensures successful outcomes:

Proven utility and JDE experience – CGI has successfully delivered large-scale data and analytics transformations for organizations such as Hydro-Québec, including modernization of legacy reporting platforms and integration of complex enterprise data sources.  CGI also has a global delivery practice for JDE, as well as experience within the proposed core Canadian team for this RFP response.

Local delivery with national scale – The engagement will be led from Newfoundland and Labrador, ensuring close collaboration and accountability, supported by CGI’s broader Canadian delivery network and specialized analytics expertise.
Low-risk, fixed-price delivery – CGI provides a predictable implementation model with clear governance, structured delivery phases, and controlled deployment processes.
Optimized use of existing Microsoft investment – CGI’s approach leverages NL Hydro’s existing Microsoft investment, avoiding unnecessary licensing costs and maximizing return on existing investments.
This engagement will be delivered using the same proven delivery patterns and methodologies successfully applied in CGI’s work with Hydro-Québec.

To support long-term success, CGI includes a comprehensive training and adoption approach that equips NL Hydro users to confidently transition to the new platform. This includes role-based training, user-friendly documentation, and ongoing support to embed new ways of working with data across the organization.

CGI’s proposal delivers a high-value, low-risk analytics platform that is simple to use, cost-effective to operate, and designed for long-term growth. By combining local leadership, proven delivery experience, and a practical, outcome-focused approach, CGI will help NL Hydro turn its data into a strategic asset that supports better decisions today and into the future.

Corporate Overview

CGI is a global IT and business consulting services firm founded in 1976, with headquarters in Montréal, Québec. With decades of experience delivering enterprise data, analytics, and systems integration solutions, CGI is an established leader in supporting utilities, public sector organizations, and regulated industries.

Data and analytics is a core CGI service offering, supported by global centres of excellence and experienced regional delivery teams. CGI has extensive experience working within JD Edwards environments, including integrating, modernizing, and optimizing reporting and analytics platforms aligned with JDE security and data structures. This is not a new line of business, but a mature and well-established capability within CGI’s service portfolio.
Proposed Solution Overview

CGI is proposing a cloud-based reporting and data analytics solution built on Microsoft Fabric and Power BI. The solution leverages Azure-native services for data integration, transformation, and governance, providing a scalable and secure analytics platform aligned with NL Hydro’s enterprise requirements.

Proposed Team

CGI will provide a dedicated, integrated delivery team with clearly defined roles and responsibilities to support the successful implementation, training, and ongoing support of the proposed reporting and data analytics solution.

The engagement will be locally led by Kevin Oram, who will serve as the Account Manager, Project Manager, and overall Engagement Lead, ensuring continuous local accountability and alignment with NL Hydro stakeholders.

In this role, Kevin is responsible for overall delivery governance, including scope, schedule, budget, and risk management, as well as acting as the primary point of contact and escalation for NL Hydro. All delivery activities, whether performed locally or by distributed team members, are coordinated and governed through this local leadership model.

While the broader delivery team includes specialized resources across Atlantic Canada and Québec, all work is directed, coordinated, and quality-controlled through Kevin’s local leadership, ensuring consistent communication, responsiveness, and alignment with NL Hydro’s operational needs.

Kevin brings over 15 years of experience in digital transformation, consulting delivery, and operational leadership across healthcare, energy, utilities, and public sector organizations. He has specific experience working with NL Power and government stakeholders, leading strategic discussions, shaping modernization and data/AI initiatives, and translating complex business needs into actionable solutions.

Based in St. John’s, NL, Kevin provides on-the-ground leadership, stakeholder engagement, and delivery oversight, ensuring that NL Hydro benefits from both local presence and the depth of CGI’s broader technical capabilities.
Solution and Technical Delivery

The solution design and technical delivery will be led by Ahmed Baha Eddine Ezzina, Solution Tech Lead, who will help define the overall data and analytics architecture, including integration with JDE EnterpriseOne, data modeling, security, and alignment with NL Hydro’s enterprise standards. Ahmed is a Senior Business Intelligence Consultant with 7 years of experience, PL-300, DP-600 and DP-700 certified).
The delivery team will be supported by key technical roles responsible for ensuring a scalable, secure, and well-governed data platform:

Data Architect – Responsible for the overall data architecture, including design of the data platform, integration patterns, data modeling standards, and alignment with NL Hydro’s enterprise architecture. The Data Architect ensures consistency across environments and establishes best practices for data governance, performance, and scalability.

Data Engineer – Responsible for building and maintaining data pipelines, ingestion processes, and transformation logic. This includes integrating data from JDE EnterpriseOne and other source systems, implementing ELT processes, and ensuring data quality, reliability, and performance within the data platform.

DevOps Engineer – Responsible for implementing and managing CI/CD pipelines, environment configuration, and deployment automation. This includes promotion of artifacts across development, test, and production environments, as well as ensuring version control, release governance, and repeatable deployments

The core technical team will include 5 Power BI and integration developers responsible for data integration, transformation, and report development, a data analyst supporting requirements definition, validation, and business insight development, and a dedicated JDE specialist providing subject matter expertise on JDE data structures and integration patterns.

The team will also support system integration testing, user acceptance testing, and data validation activities to ensure solution quality, accuracy, and alignment with business requirements. Collectively, the team brings extensive experience in enterprise data platforms, Azure-based analytics solutions, and business intelligence delivery, ensuring a scalable, and high-performing implementation.
Power BI Developers

For the RFP, CGI will provide a team of qualified Power BI Developers responsible for report migration, performance optimization, training, and ongoing support. Based on the anticipated scope, CGI estimates that 6 developers will be required, depending on workload progression throughout the project.
The BI Development Team will be structured as follows:
Senior Power BI Developers (PL300 certified and with a minimum of 5 years of experience).
They will handle high priority and complex reports, ensure quality across deliverables, and provide guidance and coaching to the rest of the team.
2 Intermediate Power BI Developers (PL300 certified or with at least 3 years of experience).
They will be responsible for most report migrations, working through the backlog established by the Project Manager and business stakeholders.
2 Junior Power BI Developers (PL300 certification considered an asset).
They will focus on migrating less complex reports and supporting the team with data validation, testing, and documentation tasks.
By the end of the project, we estimated that 2 Intermediate Power BI Developers will remain to ensure the trainings to all users and the Support of the platform.
Training, Adoption, and Support

Training, adoption, and knowledge transfer will be supported by a Power BI Developer and the Organizational Change Manager, Sarah Morris. They will work closely with NL Hydro stakeholders to facilitate user onboarding, develop training materials, and support the transition from legacy reporting tools to the new platform.

Sarah Morris, Senior Change Manager, brings 29 years of experience delivering large-scale transformation initiatives across government and public sector organizations. She has led change for complex modernization programs, including the Province of Nova Scotia’s SAP S/4HANA transformation and digital service modernization initiatives. She will lead the development and execution of the change management strategy, including communications, training, and readiness activities, ensuring a smooth transition and strong user adoption across NL Hydro.

Following implementation, CGI will provide ongoing support and maintenance through its established managed services model, including incident management, system optimization, and enhancements. Support services will leverage both regional resources and CGI’s broader organizational expertise to ensure timely resolution and continuous improvement of the solution.
Delivery Model and Resource Approach

CGI’s delivery model is designed to balance local presence with access to specialized expertise. Account leadership and project management will be anchored in Newfoundland and Labrador to ensure close collaboration, responsiveness, and alignment with NL Hydro stakeholders, while technical resources will be delivered through a blended model across Atlantic Canada and Québec.

Project Management and Implementation Plan
Project Implementation Approach
Describe the typical approach to implementing a reporting and data analytics solution. Include in the proposal:

CGI applies a structured, agile, domain-based delivery approach to implementing reporting and data analytics solutions, designed to deliver incremental business value while establishing a secure, scalable, and enterprise-grade data platform. This approach enables NL Hydro to realize early insights while progressively building out a dynamic end-to-end analytics capability.

The implementation model separates key architectural layers, including data ingestion, staging, transformation, semantic modeling, and consumption. Data ingestion is facilitated through Azure Data Factory (ADF) with a Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR), enabling secure connectivity to on-premises systems such as JDE/Db2 for ibm via outbound HTTPS only, eliminating the need for inbound firewall changes. Data is staged in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 (ADLS Gen2), leveraging partitioning, columnar storage formats, and optimized file management strategies to ensure performance and cost efficiency.

Transformation and enterprise data modeling are implemented within the data warehouse layer using Azure SQL Database or Azure Synapse Analytics Dedicated SQL Pool, depending on data volume and concurrency requirements. The semantic layer is delivered using Tabular models (Azure Analysis Services, SQL Server Analysis Services, or Power BI datasets), supporting both Import and Direct Query modes based on latency and reporting needs. Data consumption is enabled through Power BI, supported by the On-Premises Data Gateway for secure data refresh and access.
CGI’s implementation approach is executed through the following structured phases:

Initiate and Mobilize: Establish robust governance structures anchored by a predictable cadence, including weekly operational syncs, bi-weekly technical design reviews, and monthly Executive Steering Committee meetings. We will define clear roles and responsibilities (RASCI) across the blended CGI and NL Hydro teams. To ensure absolute transparency, traceability, and agile execution, we will deploy industry-standard ALM and collaboration tools - leveraging Azure DevOps (or Jira) for backlog seeding, sprint planning, and CI/CD pipeline management, alongside centralized knowledge bases (e.g., Confluence/SharePoint). During this phase, we rapidly confirm environment readiness, network access, and strict data security requirements.

Discover and Design: Validate scope, define key performance indicators (KPIs), develop JDE data mappings, establish data contracts, and confirm naming conventions and security models. Crucially, our Atlantic Canadian based Change Management Lead will begin stakeholder impact assessments during this phase to inform early user-adoption strategies.

Platform Build: Provision and configure core platform components, including ADF, SHIR, ADLS Gen2, data warehouse, and Power BI Gateway, across development, test, and production environments, utilizing Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) and Azure DevOps pipelines for secure, automated deployments.
Ingestion and ELT (Wave-Based): Develop and automate data pipelines, implement ELT processes including slowly changing dimensions (SCD), and apply validation and data quality rules.
Semantic Modeling: Design dimensional models (star/snowflake schemas), develop Tabular models, and implement role-based and object-level security (RLS/OLS), delivering certified datasets.

Testing: Execute system integration testing (SIT), user acceptance testing (UAT), and performance and security validation to ensure solution quality and reliability. This includes specific performance testing on the data extraction pipelines to guarantee zero disruption to NL Hydro’s live JDE EnterpriseOne environment.
Change, Training, and Adoption: Deliver training materials, business playbooks, and administrative runbooks, ensuring effective knowledge transfer and user enablement.

Cutover and Hypercare: Execute production deployment, enable operational processes, and provide a structured hypercare period to stabilize the solution before transitioning to steady-state operations. Our NL-based team will facilitate immediate, on-the-ground communication and user support, while our dedicated technical engine ensures rapid resolution of any backend data pipeline anomalies.

Proposed Solution – Microsoft Fabric End‑to‑End Analytics Platform
The following diagram illustrates the logical architecture for the proposed solution, including ingestion, transformation, storage, and reporting within a unified Microsoft Fabric environment.
Data flows from source systems through Fabric Lakehouse layers (Bronze, Silver, Gold), where it is transformed, standardized, and curated before being consumed through Power BI.

The platform unifies data ingestion, transformation, storage, modeling, and reporting into a single managed environment. This reduces operational complexity while improving performance, governance, and scalability.

Data from JD Edwards and other enterprise systems is ingested through Fabric pipelines using secure gateway connectivity. These pipelines support both scheduled and on-demand data movement, along with monitoring and error handling.
All data is stored within Fabric Lakehouses using Delta Lake format, providing a governed foundation with built-in support for schema management, lineage tracking, and transactional integrity.

Data transformation is performed using a combination of dataflows, SQL-based processing, and scalable compute. Business rules are applied consistently, and datasets are standardized across domains to ensure a single version of the truth.

Curated datasets are exposed through semantic models optimized for reporting and analytics. These models support large-scale data volumes and enable high-performance querying using Direct Lake technology.
Power BI provides a seamless reporting experience, enabling users to:
Access interactive dashboards
Perform ad hoc analysis
Use certified datasets
Receive automated reports and alerts

Security and governance are centrally managed through Microsoft Entra ID and Fabric’s native controls. This includes role-based access, row-level security, sensitivity labeling, and full audit logging. JDE security roles are mapped to the analytics layer to ensure consistent data access across systems.
The platform supports full development, testing, and production environments, enabling controlled deployment and validation of reporting assets through structured promotion processes.
Solution Capabilities and Alignment to Requirements
The proposed solution directly supports the requirements outlined in Appendix E.

It enables querying and reporting across multiple data sources, including JD Edwards, SQL Server, DB2, and other enterprise systems. Data is integrated into governed models that support both simple and complex queries without requiring users to understand underlying database structures.

Users can perform both scheduled and ad hoc analysis, with support for filtering, parameterization, and reusable queries. Reports can be exported in multiple formats, including Excel and PDF, and can be distributed automatically or accessed on demand.
The platform supports large-scale datasets and high user concurrency through optimized data models and scalable cloud infrastructure.
Security is enforced consistently across all layers of the solution through single sign-on, role-based access, and alignment with JDE security. All activity is logged and auditable.

The user experience is designed to support self-service analytics through intuitive interfaces, business-friendly terminology, and guided filtering. The platform supports accessibility standards and operates across modern browsers, Windows environments, and Citrix deployments.
Optional Deployment Model (Alternative Architecture)

While CGI recommends Microsoft Fabric as the primary solution, an alternative Azure-based implementation can be provided to align with specific enterprise standards or preferences. This approach leverages Azure Data Factory, Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, Azure SQL/Synapse, and Power BI to deliver equivalent functional capabilities within a modular architecture.
The following diagram illustrates the logical architecture for the Azure-based deployment model, including data ingestion, transformation, and reporting layers.:
Figure 2: Optional Deployment Model - Reporting and Data Analytics Architecture (ADF + Azure SQL + Power BI)

In this model, data is sourced from JD Edwards, on-premises databases, cloud systems, and existing Showcase extracts. Secure connectivity is established through the On-Premises Data Gateway or virtual network integration, ensuring encrypted data movement without exposing internal systems.

Azure Data Factory orchestrates data ingestion using scheduled or event-driven pipelines. It supports incremental data loads, change data capture, monitoring, and retry logic, ensuring reliable and auditable data movement across all environments.

Raw data is stored in Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2, preserving source data in its original state with full lineage and auditability. Data is then transformed into standardized, business-ready datasets through governed ELT processes. These transformations apply data quality rules, harmonize JDE structures such as company and business unit codes, and integrate data across multiple sources. Cross-system joins and derived calculations are performed at this stage to ensure consistency and performance.

Curated data models are created using dimensional modeling techniques and exposed through a consistent semantic layer for reporting. Separate development, test, and production environments support controlled promotion of data pipelines, models, and reports using structured deployment pipelines.

Power BI serves as the reporting interface, enabling interactive dashboards, paginated reports, and ad hoc analysis. Users can leverage drill-down, filtering, and parameterization capabilities, with reports securely shared across the organization and distributed through automated scheduling and subscriptions.

Security is enforced through Microsoft Entra ID integration and alignment with JDE security roles. Access is controlled using role-based access, row-level security, and object-level security, ensuring users only access data consistent with their permissions in source systems.

This alternative provides a high degree of control over individual services and may align with organizations that prefer a discrete Azure service model. However, compared to the unified Microsoft Fabric platform, it introduces additional operational complexity across multiple services and management layers.

CGI’s proposed solution provides NL Hydro with a single, modern, and fully governed analytics platform that replaces legacy reporting tools and establishes a scalable foundation for future growth.
By leveraging Microsoft Fabric and Power BI, the solution simplifies architecture, reduces operational overhead, and enables faster access to trusted data.
This approach minimizes risk, improves usability, and delivers a cost-effective platform aligned with NL Hydro’s long-term strategic objectives.

45,"Summarize your cybersecurity program and framework (policies, governance, roles, training, etc.)",H,,"CGI maintains a comprehensive, enterprise-wide Information Security Program aligned to globally recognized standards, including ISO 27001, ISO 27701, ISO 27017, ISO 27018, and the NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF and 800-53). Governance is centrally managed through formal policies, standards, and procedures, with oversight provided by CGI’s executive leadership and Audit Committee of the Board of Directors. Controls are subject to both internal and external audit validation.
Governance and Framework

CGI’s Enterprise Security Management Framework (ESMF) and Data Privacy Policy define the baseline security requirements across all services, including cloud and data platforms. These frameworks incorporate regulatory and industry standards such as COBIT, NIS2, GDPR, AI Act, and DORA, and are applied consistently across CGI’s global operations, subsidiaries, and subcontractors.
Security Integration and Risk Management

Security and privacy are embedded into CGI’s day-to-day operations and delivery practices. Controls are implemented through standardized processes and are enhanced where required using a risk-based approach that considers the sensitivity, scope, and regulatory requirements of the data being processed. Where CGI acts as a data processor, additional safeguards may be implemented to align with client-specific requirements.
Training and Awareness
All CGI personnel are required to complete mandatory annual cybersecurity and data privacy training, ensuring ongoing awareness and adherence to security best practices.
Maturity and Compliance

CGI operates at a Tier 4 (Adaptive) maturity level under the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, reflecting a highly mature and continuously improving security posture. CGI complies with applicable global and Canadian data privacy regulations and enforces strict data residency controls, ensuring that any cross-border data processing occurs only with explicit client authorization.
This comprehensive and proven program ensures that NL Hydro benefits from a secure, compliant, and low-risk operating environment, with consistent application of controls and continuous monitoring."

46,Describe your vetting process for staff and contractor onboarding as it relates to background and security checks.,H,,"CGI applies a formal and risk-based vetting process for all employees, contractors, and subcontractors prior to granting access to systems or data.
Background Verification
Background checks are conducted in accordance with role requirements and applicable legislation and may include:
Identity verification
Employment history validation (typically minimum 5 years)
Education verification
Criminal record checks
Global sanctions and politically exposed person (PEP) screening
Credit checks and government clearances (where applicable)
Onboarding Process
The onboarding process includes:
Pre-screening during recruitment
Technical and managerial interviews
Third-party background verification through approved providers
Access Control Alignment
Access to systems is granted only after successful completion of all required checks and is aligned with role-based security controls.
This approach ensures that all personnel supporting NL Hydro are appropriately vetted, compliant, and aligned with CGI’s security standards, significantly reducing insider risk."

ISO 27001 (Information Security Management)
ISO 27701 (Privacy Information Management)

48,"Describe your vulnerability management and patching processes and typical timelines, including zero-day vulnerability mitigation.",H,,"CGI maintains a comprehensive vulnerability and patch management program supported by its Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), which provides 24×7 monitoring, threat detection, and response.
Continuous Monitoring and Threat Detection
The GSOC continuously monitors networks and systems, performing proactive testing and vulnerability assessments to identify and mitigate emerging threats.
Layered Security Controls
Protection mechanisms include:
Anti-malware and endpoint protection solutions
Web content filtering
Email security (anti-phishing, spam filtering, advanced threat protection)
Network and host-based intrusion detection/prevention systems
Patch Management Process
Regular patch cycles (typically monthly or aligned to risk severity)
Vendor patch validation and deployment through controlled change management
Prioritization based on vulnerability criticality
Zero-Day Response
For critical or zero-day vulnerabilities:
Rapid risk assessment is conducted
Emergency patching or mitigation measures are deployed
Alignment with vendor advisories ensures timely remediation
Secure Configuration and Development
Systems are built using secure baseline configurations
Vulnerability scanning and penetration testing are performed regularly
Secure development practices include static/dynamic code analysis and environment segregation
This layered and proactive approach ensures continuous protection, rapid remediation, and reduced exposure to security threats."

49,Describe your Incident Response plan/process maturity and commitment to client incident notification.,H,,"CGI operates a formal, enterprise-wide Incident Response Program designed to ensure rapid detection, containment, and resolution of security incidents.
Incident Management Framework
Incidents are managed through CGI’s Incident Management Centre (IMC) and supported by the Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), providing 24×7 monitoring and response capabilities.
Incident Lifecycle
The process includes:
Detection and classification by severity
Escalation to appropriate technical and executive stakeholders
Containment, eradication, and recovery actions
Root cause analysis and post-incident reporting
Governance and Coordination
Incident response teams include representatives from:
Global Security
Privacy (Data Protection Officers)
Legal, HR, and Communications
All incident communications are centrally coordinated to ensure accuracy and compliance.
Client Notification
CGI provides timely notification to clients in accordance with contractual and regulatory requirements, including:
Ongoing status updates during incidents
Formal post-incident reports
Documentation to support regulatory reporting obligations
Testing and Continuous Improvement
Incident response processes are regularly tested through simulation exercises, and lessons learned are incorporated into continuous improvement initiatives.
Business Continuity Integration
Business continuity and disaster recovery plans are integrated into the incident response framework, ensuring rapid restoration of services and minimal operational disruption.
This mature and well-governed approach ensures rapid response, transparency, and minimized impact to NL Hydro operations."

Securing Newfoundland & Labrador’s Energy Future

As the custodian of the province’s critical energy infrastructure, Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro carries a mandate that requires an exceptionally high standard of vigilance. In a landscape where utility providers are increasingly targeted by sophisticated actors, "standard" monitoring is no longer sufficient. Security must be proactive, sovereign, and deeply integrated into your operational reality.

CGI submits this proposal for Managed Extended Detection and Response (MxDR) services with a singular goal: to provide Hydro with a sovereign, Canadian-delivered security capability that evolves as fast as the threats against it.
A Partnership Driven by Strategic Advisory

Technology alone does not guarantee resilience; leadership and collaboration does. While our operational mandate is to provide 24/7 monitoring and rapid containment, an added value within CGI’s proposal is the Strategic Advisory Model we have built around Hydro’s leadership team.

We are positioning Krishna Raj Kumar, based in Atlantic Canada, and Subin Alexander, our National Director of Security Service Delivery, as your primary strategic advisors. This dual-leadership model ensures Hydro is not simply purchasing a static service but engaging a dynamic defense partner.

Beyond Operations: While ensuring operational excellence, Krishna and Subin will look beyond the daily alerts to identify emerging industry trends and utility-specific threat vectors before they impact your grid.

Continuous Evolution: Security is not a "set and forget" discipline. Through structured quarterly strategy sessions, this leadership team will proactively recommend optimizations to detection strategies and response playbooks, ensuring your defenses mature in lockstep with your digital transformation.

Trusted Guidance: Acting as extensions of your team, they will provide the foresight needed to navigate regulatory changes and shift from a reactive security posture to a proactive state of readiness.
Sovereign Delivery, Global Intelligence

Canadian Sovereignty: All data monitoring, processing, and storage will occur exclusively within Canada, utilizing our Protected-B certified Security Operations Centre (SOC) in Gatineau and data centers in Montreal and Mississauga. A Low-Risk Transition to Resilience

By selecting CGI, Newfoundland and Labrador Hydro is choosing a partner that is invested in the community you serve. We offer not just a contract for detection and response, but a commitment to the long-term safety, reliability, and resilience of the province’s infrastructure.

Describe the onboarding process for new customers, including the level of effort required from NL Hydro’s internal team and any dependencies on internal resources, such as testing, configuration, or integration, to ensure successful implementation of MxDR services.

The MxDR (Managed Extended Detection & Response) onboarding process provides NL Hydro with a structured and efficient transition into fully managed SOC operations. The onboarding framework ensures rapid deployment, seamless integration with NL Hydro’s security environment, and a clear operational model that accelerates time-to-value while structuring and managing internal effort in a predictable and controlled manner. Total anticipated customer effort typically ranges from 196 to 250 hours depending on scope and environment complexity.
By the end of the onboarding program, NL Hydro achieves:
Full 24/7 monitoring and incident response coverage
Validated telemetry and detection capabilities
A complete escalation and communication model with the SOC
Customized use cases aligned to business and compliance needs
A continuous improvement cycle for ongoing optimization
The process is executed through a series of defined phases:
Readiness
Governance setup
Technical Integration
Use-case onboarding
Validation, and
Go-live.

Each phase is designed to progressively establish monitoring capabilities, align security operations with NL Hydro’s business requirements, and ensure the SOC can deliver high-quality detection and incident response from day one.

A key component of this onboarding model is shared responsibility. CGI’s MxDR team leads all strategic planning, configuration, testing, and operational setup. The client’s internal effort is primarily focused on approvals, providing access, installing agents, and participating in limited tuning and validation sessions. Total anticipated customer effort typically ranges from 196 to 250 hours distributed across architecture reviews, system configuration, log source onboarding, and testing activities.

The onboarding framework also identifies internal dependencies for successful implementation, including support from the NL Hydro Security Manager, Network and Identity teams, Endpoint Management, Cloud Administrators, and Governance personnel. These roles ensure the proper integration of identity systems, endpoint agents, network telemetry, SIEM/XDR technologies, and incident response workflows.

This structured onboarding approach ensures a smooth transition to managed SOC operations, reduces security risk early, and equips customers with a mature, fully integrated MxDR service model that supports long-term operational resilience.

By validating prerequisites early and confirming the environment’s readiness, the client minimizes delays, reduces risk during implementation, and accelerates time-to-value.
This phase focuses on three core objectives:
Validating client prerequisites to ensure the environment, tools, and access requirements are fully in place.
Establishing program governance to clarify roles, responsibilities, and communication paths from the outset.
Confirming technical scope and deployment readiness, which provides a clear, accurate plan for technology integration and SOC activation.

This phase establishes the operational foundation necessary for effective collaboration between NL Hydro and the transition team. Establish operational relationships that support day-to-day security operations and escalation requirements.

The Technical Integration & Deployment phase is where the core security technologies are connected, configured, and enabled to support MxDR operations. This phase delivers significant value to NL Hydro by establishing the technical backbone that powers threat detection, monitoring, and incident response. Through a structured and validated deployment approach, the environment becomes fully instrumented, ensuring continuous telemetry flow and enabling the SOC to operate with speed and accuracy.

Deploy agents across the required endpoints and systems to provide visibility.

This stage ensures NL Hydro’s environment is properly prepared and technically aligned with the MxDR platform, reducing onboarding delays and accelerating the transition to full SOC coverage.

Align detection logic to NL Hydro’s systems, applications, and threat landscape.

Historic Data and Log Migration Planning

As part of the onboarding process, the proponent must work with NL Hydro to assess and plan for the secure migration and/or retention of relevant historical security data from the incumbent MxDR vendor. The proponent must outline their approach to integrating legacy data into their platform and identify any limitations or risks associated with data migration and propose mitigation strategies.
As part of onboarding, CGI will work with NL Hydro to assess, plan, and execute the secure migration and/or retention of relevant historical security data from the incumbent MxDR vendor.
CGI proposes a scalable log management model that balances operational visibility with long-term compliance requirements. The solution combines:
Approximately 45 days of live searchable data in Elasticsearch
Up to one year of archived logs stored in secure object storage (e.g., S3 or Glacier tiers if selected)
On-demand historical re-ingestion for investigative needs
This hybrid hot storage plus archive model aligns with established MSS industry practices and ensures rapid investigative capability while maintaining audit-ready retention.
Our Approach to Assessing & Planning Secure Migration/Retention
Data Profiling (Prerequisite to Planning)
Objective: Establish authoritative specifications for legacy data before committing timelines, resources, or costs.
Activities (sample-driven):

Format & Schema Profiling: Enumerate log sources, schemas, field types, and compression/encryption methods; catalog timestamp patterns and time zones; assess schema consistency and parsing requirements.
Volume & Variability Analysis: Measure daily volumes, peak/burst behavior, and retention ranges to inform capacity and SLA design.
Data Quality Assessment: Identify duplication, corruption signatures, incomplete records, and fidelity constraints impacting investigative use.
Compliance & Residency Mapping: Confirm regulatory retention periods, legal holds, data residency, and privacy handling requirements.
Deliverable: Data Profiling Report detailing source catalog, schema/format map, volume and quality characteristics, compliance/residency needs, and recommended target parsers/mappings.
The Data Profiling Report is the basis for precise migration timelines, compute/storage estimates, rehydration SLAs, and cost controls.
Migration Activities (Time-Bound)
Scope: Secure transfer of historical logs from the incumbent MxDR vendor and NL Hydro’s existing S3 archives (1–2 TB).
Steps:
Export & Access Enablement: Coordinate secure exports or API retrieval; obtain source schemas/metadata and retention details; validate export throttles/limits.
Encrypted Transfer: Move data via approved channels (API, secure download, or bulk file transfer). Enforce encryption in transit and at rest.
Intake Validation: Perform hash/checksum verification, object counts, integrity checks, and chain-of-custody logging on receipt.
Pilot Ingestion (Representative Window): Run test migrations to validate parsing, field alignment, timestamp normalization, deduplication, and indexing performance.
Reconciliation & Sign-off: Issue reconciliation reports (record counts, errors/exceptions, successfully processed ranges). Address exceptions via defined queues and retries.
Phased Migration: Execute in controlled batches with change controls and rollback criteria. Maintain RBAC-restricted access and audit logging throughout.
Cutover: Confirm operational readiness, retire temporary pipelines, and transition to steady-state runbooks.

Incumbent Vendor Responsibilities: Provide secure, timely, and complete exports/metadata; support bulk/API retrieval; share schemas and retention details; maintain service stability during transition; assist with verification and decommissioning.
Steady-State Retention Architecture (Ongoing Operations)
Objective: Provide predictable, cost-controlled access to current and historical logs with audit-ready retrieval.
Live Searchable Data (0–45 days): Indexed in Elasticsearch (hot/warm tiers) for detections, dashboards, and investigations. Window is adjustable based on volume and cost targets.

Long-Term Archive (45 days–1 year): Stored in secure object storage (e.g., S3 or Glacier tiers). Archives include integrity controls (hashing) and optional immutability (object lock/WORM). Not continuously indexed.
On-Demand Rehydration: Retrieve specified time ranges from archive and temporarily re-index into Elasticsearch (typical visibility window: 7–14 days), then expire to control cost and cluster load.
Service Management: Formal request workflow for archive retrieval and rehydration, with defined SLAs aligned to storage class (e.g., near-immediate for S3 Standard; 12–48+ hours for Glacier tiers).
Controls & Governance: RBAC, least privilege, encryption at rest/in transit, audit logging, cost guardrails, and lifecycle policies documented in operational runbooks.
Legacy Data Integration (Dedicated)
Purpose: Ensure legacy logs are correctly parsed, normalized, searchable, and distinguishable from live data.
Schema Mapping & Field Alignment
Align legacy fields to the platform’s target/common event schema.
Maintain a source-to-target field map per log type; preserve investigative context (hostnames, usernames, asset identifiers, source types).
Manage versioning of parsers/mappings with change control, document deviations and compensating logic.
Timestamp Normalization
Normalize timestamps with explicit time zone handling and clock-skew correction where feasible.
Standardize time fields (e.g., @timestamp), preserving original fields for traceability.
Ensure cross-source temporal consistency to support correlation and timelines.
Parsing, Quality, and Deduplication
Implement resilient parsers with graceful error handling, route malformed records to an exception queue for review.
Detect and remove duplicates using record keys/hashes, record deduplication metrics in reconciliation reports.
Apply compression/decompression handling per profile (e.g., GZIP, ZIP) defined during profiling.
Tagging of Rehydrated Records
Apply explicit tags to all rehydrated events (e.g., rehydrated:true, source:archive, rehydration_window_id, rehydration_requested_by).
Maintain lineage metadata (ingest time, source bucket/path, checksum references) to support audit and investigations.
Search Behavior & User Experience
Rehydrated data appears alongside live data and is fully searchable during the configured window.
Default dashboards/detections remain intact; provide saved filters to include/exclude rehydrated:true.
Document performance expectations for broad historical queries and provide recommended query patterns/time-range filters.
Handling NL Hydro’s Existing 1–2 TB (S3)
Option A (Default): Validate and load to the archive with hashing and reconciliation; rehydrate on demand.
Option B (Partial Immediate Load): Ingest a recent slice (e.g., last 30–45 days) into Elasticsearch; keep remainder in archive.
Option C (Retain in Place): Maintain in current S3 location with documented access paths and retrieval procedures.
Final choice confirmed post-profiling to align operational needs, SLAs, and cost constraints.
Identification of Risks & Limitations
Export and Access Constraints: Vendor/API throttles, export limits, or fees impacting throughput and scheduling.
Archive Retrieval Latency: Glacier and deep archive classes may impose 12–48+ hour retrieval windows.
Volume Bursts and Index Load: High daily peaks or large rehydration requests can affect indexing/search performance.
Data Quality Constraints: Duplicates, corruption, partial records, or schema drift affecting parsing and fidelity.
Timezone and Clock Skew: Inconsistent or missing time zone data complicating correlation.
Residency/Privacy Controls: Jurisdictional requirements for storage/processing and PII handling.
Cost Variability: Egress, retrieval tier selection, and unplanned large rehydrations increasing spend if unmanaged.
Investigative Fidelity for Older Logs: Legacy data may lack context or depth required for modern detections.
Mitigation Strategies
Profile-Then-Plan: Use the Data Profiling Report to finalize timelines, compute/storage sizing, parsers, and rehydration SLAs before execution.
Pilot First: Validate mappings, normalization, performance, and dashboards with a representative historical window; adjust parsers and capacity based on results.
Technical Controls (Mandatory):
Encryption: In transit and at rest across transfer, archive, and indexing tiers.
Hash/Checksum Validation: Source and post-transfer verification with reconciliation reports.
Test Migrations: Sample-based test runs prior to bulk migration; defined rollback criteria.
Reconciliation Reports: Counts, integrity checks, exceptions, and deduplication metrics per batch.
Audit & Chain-of-Custody: Full event and file lineage logging; restricted RBAC with least privilege.
Capacity & Guardrails: Right-size hot/warm tiers; throttle/queue rehydration; schedule large jobs off-peak; place approval workflows and budget alerts on archive retrievals.
Schema & Parser Adaptability: Maintain source-specific parsing rules and versioned mappings; document exceptions with compensating transformations.
Residency & Privacy Compliance: Store/process within approved jurisdictions; apply data masking where required; maintain evidence of control effectiveness.
Operational SLAs: Publish storage-class-specific retrieval SLAs; communicate expected timelines for S3 vs. Glacier; set user expectations for large historical queries.
Outcome for NL Hydro
Upon completion, NL Hydro will have:
A validated retention and access model: ~0–45 days live searchable in Elasticsearch; 45 days–1 year in secure archive with on-demand, time-bounded rehydration.
Fully integrated legacy data with documented schema mappings, normalized timestamps, field alignment, deduplication, and explicit tagging for rehydrated events.
Operational runbooks and SLAs covering migration, archive retrieval, rehydration, exception handling, and cost guardrails.
Assurance artifacts: encryption evidence, hash/check reconciliation reports, audit/lineage logs, and test migration results.
A repeatable, compliant process for accessing historical logs post-cutover with predictable performance and cost controls.

Integration Examples from Prior Engagements
CGI has successfully implemented unified XDR patterns across multiple client environments, including:

Phishing-to-Endpoint Correlation: Integration of Defender for Office 365 and Defender for Endpoint to automatically correlate malicious email delivery with endpoint execution events, triggering automated containment actions such as endpoint isolation and account risk elevation.

Identity-Driven Threat Prioritization: Use of Defender for Identity signals to enrich endpoint and cloud alerts, prioritizing incidents involving privileged or high-risk identities and dynamically adjusting incident severity within the SOC workflow.

Cloud and SaaS Visibility Expansion: Integration of Defender for Cloud Apps with endpoint and identity telemetry to detect abnormal access patterns, risky OAuth applications, and data exfiltration attempts across sanctioned and unsanctioned SaaS platforms.

Hybrid Infrastructure Coverage: Correlation of on-premises identity events with cloud and endpoint signals, enabling consistent detection and response across hybrid environments without introducing parallel tooling.

This unified approach enables cross-domain correlation, allowing the SOC to detect complex attack chains that span multiple control layers—such as credential compromise originating from phishing, lateral movement via endpoints, and data exfiltration through cloud applications.

Methodology for Continuous Improvement

The proponent will describe their methodology for continuous improvement, including how they perform ongoing tuning, detection rule optimization, and adapt to emerging threats to maintain service effectiveness.

CGI applies a formal and operationally embedded Continuous Service Improvement methodology to ensure that NL Hydro’s Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service remains effective and aligned with the evolving threat landscape. Continuous improvement is integrated into daily SOC operations and structured detection engineering practices, with monitoring enhancements aligned to NL Hydro’s operational priorities and risk tolerance.

Adaptation to emerging threats is driven through CGI’s integrated global threat intelligence feeds into SIEM and structured threat hunting. CGI leverages its integrated global Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP), which aggregates indicators of compromise, adversary tactics, and emerging threat insights contributed by CGI’s nine SOCs worldwide. This centralized intelligence feed is continuously operationalized into the SIEM, enabling timely updates to detection logic, correlation rules, and monitoring use cases. Intelligence insights are translated into actionable detection enhancements and response playbook refinements to ensure monitoring capabilities evolve in line with emerging threats. Threat hunting activities are conducted to proactively identify anomalous behavior and uncover monitoring gaps, with findings feeding directly into detection enhancements.

Ongoing tuning and detection optimization are managed through a structured detection engineering lifecycle. Each detection use case is developed with defined objectives, mapped to adversary behaviors using frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, and supported by validated telemetry sources. CGI continuously evaluates alert volumes, false positive rates, escalation quality, and detection performance metrics. When incidents occur or anomalous trends are identified, root cause analysis is performed to determine whether refinements are required to correlation logic, thresholds, enrichment processes, or response procedures.

Detection effectiveness is further maintained through periodic performance and coverage reviews, including analysis of incident trends, missed detections, and telemetry completeness. CGI performs tuning adjustments, use case modifications, and suppression logic changes to minimize false positives and improve monitoring effectiveness. These refinements are tailored to NL Hydro’s environment and operational patterns. Where business context is required to distinguish legitimate from suspicious activity, CGI engages NL Hydro to validate observed traffic to ensure tuning decisions maintain detection integrity while reducing noise. Recommendations for additional data sources, configuration adjustments, or workflow improvements are incorporated into ongoing monitoring enhancements to sustain service effectiveness over time.

Automation and workflow optimization are implemented where appropriate within the SOAR platform or directly within endpoint security tools to enhance detection response efficiency and consistency. These automations are designed to support ongoing service effectiveness by reducing manual effort, accelerating containment actions, and improving response timelines. Examples include automated host isolation or file quarantine actions triggered through the endpoint agent when high-confidence malicious activity is detected. Workflow automations may also include enrichment steps such as threat intelligence lookups or asset context retrieval to improve alert quality and investigative speed. All automation use cases are validated prior to deployment to ensure they strengthen detection and response outcomes without introducing operational risk.

As part of the proposed Elastic SIEM platform, CGI leverages machine learning capabilities to support continuous improvement. Elastic’s behavioral analytics rely on normalized and enriched data to establish activity baselines across users, hosts, and network traffic, enabling detection of anomalies not captured by static rules. Machine learning outputs are regularly reviewed and tuned by CGI analysts to reduce noise and enhance detection fidelity within NL Hydro’s environment. Insights derived from behavioral analytics inform ongoing rule optimization, threat hunting, and use case development.

Through this structured, collaborative, and metrics-driven methodology, CGI ensures that NL Hydro’s MDR service continuously matures while maintaining strong governance, shared oversight, and alignment with organizational priorities.

Cyber Security Services – Optional Services
A – Risk Identification and Vulnerability Management

CGI employs a comprehensive and systematic strategy for risk identification and vulnerability management grounded in industry-standard frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, OWASP, and the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). The approach begins with a structured risk assessment process that includes discovery and requirements gathering to understand business context and current controls, followed by risk identification through control assessment and policy review.

For vulnerability management, CGI leverages a multi-vulnerability management, detection and response (VMDR) environment that scans internal and external environments to discover all assets including servers, workstations, applications, network devices, and middleware. The process includes creating detailed asset and software inventories integrated with CMDB, performing asset-level vulnerability scans and compliance checks, and conducting policy-alignment and CIS Benchmark customizations. Vulnerabilities are assessed based on CVSS scores and aligned with compliance frameworks such as NIST SP 800-30 or ISO 27001.

CGI follows a structured triage and prioritization process that categorizes vulnerabilities based on CVSS scores into Critical (≥9.0), High (7.0-8.9), Moderate (4.0-6.9), and Low (<4.0) levels. Risk levels are determined by combining severity ratings with factors such as exploitability, complexity, whether the vulnerability has been exploited in the wild, use in chained attacks, ability to mitigate, zero-day status, and impact on business, applications, systems, and users. CGI recommends fine-tuning the risk rating based on vulnerability type, such as newly added exploited vulnerabilities, increased attacks from threat actors, published zero-day vulnerabilities, and missing mitigation strategies.

D.1 – Penetration Testing

CGI can provide penetration testing services to help identify and validate security weaknesses across applications, infrastructure, cloud environments, and supporting technologies. CGI’s penetration testing approach combines automated tooling with expert-led manual testing to simulate real-world attack scenarios and assess the effectiveness of preventive and detective security controls. Testing activities are conducted using industry-recognized methodologies and standards, with scope, frequency, and testing depth defined collaboratively with the tenant. Findings are documented in clear, actionable reports that prioritize risk, outline potential business impact, and provide practical remediation recommendations. Penetration testing services may be delivered independently or used to complement SOC operations, threat detection, and security improvement initiatives, and are available on an on-demand or scheduled basis under separate commercial terms.
D.2 – Secure Code Review and Application Security Assessments (including in-house DevOps environments)

CGI can provide secure code review and application security assessment services to help identify and remediate security vulnerabilities across applications, APIs, and supporting systems. CGI’s approach combines automated static and dynamic analysis with expert-led manual testing to uncover both code-level weaknesses and runtime security issues, simulating real-world attack scenarios where applicable.
The testing activities will be conducted using industry-recognized methodologies and standards, with the scope, frequency, and depth of assessment defined collaboratively with the NL Hydro.

The CGI Secure Code Review (SAST) is designed to identify security weaknesses early in the development lifecycle, helping reduce remediation costs and promote secure coding practices. The assessment focuses on detecting vulnerabilities such as insecure coding practices, data flow issues, memory leaks, logic errors, input validation flaws, authentication and session management weaknesses, insecure direct object references, cryptographic issues, hardcoded secrets, and injection vulnerabilities.

The Application Security Assessment (DAST) complements this by evaluating the running application to identify runtime and server configuration issues. This includes detecting open redirects, information disclosure, input validation weaknesses, misconfigured security headers, API and component vulnerabilities, business logic flaws, injection attacks, and insecure file upload mechanisms. Together, SAST and DAST provide a comprehensive view of application security, addressing both code-level and runtime risks.

CGI employs a combination of automated and manual techniques to conduct comprehensive security assessments. Manual testing complements automated scans by helping to reduce false positives and validate findings more accurately. For SAST and DAST testing, CGI leverages a mix of open-source and commercially available tools, carefully configured to ensure assessments are safe and do not cause any disruption to the NL Hydro environment.

To align with industry best practices, CGI conducts all secure code review and application security assessments within the context of established security frameworks and standards, including OWASP Top 10, CWE/SANS Top 25, and NIST secure SDLC guidance. This structured approach ensures that remediation step is actionable and consistent with the NL Hydro overall risk management objectives.
D.3 – Cloud Security Assessments (IaaS, PaaS, SaaS)

CGI provides comprehensive security assessment capabilities across IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS cloud environments. CGI's approach includes reviewing traditional data center and cloud environments, with advisory services that can prepare a Cloud Security Framework to ensure organizations can safely procure and manage audits with their cloud providers.

CGI assesses the security postures of individual cloud services to maintain a secure cloud environment, leveraging expertise in managing Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) across multi-cloud and hybrid environments. The approach addresses challenges associated with regulatory compliance and cloud adoption, ensuring that cloud environments adhere to security best practices. CGI's security approach is tailored to ensuring protections across the full range of cloud solutions and products including SaaS, IaaS, and PaaS.

CGI's cloud security assessment methodology works across major cloud platforms and hybrid environments, with deep understanding of cloud architectures, APIs, security models, and compliance requirements of IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS offerings. The assessment process includes security posture assessment, compliance evaluation against industry regulations and organizational policies, and comprehensive assessment of vendor self-attestation. CGI provides ongoing, real-time insights into cloud application usage and risks, enabling proactive security and compliance management.
D.5 – Risk Analysis

CGI employs a comprehensive and structured methodology for cybersecurity risk analysis grounded in industry-standard frameworks such as NIST 800-61, NIST 800-53, NIST CSF, ISO/IEC 27001:2013, ISMS and ITSG-33.

The risk analysis process follows several key stages. First, risk identification is conducted through control assessment, policy review, and policy governance. Next, risk analysis and prioritization evaluates threat exposure, impact, and probability of occurrence. The process then moves to risk mitigation, which involves mapping risks with existing controls and developing remediation plans. Finally, we publish the risk assessment report and explain identified risks along with remediation plans.
CGI's risk assessment methodology includes the following specific steps:
Kick-off of the risk assessment,
Information gathering (reconnaissance),
Asset identification,
Assessment of threats and vulnerabilities,
Assessment of existing safeguards,
Assessment of residual risk,
Development of mitigating recommendations, and;
Production, submission and presentation of an assessment report.
D.6 – Security Architecture & Design Reviews

CGI offers comprehensive security architecture and design review services as part of its cybersecurity consulting capabilities. CGI partners with clients not only to design innovative security solutions but also to enhance the security of existing systems.

Our approach begins with a deep understanding of the client's environment including network and application components within the scope of assessment. The service then utilizes tools and methodologies such as threat modeling to prioritize minimizing risks and addressing potential threats to solutions. The process captures operational security capabilities across People, Processes, and Technology, resulting in industry-leading reference architecture. Additionally, CGI provides assurance for third-party offerings, guiding clients on how to best integrate them into their overall architecture.

Key features of the service include comprehensive security assessment to evaluate current security posture and identify vulnerabilities, as well as customized security frameworks tailored to specific business needs and regulatory requirements. CGI can review the overall network topology including placement of security devices globally and can review security configuration of operating systems and databases against defined minimum baseline security policies and industry best practices. CGI can also conduct workshops to understand current infrastructure and develop an Enterprise Security Architecture and Delivery Framework, with recommendations including a roadmap to migrate existing environments based on best practices.
D.7 – Identity & Access Management (IAM) Assessments

CGI provides comprehensive IAM assessment services to ensure strong alignment with particular business needs. The services include IAM strategy development, business cases, benchmarks, program and project planning, process redesign, governance procedures, audits, implementation of security policies, development of architecture, and functional and technical specifications development.

CGI's IAM assessment approach begins with business requirements and analysis through facilitated discussions to refine and confirm the strategic IAM vision and future requirements via workshops, stakeholder interviews, and document analysis of existing systems. This methodology delivers detailed business requirements documents, current state assessments, and a high-level target state architecture aligned with client objectives.

The assessment process addresses key challenges including lack of visibility in tracking user access and entitlements across different systems, manual provisioning processes that are inefficient and error-prone for user onboarding and offboarding, orphaned accounts creating security vulnerabilities, and inadequate controls over privileged accounts leading to potential insider threats. CGI leverages extensive hands-on experience with leading IAM and Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions to ensure a secure, centralized, and compliant system that meets operational and compliance requirements.

CGI has over 15 years of experience delivering IAM solutions for public sector, health, and insurance clients, covering Identity Governance, Privileged Access Management (PAM), Single Sign-On (SSO), and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA). The company delivers over 20 IAM-related projects annually across North America.
