ITEM,80123_105067_0,,A.,"Public Commitment

Has the Proponent (Board, CEO) made a public commitment to ESG initiatives? This could include reference to initiatives in the Proponents mission statement, vision, values, principles, code of conduct, etc. or it could be a stand-alone commitment statement.

",0,"CGI's Board and CEO have made a public commitment to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. This commitment is reflected in CGI's mission statement, vision, values, and principles, which emphasize the importance of being a responsible corporate citizen. CGI's business model is designed to ensure close engagement with clients and communities, highlighting their social responsibilities and contributions to the continuous development of the communities in which they operate.

Additionally, CGI remains a signatory to the United Nations (UN) Global Compact, which includes principles related to human rights and environmental sustainability. The company follows UN principles and global best practices in setting its ESG objectives and targets, which are cascaded into the plans of its business units.

CGI's commitment to ESG is further demonstrated through the publication of its ESG report, which outlines quantified targets and progress in various ESG initiatives. This report is shared transparently with stakeholders, showcasing CGI's dedication to integrating sustainability into its daily business practices.
Overall, CGI's leadership has made a clear and public commitment to ESG initiatives, reinforcing the organization's values and guiding principles.
*screenshot*"
ITEM,80123_105068_0,,B.,"ESG Standards, Certifications and Member Associations
Provide details of any current ESG relevant standards and certifications and/or memberships held.
",0,"CGI holds several current ESG-relevant standards, certifications, and memberships that reflect its commitment to sustainability and responsible business practices:

1. EcoVadis Certification: CGI has achieved the EcoVadis Platinum medal, placing it among the top 1% of companies globally for sustainability performance. This certification assesses companies based on international sustainability standards, including the Ten Principles of the UN Global Compact and the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) standards.
2. ISO Certifications: CGI has obtained various ISO certifications that demonstrate its commitment to quality, safety, and environmental performance. These include:
o ISO 9001: Quality management systems
o ISO 14001: Environmental management systems
o ISO 20000: Information technology service management
o ISO 22301: Business continuity management.

3. CDP Membership: CGI participates in the Carbon Disclosure Project (CDP), which supports companies in measuring and managing their environmental risks and opportunities. CGI received a score of B in 2023, indicating a strong commitment to environmental transparency.
4. UN Global Compact: CGI is a signatory to the UN Global Compact, which aligns its operations with universal principles on human rights, labor, environment, and anti-corruption.
5. Dow Jones Sustainability Index: CGI is monitored by the Dow Jones Sustainability Index, which evaluates companies based on their sustainability practices and performance.
These standards and memberships underscore CGI's dedication to integrating ESG principles into its operations and ensuring continuous improvement in its sustainability efforts. "
ITEM,80123_105069_0,,C.,"ESG Policies, Processes, and Reporting
(a) Does the Proponent have an existing standalone ESG Policy?
(b) Does the Proponent have a framework or plan to monitor and measure progress towards your ESG goals?
(c) Are you aligned with any regulatory reporting?
(d) Which department or position has the overall responsibility for ESG matters?

",0,"(a) Standalone ESG Policy: CGI has a dedicated Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) policy that serves as a framework for responsible operations across all its subsidiaries and affiliates. This policy promotes environmentally and socially responsible conduct by integrating best practices and processes for ESG management. It outlines the risks associated with ESG factors and is applicable to all CGI employees, contractors, and vendors, ensuring a comprehensive approach to sustainability.

(b) Monitoring and Measuring Progress: CGI has established a robust framework to monitor and measure its progress toward ESG goals. The company undergoes annual assessments by leading external organizations, such as EcoVadis, which evaluates its sustainability performance based on international standards. CGI's ESG goals and progress are transparently shared with stakeholders through its annual ESG report, which includes quantified targets and performance indicators. This report is prepared in accordance with the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) Standards, ensuring that CGI's commitments are publicly accessible.

(c) Regulatory ESG Reporting Requirements: CGI aligns with various regulatory ESG reporting requirements, including the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) standards and the United Nations Global Compact principles. This alignment ensures that CGI's reporting practices meet global best practices and regulatory expectations, reinforcing its commitment to transparency and accountability in its ESG initiatives.

(d) Responsibility for ESG Matters: Overall responsibility for ESG matters at CGI lies with the executive leadership team, including the CEO and the Board of Directors. This leadership structure ensures that ESG considerations are integrated into the company's strategic decision-making processes and that there is accountability for achieving ESG objectives.

Through these initiatives, CGI demonstrates its commitment to being a responsible corporate citizen, actively engaging in sustainability practices that benefit its stakeholders and the communities in which it operates.
*Screenshot*"
ITEM,80123_167218_0,,D.,"Organization Social Responsibility

(a) Does the Proponent have a separate standalone Corporate Social Responsibility governance that provides details of your approach to how every employee does their job everyday (i.e., environment, health & safety and financial)?
(b) How does the Proponent promote wellness, employee training and development etc.

",0,"CGI has a standalone Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) governance framework that outlines its approach to daily employee responsibilities, including environmental, health and safety, and financial considerations. This framework is designed to ensure that all employees understand their roles in contributing to the company's CSR objectives. It emphasizes responsible business practices across various dimensions, including quality management, environmental responsibility, community engagement, and the well-being of employees. The framework is integrated into CGI's overall business model, reinforcing the importance of corporate responsibility in all facets of operations.

(b) CGI promotes employee wellness, training, and development initiatives through several key programs and policies. The company has implemented the ""Oxygen"" health and well-being program, which focuses on the mental, social, physical, and financial well-being of its employees. This program includes prevention, education, risk identification, and intervention strategies to support employees' health.

Additionally, CGI invests significantly in training and development, providing employees with resources to enhance their skills continuously. The training program is designed to help employees maintain, refresh, and advance their skill sets, ensuring they are well-equipped to meet the evolving challenges in the IT industry. This commitment to ongoing professional development is a critical component of CGI's strategy to be an employer of choice and to foster a culture of continuous improvement. "
ITEM,80123_167219_0,,E.,"Indigenous Reconciliation:
Describe how the Proponent engages with Indigenous communities and persons and/or provide socio-economic opportunities?

",0,"CGI engages with Indigenous communities and persons through various initiatives aimed at fostering inclusion, understanding, and socio-economic opportunities that support reconciliation. Here are some key aspects of their engagement:

1. Partnerships with Indigenous Organizations: CGI actively forms partnerships with Indigenous organizations, businesses, and consultants to incorporate Indigenous perspectives into their projects. These collaborations aim to enrich project outcomes and support economic development within Indigenous communities. Within Nova Scotia, CGI has collaborated with Dalhousie University, to support sending two students from CGI’s Atlantic Business Unit to work with the Truro Start Program to support Indigenous Computer Science initiatives at Millbrook First Nation.
*Screenshot*

2. Training and Awareness Programs: CGI provides extensive training to its employees, such as the ""4 Seasons of Reconciliation"" courses from the First Nations University of Canada. This training enhances awareness and understanding of the historical and contemporary relationships between Indigenous peoples and settlers in Canada, aligning with the Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada's Calls to Action.

3. Inclusive Hiring Practices: CGI prioritizes hiring consultants, staff members, and vendors from under-represented communities, including Indigenous professionals. This approach ensures that project teams reflect the diversity of the communities they serve and provides opportunities for Indigenous individuals to contribute their expertise.

4. Economic Opportunities: CGI is committed to increasing economic opportunities for First Nations, Inuit, and Métis businesses. The company aims to build capacity, reduce barriers, and increase access to capital for Indigenous communities, thereby enriching its workforce through inclusion and appreciation of Indigenous cultures.
Through these initiatives, CGI demonstrates its commitment to supporting reconciliation and fostering socio-economic opportunities for Indigenous communities. "

PART 1 – INVITATION AND SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS
1.1 Invitation to Respondents
This Request for Supplier Qualifications (“RFSQ”) is an invitation by the Province of Nova Scotia (the
“Province”) on behalf of the Department of Cyber Security and Digital Solutions (“CSDS”) and the Nova
Scotia Health Authority (“NSHA”), to prospective respondents to qualify in accordance with Evaluation
of Responses (Part 2) for eligibility to potentially provide IT Resources for Transformational Projects as
further described in the RFSQ Particulars (Appendix B) (the “Deliverables”). This RFSQ is being conducted
pursuant to the Nova Scotia Sustainable Procurement Policy and Procurement Manual.
CSDS and NSHA invite qualified vendors to join a supply arrangement for IT resources to support key
transformational projects. Vendors will provide skilled IT professionals in areas such as software
development, cloud computing, cybersecurity, data analytics, and project management, contributing to
impactful projects that enhance efficiency, security, and digital transformation. Interested vendors are
invited to submit a proposal for stage 1 of this RFSQ. Successful respondents, known as Master Agreement
Holders, will be invited to submit proposals to project-specific statements of work (“SOW”) in a process
as described in section B.2 of this RFSQ.
In accordance with Nova Scotia’s procurement policies and applicable trade agreements, and
notwithstanding any provision of this RFSQ, the Province may initially evaluate only those SOWs
submitted by Canadian Suppliers, Canadian Business Subsidiaries, and International Free Trade
Agreement Suppliers. If this process does not identify a successful proposal, SOWs submitted by United
States of America (USA) Suppliers and International Non-Free Trade Agreement Suppliers may
subsequently be evaluated or eliminated for consideration.
1.2 RFSQ Contact
For the purposes of this procurement process, the “RFSQ Contact” shall be:
Kirsty Slauenwhite
Procurement Specialist, – IT/Digital Procurement
Department of Service Nova Scotia
All communications must be directed through the Ariba Sourcing Event Message Board
The Ariba Sourcing Event Message Board is an area in Ariba where all system notifications and
Government of Nova Scotia (GNS) created messages can be viewed. Suppliers can send messages directly
to the GNS procurement team through the Event Message Board. Note: All messages sent from suppliers
can only be viewed by the GNS Procurement team and not by other suppliers that are participating in the
same sourcing event.
Respondents and their representatives are not permitted to contact any employees, officers, agents,
elected or appointed officials or other representatives of the Province, other than the RFSQ Contact or
their designate, concerning matters regarding this RFSQ. Failure to adhere to this rule may result in the
disqualification of the respondent and the rejection of the respondent’s response.

1.3 Master Agreement
Selected respondents will be invited to enter into a professional services agreement in the form set out
in Appendix F (the “Master Agreement”), which will govern the potential subsequent provision of the
Deliverables pursuant to potential invitational second stage competitive processes. The term of the

the Master Agreement on the same terms and conditions for an additional term of up to one (1), two (2)
year extension for an overall length of seven (7) years. For clarity, the Master Agreement is intended to

PART 2 – EVALUATION OF RESPONSES
2.1 Stages of Evaluation
The Province will conduct the evaluation of responses in the following two stages:

requirements. If a response fails to satisfy all of the mandatory submission requirements, the Province
will issue the respondent a rectification notice identifying the deficiencies and providing the respondent

requirements within the Rectification Period, its response will be excluded from further consideration.
The Rectification Period will begin to run from the date that the Province issues a rectification notice to
the respondent.
The mandatory submission requirements are as follows:
2.2.1 No Amendment to Forms
Other than inserting information requested on the mandatory submission forms set out in the
RFSQ, a respondent may not make any changes to any of the forms. Any response containing any
such changes, whether on the face of the form or elsewhere in the response, will be disqualified.
2.2.2 Submission Form (Appendix A)

authorized representative of the respondent. Respondent must include all pages of Appendix A

(Appendix D) completed according to the instructions contained in the form.

according to the instructions contained in the form.

B.1 THE DELIVERABLES
CSDS and NSHA are seeking qualified vendors to participate in a supply arrangement for IT resources to
support transformational projects. These initiatives aim to modernize and enhance our digital
infrastructure, streamline operations, and deliver innovative solutions that meet evolving organizational
and public needs. Respondents will provide skilled IT professionals with expertise across various
categories, including software development, cloud computing, cybersecurity, data engineers, data
analytics, and project management. By participating in this supply arrangement, vendors will contribute
to the successful execution of high-impact projects that drive efficiency, security, and digital
transformation across the Province.
The projects listed below represent current transformational initiatives that may involve vendors
selected from the supply arrangement for engagement by CSDS:
• Early Years Modernization Program
• School Lunch Program Support
• Web Transformation
• Land Modernization
• Digital Case Management
• Rebate Program Delivery
• Digital Service Modernization
• Risky Apps Modernization
• Hosting / Cloud Modernization
• Housing Programs Modernization
• Digital Justice Transformation
• Opportunities and Social Development Digital Transformation
• Cyber Security Strategy
• Digital Platforms Modernization
• Data and AI Strategic Action Plan Supports
• O365 Productivity Tool Training
• Digital Transformation Advisory Services
The projects listed below represent current transformational initiatives that may involve vendors
selected from the supply arrangement for engagement by NSHA:
• Adoption and implementation of AI initiatives.
• Cloud and data engineering initiatives in support of data infrastructure.
• Ensuring interoperability of disparate data sources to support sharing information with citizens
or clinical transformation and efficiencies.
• Development of new digital applications to support sharing information with citizens or clinical
transformation and efficiencies
• Integration of new features and functionality into existing applications
• Preparation for and integration of existing systems into new digital systems that may be
adopted to support healthcare transformation

support of transformational projects.

capacity and requirements.

Respondent Experience and Qualifications
About CGI

Founded in 1976 in Quebec City by Serge Godin (current Chairman of the Board) and André Imbeau (former board member and advisor), CGI is a proudly Canadian, multinational information technology consulting and systems integration firm. Over the past 49 years, CGI has grown into one of the largest IT and business consulting services firms in the world, generating over $14.7 billion CAD in global revenue annually—approximately $2 billion CAD of which comes from Canadian clients.

As a 100% Canadian-owned company, CGI is a true Canadian success story. With more than 94,000 professionals operating in 40 countries, we combine global delivery capabilities with local accountability. This model allows us to bring world-class expertise directly to our clients’ front doors while maintaining a deep understanding of local needs and priorities.

CGI offers a comprehensive portfolio of services, including strategic IT and business consulting, systems integration, managed IT and business process services, and proprietary intellectual property solutions. Our disciplined delivery approach has earned us an industry-leading track record for completing projects on time and within budget.
CGI in Atlantic Canada

CGI has had a strong and growing presence in Atlantic Canada since opening our first regional office in 1991. Initially focused on systems integration and IT consulting for both commercial and public sector clients, our services have since expanded to include business process services and software application management.

CGI Atlantic is a proud Nova Scotia business, which has been validated with Nova Scotia Government Procurement Office. We employ over 400 full-time, permanent employees across Nova Scotia. We are located at 7071 Bayers Road, Suite 1007, Halifax, Nova Scotia and our Nova Scotia Registry of Joint Stock Number is 3281955.

Today, CGI employs over 840 professionals across Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland. We are one of the region’s largest IT employers, with a diverse consulting practice, a thriving banking business, and a state-of-the-art global delivery center.

In 2001, CGI Group Inc. and Service New Brunswick Inc. (SNB) signed a memorandum of understanding to establish CGI’s global government service delivery initiative in Fredericton, New Brunswick. This led to the creation of our “g-Commerce Lab” at the Fredericton Knowledge Park, further cementing our commitment to innovation and public sector transformation.

In 2004, CGI partnered with Manulife to launch the Atlantic Global Delivery Center (AGDC), headquartered in Halifax with a satellite office in Charlottetown, PEI. The AGDC provides application development, maintenance, and outsourcing services to clients across Canada, the U.S., and Europe.
Proven Experience and Delivery Excellence

CGI has a 49-year track record of delivering end-to-end solutions for complex, large-scale projects. Our work with public sector organizations, including the Nova Scotia Health Authority, Government of New Brunswick, the Province of Nova Scotia, Medavie Blue Cross, and local credit unions—demonstrates our ability to drive economic growth and deliver high-quality, reliable services.

We are known for our ability to manage projects involving multiple stakeholder groups, competing priorities, and significant organizational change. Our resourcing strategy enables us to quickly mobilize skilled teams, ensuring projects are executed efficiently, within budget, and to the highest quality standards.

Our customer-centric culture emphasizes transparency, accountability, and results. We build and maintain strategic partnerships with internal and external stakeholders to ensure the successful delivery of both business and IT initiatives.
Experience in Public Sector IT Projects:

CGI is a significant player in modernizing public sector applications and services globally, with a strong focus on Canada. The company helps government organizations leverage technology and data to enhance citizen experiences, increase transparency, and ensure data security and privacy. CGI has over 5,000 professionals dedicated to the public sector and generates more than $1 billion in revenue from this sector, making it one of the largest IT and business process services providers to government in Canada and the U.S.

In Canada, CGI serves the federal government and 75% of provincial and territorial governments, reflecting its deep expertise in facilitating business transformation within the public sector. The company collaborates with clients to develop adaptive cloud strategies and employs a modernization approach that encompasses foundational systems, data, and application portfolios. Recent projects include the modernization of procurement processes and the development of centralized data repositories for health services, which aim to improve efficiency and service delivery.
Overall, CGI's efforts are geared towards helping public sector clients modernize and transform their services to better serve citizens and improve operational efficiency.

CGI has a history of delivering IT projects to various public sector clients, including government agencies and public administration organizations. An example is CGI's eight-year framework agreement with Valtori, the Finnish government’s ICT service provider, valued at approximately 384 million euros (CA $576M). This agreement encompasses a wide range of services aimed at enhancing the efficiency and security of government information and communication technology. CGI's experience in managing mission-critical services ensures that projects are executed securely and efficiently, meeting the high availability and security requirements essential for public sector operations.

CGI has a long-standing and multifaceted relationship with the Province of Nova Scotia, having collaborated on a wide range of initiatives. These include the SAP Modernization Program, AMANDA Upgrade Project, LaMPSS/ICM, Online Grants & Subsidy Services, Congratulatory Message Service System, De-Risking Services, and numerous cybersecurity projects—such as Threat Risk Assessments (TRAs) as a service, penetration tests (PTs), privacy impact assessments (PIAs), and strategic advisory engagements. CGI has also supported several Nova Scotia Department of Health initiatives.

In November 2020, CGI and NSHA entered into a strategic partnership aimed at building a stable, scalable service while achieving significant cost savings on TRAs. This collaboration has been renewed through successive contracts in August 2021, April 2022, and April 2024. Over the past 53 months, CGI and NSHA have cultivated a partnership grounded in collaboration, transparency, and trust—consistently exceeding expectations and delivering added value to the province.

One notable outcome of this partnership has been the economic benefit generated by the creation of 10 new cybersecurity roles at CGI in Halifax, Nova Scotia. Since the partnership began, CGI has successfully delivered 85 TRAs, at least 37 PTs, and a minimum of 5 vulnerability assessments (VAs) to NSHA.

Beyond NSHA, CGI maintains strong relationships with the Province of Nova Scotia and its CSDS and IM/IT groups. CGI also provides strategic advisory and staffing support to other key organizations, including Halifax Water (e.g., architectural advisory), Medavie Blue Cross, Service New Brunswick, and NB Families.

Healthcare Industry Expertise: CGI is a leader in working with provincial health organizations, health regions, and hospitals to harness the power of technology and improve the quality of care, while managing costs and enhancing productivity.  We live and work close to our clients. Immersed in local markets and political environments, CGI has subject matter experts for specific regional offerings who are well-versed in digital transformation and the human-political dynamics of large-scale healthcare service design. At CGI, healthcare is not simply one of our areas of expertise, it’s personal. We have a vested interest in seeing our healthcare systems perform better and in helping healthcare organizations turn their future vision into tangible patient outcomes.

CGI and many of our Atlantic members have worked with provincial health organizations, health regions, and hospitals in Canada and the US. We currently provide services to the Province of Nova Scotia’s Cyber Security and Digital Services, the Department of Health and Wellness and Nova Scotia Health, and other with Health Ministries and Authorities across Canada, including Ontario, Saskatchewan, Alberta and British Colombia. We have a strong US and global healthcare business, with clients in over a dozen countries.
CGI health solutions and services support:
Billions recovered in improper health claims payments.
6.6 billion records for health systems
55+ million Medicare beneficiaries through portals
17+ billion in EHR incentive payments
230+ hospitals and departments of health
195+ million people covered by health plans served by CGI.

Connecting data insights to clinical and operational actions enables evidence-based decision-making that drives e-health. As a result, healthcare organizations must focus on finding ways to safely capture, store, and provide access to patient information—such as electronic medical records, e-prescriptions, and electronic vaccination records—across patients and providers.

CGI’s Health Information System (HIS) Center of Excellence provides end-to-end services, helping health systems and hospitals achieve their goals while maximizing value. CGI’s HIS Centre of Excellence has developed a CGI Health Information Integration Framework® (HIIF) based on a standard cycle of organizational planning and effort. It brings both technical and business planning and execution together, creating the necessary alignment for health information integration mandates. It provides healthcare organizations with a way to evaluate, prepare, implement and support new information sharing reality by applying a flexible yet structured approach to information integration. It also provides a flexible underlying foundation to deliver increased clinical and business functionality through expert integration and enterprise architecture management. Ultimately, its strength in leveraging existing data, processes and infrastructure will provide the relevant information required for creating patient-centered knowledge.
Commitment to Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) and Sustainability Commitments

At CGI, we are deeply committed to advancing Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles across all aspects of our operations and client engagements. Our approach to sustainability is comprehensive, encompassing environmental stewardship, social responsibility, and strong governance practices.

Environmental Responsibility is a cornerstone of our strategy. We actively partner with clients to implement green space creation and restoration projects, organize litter pick events, and deliver integrated environmental and energy solutions. Through our advanced IT capabilities and under the guidance of our Chief Sustainability Officer, we support clients in navigating sustainability challenges and seizing opportunities. Our services are designed to help clients progress toward their net-zero goals, with offerings that include sustainable technology solutions and enhanced ESG capabilities.

CGI is committed to fostering a healthier environment through active community engagement and ambitious climate goals. We support local initiatives such as tree planting, blue and green recovery efforts, and environmental events in partnership with organizations like the Canal & River Trust. Our employees contribute through recycling programs and eco-conscious practices promoted by our Green Committee.

We have set a clear target to achieve net-zero carbon emissions by 2030. Our Climate and Sustainability Advisory Practice supports clients on their net-zero journeys through green IT infrastructure, paper-reducing document solutions, and facility optimization. This commitment is reinforced by our participation in global climate initiatives, including COP27, and our endorsement of climate-focused partnership charters.

Additionally, our collaboration with Project Seagrass helps conserve vital seagrass ecosystems—key natural carbon sinks—by processing and cleaning samples across the UK, contributing to long-term CO₂ reduction and environmental preservation.

Social responsibility is equally integral to our mission. We foster a collaborative and inclusive culture that prioritizes the well-being and development of our professionals. CGI invests in both the personal and professional growth of our team members and is committed to driving positive societal change through responsible business practices and active community engagement. We uphold the highest standards of human rights across our operations and supply chains, in alignment with United Nations guidelines.

On the governance front, CGI operates with unwavering integrity and transparency. We maintain a robust ESG governance structure that informs our strategic decisions and ensures ethical conduct across all regions and stakeholder groups. Our commitment to responsible innovation is reflected in our efforts to minimize the environmental impact of digital technologies and to apply ethical principles in the development and deployment of artificial intelligence. This is exemplified by the publication of our inaugural Responsible AI (RAI) report, which outlines our approach to the ethical use of AI in alignment with ESG values.

Our environmental, social and governance commitment is rooted through our core Values, through projects delivered in collaboration with clients, and through operating practices, supply chain management, and community services projects. For more information, please visit CGI’s ESG page to learn more.
Services Offered

CGI has extensive experience in providing digital solutions for Canadian public sector and healthcare clients, focusing on enhancing citizen services and operational efficiency. With over 49 years of consulting experience, CGI has worked on numerous projects with the Province of Nova Scotia, including the SAP Modernization Program, AMANDA Upgrade Project, LaMPSS/ICM, Online Grants & Subsidy Services, Congratulatory Message Service System, De-Risking Services, various cybersecurity projects (TRAs as a service, PTs, PIAs, Strategic advisory), One Patient One Record (OPOR) clinical support model, A2i application support, and several Department of Health initiatives, such as Health Data Exchange. In addition, CGI provides skilled IT staff professionals to Halifax Water, Medavie Blue Cross, Service New Brunswick (including the Clinical Information System project), NB Families, and more.

CGI is playing a pivotal role in transforming public services across Canada and globally by delivering innovative, digital-first, cloud-enabled, and AI-native solutions. Their work is helping governments and healthcare organizations become more agile, efficient, and citizen-focused—especially in regions like Nova Scotia.
Global and National Impact

CGI’s approach to digital transformation is rooted in deep collaboration with public sector clients. Through platforms like DigitalGov360, CGI supports governments in delivering seamless digital services such as online payments, licensing, and permitting systems—handling millions of transactions annually. Our emphasis on responsible AI adoption, data governance, and secure ecosystems ensures that innovation is balanced with public trust and ethical standards.

In healthcare, CGI is a leader in enabling patient-centric digital transformation. We offer end-to-end services that include health information systems (HIS), data analytics, machine learning, and intelligent automation. These tools help healthcare providers improve outcomes, reduce costs, and enhance operational efficiency.
For the Province of Nova Scotia, CGI’s capabilities are especially relevant in two key areas:
Public Sector Modernization:

CGI’s industry and technology experts can help CSDS develop a vision for future-oriented connected public services enabled by practical and executable strategies and plans to enable digital transformation.
Our automated tools combined with cloud, data and AI experts can support application rationalization, modernization and data migration, exchange and archival strategies.
Our cloud-native platforms can help Nova Scotia streamline citizen services, improve accessibility, and reduce administrative overhead.
Our expertise in AI and automation can support smarter decision-making and more responsive government operations.
Healthcare Transformation:
CGI’s work with provincial health organizations across Canada positions us well to support Nova Scotia Health in building a more connected, data-driven, and patient-focused system.
We have unique experience implementing data exchange and interoperability strategies and plans specifically tailored to healthcare data.
Our solutions can enhance interoperability between systems, enable virtual care, and unlock the value of health data to improve patient outcomes.
Inspiring the Future

CGI’s mission is not just about technology, it’s about empowering communities. By embedding innovation into the fabric of public services, we are helping governments and healthcare providers deliver better experiences and outcomes for citizens. In Nova Scotia, this means a future where services are more accessible, healthcare is more personalized, and public institutions are more resilient and responsive.
Figure 1: Unlocking the full potential of technology
CGI provides a full range of services to help our clients unlock the full potential of technology.

Business and Technical Advisory Services: CGI's Global Consulting Services Framework supports clients through every stage of business transformation, from concept development and planning to design, execution, and sustainment. This service encompasses strategy, governance, people, process, and technology, ensuring a holistic approach to addressing complex business challenges. CGI employs a diverse team of specialists, including Six Sigma and Lean certified consultants, ITIL Foundation certified professionals, and Project Management Professionals (PMP), to deliver best-in-class advisory services.

Application Development and Integration: CGI's approach to Application Development Services focuses on effectively integrating new or existing software and hardware or developing and modifying applications to align with the client's business objectives. This includes designing customized architectures or applications and ensuring that all integrations respect the approved scope regarding effort, cost, and quality. CGI's commitment to meeting evolving business needs is evident in its ability to adapt and enhance information systems as required.

Digital Transformation Services: CGI has successfully managed numerous digital transformation projects, including the implementation of electronic document management systems and the digitization of security and election monitoring processes. The company has also developed online citizen service portals and digital twins of cities to promote sustainability and innovative solutions. CGI's role in these projects includes IT project management services, agile project management, and comprehensive business process management services.

Managed Services: CGI offers a comprehensive suite of managed services that cover all aspects of application development and maintenance lifecycles. This includes infrastructure services that provide clients with technology, industry, and domain expertise to enhance operations and drive innovation. CGI's managed services encompass energy-efficient data centers, cloud computing, managed security services, and the strategic use of artificial intelligence, all supported by a unique enterprise services management toolset.

Cybersecurity Services: CGI provides a range of cybersecurity services, including consulting and risk assessment to help clients identify and manage security vulnerabilities. The services include governance, management, compliance, and maturity assessments of security strategies. CGI also offers engineering and business protection services, focusing on security architecture, safe engineering, and ongoing testing and assurance. Additionally, CGI's managed security services help clients monitor and respond to security threats effectively, ensuring a reliable and cost-effective security posture. Some of our Cyber Security clients include NSHA, CSDS, EfficiencyOne, Halifax Water, Halifax Harbour Bridges, British Columbia Ministry of Health, Workers Compensation Board of Nova Scotia, and more.
Data Privacy:

CGI’s Enterprise Data Privacy organization is a dedicated global data privacy team with explicitly defined responsibilities and accountabilities regarding the delivery and operation of CGI’s enterprise privacy program. Headed by CGI’s Chief Data Protection Officer, Lucille Bonenfant, CGI’s Enterprise Data Privacy organization reaches across all CGI business units through qualified and experienced data protection specialists who a) provide guidance, direction, and training regarding CGI’s privacy policies and industry best practices, b) monitor compliance with CGI’s privacy policies and processes, c) contribute to the ongoing development and enhancement of CGI’s privacy program, d) promote and foster a culture of data protection excellence within CGI. Within Canada, CGI’s Enterprise Data Privacy is led by the Canadian Data Protection Officer, Rob Clark. The members of CGI Canada’s Privacy Team are all certified privacy professionals whose responsibility includes keeping track of applicable federal, territorial and provincial regulations and policies, as well as changes to the regulations, and the guidance or decisions made by Canada’s Privacy Commissioners and Ombudsmen, to ensure that CGI’s knowledge and application of applicable laws and regulations remains current.
CGI takes a holistic approach to IT transformation, which allows us to support our clients across the dimensions of their business and operations.
Figure 2: Framework for IT Operating Model Transformation
We have experience and expertise to help our clients address the needs of transformation holistically, where we can hone in on one or many capabilities required to enable major transformation.
Figure 3: Transformation Capability Model

These services collectively demonstrate CGI's capability and experience in delivering solutions that align with the broad range requirements of the RFSQ, ensuring that clients receive comprehensive support throughout their transformation journeys.

CGI partners with over 150 technology companies so that we can dynamically bring our clients best-of-breed modern platforms, to not only help them deliver today’s business outcomes, but also be ready for tomorrow. CGI defines a strategic alliance as global in scope, aligned with our core service offerings and focus industries, and best positioned to drive growth for both CGI and our partners. Today, we have nine strategic alliances: Microsoft, AWS, Google, SAP, Salesforce, ServiceNow, UIPath, Blue Prism and NetApp.
Figure 4: CGI's Global Alliance Partnerships
CGI has partnerships with a variety of leading technology companies to enhance its service offerings. Key partnerships include:
Major Technology Partners:
Specialized Partners:
The Value of Strategic Technology Partnerships

In today’s rapidly evolving digital landscape, partnerships with technology companies are more than just beneficial—they're essential. These collaborations empower organizations to accelerate innovation, enhance operational efficiency, and deliver better outcomes.

Technology partners bring specialized expertise, tools, and services that help businesses navigate complex challenges such as cloud adoption, digital transformation, cybersecurity, and data analytics. Whether it's through software solutions, infrastructure support, or strategic consulting, these partners provide tailored guidance and proven methodologies that align with business goals.

Many of the world’s leading organizations rely on technology partnerships to stay competitive. These collaborations often include access to exclusive training, certifications, and corporate resources that ensure partners are equipped to deliver high-quality, scalable solutions. Additionally, recognized partner programs often include rigorous validation processes, giving customers confidence in the capabilities and reliability of their chosen providers.
By working with trusted technology partners, CSDS and NSHA can:
Accelerate time-to-market for new products and services
Reduce risk through expert-led implementations
Optimize costs and performance with best-in-class tools
Gain access to innovation and emerging technologies
Scale operations with flexible, cloud-based solutions

Whether you're just beginning your digital journey or looking to optimize existing systems, partnering with the right technology providers can be a game-changer. In summary, CGI's knowledge, skills, and expertise in analyzing business needs and translating them into effective IT solutions are evident in its structured approach, problem-solving capabilities, innovative mindset, collaborative practices, and proven track record of success.

CGI helps our Healthcare clients pursue an end-to-end model that includes business and enterprise digital strategy encompassing change management; systems design, implementation, and integration; and the use of managed IT and business process services to mitigate cost pressures and fund greater innovation.

We build partnerships that give us a unique point of view, proven expertise, and innovative solutions directly related to our clients’ business goals. Ultimately, our partnerships are driven by client preference, aligned with client goals, and managed in a way that helps clients respond quickly and competitively to change.

We adhere firmly to the principle of objectivity when it comes to meeting our clients’ needs. We never approach a client with a preconceived position or approach, nor do we ever force a partnership. These many alliances and partnerships support our development of expertise in a wide variety of modern platforms to bring the best possible level of service to our clients. We feel strongly that we can support our clients in their objective to build local, national, and international partnerships across and within the innovation ecosystem.

To augment our capacity in strategic and technical healthcare consulting, we have partnered with Pivot Point Consulting. Pivot Point is also a leader in Health sector IT staffing and has an EMR practice team that brings experience implementing over 100 EMR installations. Their analysts average 10 years of experience and four or more certifications in their respective EMRs and have experience with clients across Canada and the US. They are attuned to previously observed challenges, opportunities and craft effective responses. DRIVE is comprised of 4 phases: Discover, Refine & Integrate, Validate and Engage. Each phase contains a different engagement and outcome to be achieved to ensure a seamless implementation working closely with our clients.
Discover

During the Discover phase CGI gathers requirements and designs the functional and technical solution. As a team, we identify and plan, the key milestones to be accomplished according to the agile methodology. Optimize the customer experience across all touchpoints
Move to real-time integrated operations
Align design, technology and data
Improve predictability to anticipate users’ needs
Align and leverage tools to drive product strategy
Make decisions based on insights (Intelligent Experience Design, quantum segmentation)
Take advantage of connectivity and cheaper economics
Refine & Integrate

The Refine and Integrate phase is when we configure the module, run playbacks with business experts and adjust accordingly, using sprints to configure and develop the solution. The team holds pre-sprint activities to detail the backlog refinement and plan the sprint. During the sprint, we hold daily scrums to synchronize activities and create a plan for the next 24 hours. We deliver to the playback environment, which is our prod-like environment.
Mid-Sprint Review: Adjustments mid-sprint
Playbacks: Held after 2-3 sprints, they showcase delivered value to the customer
New stories: New requirements discovered or corrections
Retrospective: Review and adjust for next sprints
Validate

The Validation phase is the last full test done when the product is ready to go in production. We conduct testing to confirm that the solution has been successfully adapted and meets your requirements, using automated tools to test core functionality and custom testing scripts for integrations and reports. We also conduct the User Acceptance Test, which is the last sign-off by the solution owner to make sure the product fits their needs. The client’s feedback is taken into consideration, and the product is modified accordingly.
Engage

The Engage phase deploys the configuration and extensions in the production environment and triggers conversion steps and other legacy system activities. This phase also includes major data conversion or process change activities that are required for a go live. We provide the client with training, and our team of implementers delivers Hypercare to make sure that the solution is fully adopted by the organization. Our leadership in sustainable IT was recognized with the “Sustainable IT Label, Level 1” award, underscoring our dedication to ethical and regenerative digital environments. We also develop and share resources such as eco-design guides and training programs to help clients and partners adopt more sustainable digital practices.

Through these comprehensive actions, CGI demonstrates a deep and ongoing commitment to advancing inclusion, equity, and sustainability in the IT sector. Our initiatives not only support marginalized communities but also contribute to a more diverse, innovative, and resilient workforce and society. We believe that by investing in people, communities, and the planet, we can help shape a more just and sustainable future. This commitment is reflected in every aspect of our work—from how we recruit and develop talent to how we design and deliver technology solutions. As we continue to grow, we remain focused on creating lasting impact and driving meaningful change across the regions and sectors we serve.

6.0 BACKGROUND INFORMATION
6.1 GENERAL OVERVIEW OF THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH SHARED ANALYTICS
BRANCH:
A principle of the Government of New Brunswick (GNB) Digital New Brunswick
2.0 strategy is making evidence-based decisions using accurate up-to-date data.
As part of the associated action plan, GNB is revisiting barriers that limit
constructive data sharing between departments while upholding privacy and
security. To address one such barrier, the Department of Health (DH) and the
Department of Social Development (DSD) combined their analytics and research
units to form Shared Analytics. The goal of the Shared Analytic Branch is to
serve the analytics and research needs of both DH and DSD.
The Shared Analytics Branch (SAB)
includes
• data specialists, epidemiologists, health economists, Health Information
Management (HIM) professionals, and other technical subject matter
experts,
who
• acquire, wrangle, analyze, transform, and serve data,
from
• A variety of on-prem and cloud solutions,
to:
• plan/monitor/evaluate health programs, enable executive decision support,
enable research, and execute health economics, epidemiological, and
health system performance analytical exercises,
for
• consumption by GNB Health System Partner executives, DH and DSD
branches, DH/DSD staff, external agencies and researchers, and the
public.
One source of data for the Shared Analytics Branch is the Data Sharing Platform
(DSP). The DSP was set up to integrate health data, ingesting, storing,
transforming, and serving large and varied datasets for analysis. Appendix C
(DSP Solution Diagram) defines the current state architecture for the DSP, while
Appendix D (DSP Data Estate Spec Sheet) describes basic components of data
structures implemented within the architecture as well as the data that is
processed and stored by the system.
Two GNB groups oversee the management, maintenance, and governance
responsibilities for the DSP:
• A Shared Analytics Branch team (SAB-DSP) that:
o Defines the business vision, strategy, roadmap, governance and
requirements for the DSP.
o Implements and maintains business policies, standards, and
processes (including data governance) to realize the mission and
vision of the DSP and provide operational oversight.
• A Provincial Health Application Services (PHAS) team within Service New
Brunswick (SNB) (SNB-DSP) that:
o Defines the architecture, infrastructure, and technology needed to
achieve the DSP strategy and roadmap.
o Implements and maintains the technology and infrastructure needed
to realize the mission and vision of the DSP.
Our mission for the DSP is to provide the data needed to enable the holistic,
integrated, and advanced analytics necessary for the Department of Health and
Social Development to make evidence-informed decisions that support the health
of New Brunswicker’s and guarantee the sustainability of our Health System. Our
vision for the DSP is to serve as the single-source-of-truth for all the New
Brunswick Health System Partner’s analytical needs towards those same goals.
Currently, the DSP empowers the research and analytical staff from multiple
public bodies to implement all phases of the data/analytics/research life cycles.
The SAB-DSP team has completed strategic planning exercises to define current
and future states of the DSP, finding potential gaps that the SAB and SNB DSP
teams will need to address to advance the DSP. Further, SNB-DSP staff
performed a series of scoping and requirements gathering exercises to define an
SAB data architecture and understand where the DSP aligns within that larger
context. The results of these exercises outlined several foundational services
needed to advance the DSP to a future state where it achieves its mission, fulfills
its vision, and is positioned to be the core of any SAB data architecture.
These foundational services include features that ensure the data is secure,
private, accurate, available, and usable.
6.2 CURRENT STATE PROBLEM STATEMENT
As the DSP continues to evolve in alignment with its mission and vision and to
become the core of the SAB data architecture, the growing scope and scale of
the system risk turning it from strategic asset into a potential liability due to the
absence of comprehensive solution(s) that enable the accuracy, availability, and
usability components listed above while also enhancing existing privacy and
security procedures.
Throughout the requirements gathering exercise, user described themes relating
to the foundational services described above arose:
• Availability: users were unable to understand the full extent of information
included in the DSP.
• Accuracy: users struggled to understand the provenance and quality of
data information available.
• Usability: users had planned analyses derailed due to outdated or sparse
metadata and documentation.
• Security: users need to access the DSP environment before they can
evaluate whether specific data products will serve their use case.
• Privacy: users need to access microdata within the DSP to decide whether
specific data elements will serve their use case.
While the SAB-DSP team implements policies to address the above issues, they
are falling short as the DSP expands. Manual efforts alone are no longer
sufficient to comprehensively understand, manage, and communicate the DSPs
current state.
6.3 SERVICES REQUIRED BY THE DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH SHARED ANALYTICS
BRANCH:
To achieve the DSPs mission, prepare for future states, and become the core of
SABs data architecture, the SAB-DSP team is seeking solutions that:
1. Comprehensively serve all available metadata in a singular, simple-to-use
and coherent platform that enables holistic discovery.
2. Automatically surface, house, and present DSP data structures as
interactive metadata.
a. Data products, databases, data sets, tables & views, data columns,
schemas, keys, lineage etc.
3. Automatically surface and transform, house, and present DSP data
expression as interactive metadata.
a. Data quality, select summary statistics, and other profiling
mechanisms.
4. Automatically track, house, and present changes in data and metadata
defined in 1-3 above.
The SAB-DSP team believes that an Enterprise Data Catalogue Solution
deployed alongside the DSP will allow us to enhance a variety of the availability,
accuracy, usability, security, and privacy services described above. The
Enterprise Data Catalogue will have a platform that serves as a window into the
DSP that increases observability and discoverability of the system without direct
access to the DSP or microdata. To achieve this, the data catalogue should
automatically define aspects such as data structures, lineage, quality, and
statistical profiles of select data elements.
With the selected Enterprise Data Catalogue solution in place,
• Analytical staff should be able to:
o use the singular comprehensive platform to understand what
information is in the DSP,
o rely on the holistic presentation of information in the catalogue to
confidently select the most relevant data product(s) for their use
case,
o use system derived metadata to achieve more granular
understanding of specific data product structures prior to microdata
access,
o evaluate the provenance of specific data products to understand
dependencies without elevated or expanded access,
o examine the data quality profile of data products to decide
analytical suitability without access,
o examine the basic statistical summaries of specific data elements
within data products to decide analytical suitability without
microdata access.
• Engineering staff should be able to:
o examine lineage of data products to understand up- and
downstream dependencies.
• Governance staff should be able to:
o direct analytical users to the Data Catalogue for preparatory data
structure investigation in lieu of access to the DSP,
o direct analytical users to the Data Catalogue for initial microdata
profiling in lieu of access to the DSP.
o manage the metadata profiles of the products or domains for which
they are responsible.
6.4 RESULTING CONTRACT:
Service New Brunswick on behalf of the Department of Health Shared Analytics
is seeking to enter into a two (2) year contract with two (2) option-years. Option
years may be executed annually or in any part, not exceeding the maximum
number of years upon mutual agreement.
SNB on behalf of the Department of Health Shared Analytics reserves the right to

such solicitations will be based on the Department’s assessment of operational
requirements and the awarded vendor’s ability to meet those specific needs.
SNB’s intent would be to have solution deployed within the current fiscal year
ending March 31, 2026, following the award of the contract.
6.5 LANGUAGE REQUIREMENTS
The solution’s interface must be available in both English and French The
multilingual interface must include but is not limited to:
System Field labels (e.g. drop-down lists), titles, headers, footers, navigations
menus, and reports, user-generated content labels where applicable, and any

services with the Province here under.
7.0 PROPOSAL CONTENT & REQUIREMENTS
Proposals should include a table of contents and a response to each requirement
in the order in which it is presented in Appendix A.
NOTE: Responses to this RFP will be evaluated using a one stage
approach and as such all pricing information requested in section 7.4 must
be submitted in a separate electronic file in accordance with section 4.
7.1 MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
a) Submissions must be received in their entirety by the time and date indicated.
b) Submissions must be signed by an official of the company who is authorized
to sign on behalf of/and bind the company to statements made in their
submission.
c) Submissions must include a completed Appendix A – RFP Requirements
d) Submissions must include a completed Appendix B – Pricing Parameters
e) Submissions must include completed Appendix H – Attestations
Please note, appendix F - GNB IT Security and Procurement represents
minimum requirements. Anything in Appendix A with higher standards
supersedes the minimum requirement in appendix F - GNB IT Security and
Procurement. Any instances where it appears Appendix A requests lower
standards than those in appendix F, appendix F takes precedent.
Please note, prior to entering into contract, controls attested to during
procurement process will be validated.
7.2 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
Each qualified proposal will be evaluated based on the rated criteria as defined in
Section 8. Please reference section 6 for background information on the Solution
Requirements.
7.2.1 VENDOR, TECHNICAL, SECURITY BUSINESS REQUIREMENTS
Note: Appendix A - RFP Requirements contains seven (7) tabs. Tabs have been
titled to encompass the requirements for the various groups and end users that
will utilize the solution. Tabs are also grouped into areas:
• Index and Checklist (One (1) Grey-colored tab)
• Mandatory requirements. These describe requirements (Submission,
Vendor, Technical, and Security focused) that must be met to be given
further consideration. (One (1) Yellow-colored tab).
• Vendor /Vendor-Project requirements. These describe Shared Analytic
expectations from the Vendor. (One (1) Blue-colored tab).
• Technical, Security, and AI/ML requirements. These describe Technical,
Security, and AI/ML expectations from the solution. (Three (3) Green-
colored tabs).
• Business requirements. These describe business expectations from the
solution. (One (1) Maroon-colored tab).
Proponents should describe in the spreadsheets provided (Appendix A - RFP
Requirements) how they will meet the requirements. This should include details
of the approach, structure/design, strategy, methods, tools, and
policies/procedures as applicable.
When responding to the Mandatory requirements, please follow these
instructions:
• Mandatory requirements are indicated under the Mandatory (Y/N)
column.
• All Mandatory requirements must be met for the proposal to be given
further consideration.
• Failure to provide a response in the “Meets Requirements (Y/N)”
column, in the Mandatory tab, or not indicating “Yes”, for Mandatory
requirements will result in the proposal being disqualified from
further consideration.
When responding to the Scored requirements, please follow these
instructions:
• The “Priority Ranking” column describes the priority the requirement has
for the client. Priority Ranking values are Low, Medium, High.
• Under the “Response” column, the proponent should describe how the
proposed solution meets the requirements. Proponents are strongly
encouraged to describe their solution in enough detail for the Committee
(as described on Section 8) to evaluate how closely the solution meets the
requirements described.
Ambiguity will negatively impact evaluation scores. Alternately,
comprehensive notes and examples may add value and consequently the
proponent may score higher.
If descriptions for the “Response” column are lengthy, proponents may
use appendices in their response. Please reference any related appendix
in the response. Proponents are advised to use the requirement
numbering as detailed in Appendix A – RFP Requirements when
authoring responses.
7.2.2 PRESENTATION/DEMO
Following the technical evaluations, the department will request
presentations from up to five (5) of the highest scoring proponents having
met all the mandatory and minimum scored requirements of the RFP.
The presentations will be held virtually and can be scheduled Monday
through Friday from 8:15 am to 4:30 pm local time. The selected
proponents will be given ten (10) business days’ notice to prepare for their
scheduled presentation.
The presentation stage is an essential component of the evaluation
process and serves as a dynamic means to assess the practical
application of the proposed solution and how it aligns with the
requirements of this RFP.
Once the five (5) highest-ranking proponents are identified, SNB will
provide the requirements and criteria for the presentation. It is intended
that presentations will be scheduled for a two (2)-hour period, of which
thirty (30) minutes will be used for questions and answers.
Costs related to any responses or presentations are the responsibility of
the Proponents. Proponents shall not be permitted to present new
information or adjust proposal content.
7.3 Sub-contracting
Utilizing subcontractor(s) in the primary bidder’s response is acceptable. A joint
submission by two or more bidders having no formal corporate links is also
acceptable. However, in this case one of these bidders (the primary bidder) must
be prepared to take overall responsibility for successful interconnection of the
multiple organizations and this must be defined in the Proposal. Also, one firm
must act as the sole interface between the joint partners and the Department.
By submitting subcontractor information, the primary bidder agrees that they
have responsibility for the compliance of all named subcontractors to the
requirements imposed on the primary bidder in this RFP and any resulting
contract. The primary bidder confirms that they have reviewed all RFP
requirements, including privacy and security requirements with the
subcontractor(s), and each subcontractor agrees to comply with all applicable
legislation, policy, and practices as required of the primary bidder as described in
this RFP, it’s appendices (schedules), and any resulting contract that may be
issued.
The primary bidder must:
a) Identify any Subcontractors, providing information on each Subcontractor.
b) Identify which bidder is responsible for the overall project and describe how
the sub-contractor(s) will interconnect with the prime bidders.
c) Identify who will be the sole interface between the joint partners and the
Department.
7.4 PRICING
NOTE: All pricing information should be submitted in a separate electronic
document, in accordance with section 4 in the form of a completed Appendix
B - Pricing.
Appendix B - Pricing must include:
Costs for the initial implementation and two (2) years of individual annual
license/support contracts, including all costs (e.g., training, implementation,
support). Costs should be itemized, identified, and clearly separated into the
initial implementation and two (2) annual licensing/support costs. The total cost
of the initial term of two (2) years is what will be evaluated.
Guidelines to completing the Financial Proposal are:
(a) Prices must be:
• Fixed Price for the full implementation of a multilingual solution and initial
two (2) individual years of Licensing/Support contracts.
• In Canadian dollars.
• Exclusive of any applicable taxes.
The all-inclusive price must include (but is not limited to):
• Application Setup & Configuration Fee.
• Training Fees (training/train the trainer).
• All relevant fees based off of how proponent’s pricing model would relate to
the DSP information provided in APPENDIX C - DSP environment ‘Spec
sheet’
• Maintenance & Support Fees.
• Any other fees Shared Analytics may not be aware of.
In the financial proposal, detail any costs based on the inclusion of any functions
that are necessary and that Shared Analytics may not be anticipating or defining
in this RFP. Please clearly outline one (1) time expenses versus on-going
expenses. Financial proposal must outline a two (2) year total cost, which will be
evaluated as noted below in “Pricing Score”.
Note: After the initial two (2) year period, for an additional two (2) year
contract renewal period, should the optional period be mutually agreed
upon, the Vendor’s price shall not increase by more than two percent (2%)
or New Brunswick Consumer Pricing Index (CPI) All Items, (whichever is
lower).
Pricing Score: (lowest proposed price [MIN] X Marks [20points] / price on
proposal under evaluation [P] = total marks for price [Score].

7.5 APPENDICES / ATTACHMENTS
All materials submitted as appendices / attachments to the proposal should be
clearly indicated in the Table of Contents. Material not so documented by the
Vendor will be considered as extraneous information. This list of attachments
should also contain a brief description of the attached material, including what
information can be gained by the evaluation team from its examination of the
material.
8.0 EVALUATION PROCEDURE
A Committee made up of representatives from the Department of Health, Shared
Analytics Branch and the Strategic Procurement Division, Service New
Brunswick will evaluate all proposals. The accepted proposals will be used as the
basis for selecting the successful proponent(s).
The process will include a review and check of the information contained in the
proposals. SNB reserves the right to validate the highest scoring proponent’s
references prior to award.
8.1 EVALUATION CRITERIA
The evaluation of proposals will be conducted using a one (1)-stage process with

Following the technical evaluations the province will request presentations from

To whom it may concern,

On behalf of CGI, I would like to thank you for giving us the opportunity to submit this proposal in response to your Request for Proposal for Tender # 8026135-26 Data Sharing Platform Shared Analytics.

CGI is a Canadian multinational information technology consulting and systems integration company, established 49 years ago in Quebec City in 1976 by our two founders, Serge Godin, our current Chairman of the Board, and André Imbeau, former board member and advisor to the Chairman. Since opening our first Atlantic Canada office in 1991, CGI has expanded its services and presence, employing ~800 professionals across Nova Scotia, New Brunswick, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland. Our service mix now includes systems integration, IT consulting, business process services, and software application management, supported by local consulting practices, a global delivery center, and extensive infrastructure services. In 2001, CGI reinforced its commitment to Atlantic Canada through a landmark agreement with Service New Brunswick Inc., establishing our “g-Commerce Lab” at Fredericton’s Knowledge Park, which continues to drive innovation and government service delivery worldwide. Today, CGI is one of Atlantic Canada’s largest IT employers, delivering a full breadth of services to clients across Canada, the U.S., and around the globe.

We are confident that our experienced team will not only be the right fit for this engagement but will also exceed expectations in delivery. On behalf of CGI, it is my pleasure to submit this proposal for your review and consideration.

PROPRIETARY AND CONFIDENTIAL

The information contained in this document may be proprietary and confidential to CGI and/or to the receiving party. This document cannot be reproduced in any form or by any mechanical or electronic means, including electronic archival systems, without the written approval of CGI. The receiving party is exempt from this restriction for evaluation purposes only.

If you have received this document by mistake, note that the reading, reproduction, or distribution of this document is strictly forbidden. You are hereby requested to inform us by telephone at  and to return this document by certified mail.

Assumptions

As part of CGI’s submission for Service New Brunswick’s Data Sharing Platform (DSP) Data Catalogue RFP, CGI has outlined the following commercial and technical assumptions to ensure clarity, alignment, and completeness of the proposed solution. These assumptions are intended to support a shared understanding during evaluation and contract discussions, reinforcing healthy collaboration and transparency for both parties within the fixed‑price model defined in the RFP.
1. Fixed-Price Proposal and Cloud Consumption Considerations
The RFP requires a fixed price for the initial two-year period. CGI has structured pricing accordingly, based strictly on the scope and DSP data estate provided in the RFP.

As Microsoft Purview operates on a consumption-based model, ongoing costs will naturally be influenced by how the client chooses to use the platform. To maintain clarity and fairness for both parties:
Our fixed price covers all implementation, configuration, professional services, and support elements described in our proposal.
Microsoft Purview consumption costs remain directly aligned with the usage decisions and governance approach chosen by the client.

Should the Province wish to expand scope—by onboarding new data sources, increasing governance coverage, adjusting scan schedules, or enabling advanced data quality/ML capabilities—CGI will gladly adjust pricing through a mutually agreed change process.
This ensures predictability while supporting future flexibility.
2. Microsoft Licensing Options
CGI fully supports the Province in selecting the most advantageous path for Purview licensing.
Many public-sector organizations benefit from direct licensing through Microsoft, particularly when they already have enterprise agreements in place.
CGI is equally able to procure and administer Purview licensing on your behalf and collaborate directly with Microsoft to model future cost scenarios.
Whichever path the Province prefers, we will work collaboratively to ensure transparent, predictable cloud consumption and responsible cost management across the two-year term and beyond.
3. Technical and Scope Assumptions
The following assumptions provide the basis for our fixed-price estimate and reflect information available within the RFP.
Data Scope & Environment Assumptions
Scope is limited to the 81 structured relational databases and related metadata described in the RFP.
Total data volume (~17.1 TB + logs) and 346K structured metadata assets represent the full in-scope estate.
Unstructured sources (SharePoint, OneDrive, ADLS, Blob, File Shares, etc.) may be added in the future but are not included in the initial estimate.
Additional data lakes, analytics platforms, or new integrations may be incorporated through future change requests.
Built-in lineage extraction is assumed; advanced or custom lineage patterns can be added if required.
No third-party scanning engines or custom connectors are included at this stage.
Governance & Purview Consumption Assumptions
Scanning through the Purview Unified Catalog does not incur charges.
Only governed assets contribute toward billing.
A typical governed-asset ratio of 10–30% is assumed where the client has not yet defined a governance target.
DGPU usage applies when DQ/Data Health workloads are executed.
Initial use is expected to involve moderate DQ rules and profiling activities.
Moderate DGPU consumption is assumed based on the scan frequencies provided.
Increased profiling, ML-based classification, or enhanced DQ rules can be incorporated through future capacity refinements.
User population is assumed at ~110–135, with no major expansion of stewards or governance roles during the initial rollout.
Infrastructure Assumptions
Three SHIRs (Dev, UAT, Prod) and two Data Map Capacity Units are assumed for an S-size Purview deployment.
Standard Purview architectural patterns are assumed for this implementation.
Purview will operate using Microsoft’s Pay-As-You-Go Unified Catalog billing model.
The S-size profile is used as the baseline estimate based on the DSP estate provided.
4. Commitment to Long-Term Collaboration

CGI values its long-standing relationship with the Government of New Brunswick and remains committed to supporting the Shared Analytics Branch as it advances its data governance and analytics capabilities.
We are committed to:
Transparent communication
Predictable and responsible cost management
Flexibility as the Province’s needs evolve
A collaborative partnership grounded in trust and shared success
Our goal is to provide a scalable, future-ready data catalogue that supports the DSP’s mission of enabling evidence-informed decisions across the health and social services sectors.

PART 1 – INVITATION AND SUBMISSION INSTRUCTIONS
1.1 Invitation to Proponents
This Request for Proposals (the “RFP”) is an invitation by the Province of New Brunswick (the “Province”)
to prospective Proponents to submit proposals for the Provision, Implementation, and Support of a Court
Case Management System Replacement as further described in the RFP Particulars (Appendix D) (the
“Deliverables”). This RFP is being conducted pursuant to the Procurement Act, regulations thereunder,
and the Atlantic Standard Terms and Conditions (ASTC). In the event of conflict between the provisions of
the RFP and/or the ASTC and/or the overarching legislation, the latter prevails. In the event of a conflict
between the provisions of the RFP and the ASTC, the RFP prevails.
The Department of Justice and Public Safety (the “Department”) strives to provide quality programs and
services that enhance the safety and security of New Brunswickers and their communities, and a fair
accessible justice system. The vision of the Department is “Working together for a safe, secure and just
New Brunswick”.
Serving as a vital foundation for upholding the rule of law and ensuring equitable access to justice, the
Department seeks to modernize and integrate critical legacy systems used to manage court records. New
Brunswick’s court processes are primarily manual and paper-based, supported by custom built, aged
legacy information technology applications. These applications no longer meet the changing and dynamic
needs of the Department.
The Department is seeking a configurable, cloud-based, SaaS case management system to replace four (4)
legacy systems used across the New Brunswick Court of Appeal, Court of King’s Bench, and Provincial
Court. The Department is looking for a Proponent whose core system includes the components and
capabilities listed below and where the Proponent actively develops the system focused on the needs of
the courts.
System Components:
• User Dashboard
• Case and Party Management
• Public Access, Litigant/Justice Partner Portal, and Electronic Filing
• Scheduling
• Document/Email Management
• Document Generation
• Exhibit/Evidence Management
• Judicial Tools and Hearing Management
• Workflow/Task Management
• Accounting/Financial Management
• Electronic Payment Processing
• Records Management
System Capabilities:
• Multilingual (English and French) Supported
• Workflow Engine and Notifications
• Reporting and Analytics
• Search Engine
• Identity Management
• Business Rules Engine
• Enterprise Security
• Integration Engine
• Event Logging and Auditing
Each level of court is considered a separate business entity where data accessed and modified is based on
the security level a user is associated with. Court users may require different access levels to each level of
Court. Adult and youth matters will require different access levels. Each level of Court will have unique
workflow requirements.
The successful proponent will provide the following deliverables:
1. Identify and recommend an appropriate system which fulfills the Department’s requirements.
2. Software licenses required to implement the system.
3. Overall solution design and system documentation.
4. Project management methodology and project plan recommendations.
5. Organizational change management strategy and stakeholder communication plan.
6. Configuration of the software and quality assurance strategy.
7. Data migration/conversion.
8. Integration.
9. Testing.
10. Training.
11. Implementation/Go-Live Support.
12. Ongoing operational support and maintenance post go-live.
13. Reporting components.
14. Cloud hosting.
Additional information regarding the deliverables is included in RFP Particulars (Appendix D).
Additional information on the Department’s structure; current technology environment and challenges;
current interfaces; and organizational challenges can be found in the Overview of the Department of
Justice and Public Safety (Appendix E).

The selected Proponent will be requested to enter direct contract negotiations to finalize an agreement
with the Province for the provision of the Deliverables. The terms and conditions found in the Form of
Agreement (Appendix A) are to form the basis for commencing negotiations between the Province and
the selected Proponent. The final agreement will be substantially in the form of Appendix A subject to
