• BMS systems control mechanical and facility infrastructure such as HVAC, chillers, and building automation systems.
The DCIM platform may integrate with an existing BMS to ingest environmental or electrical monitoring data; however, it does
not replace or directly control building systems.
Implementation and Support
CGI will serve as the prime contractor and delivery partner, providing end-to-end implementation leadership and governance.
Responsibilities include:
• Requirements validation and solution configuration
• System integration and data migration
• Training and operational onboarding
• Governance oversight and escalation management
Nlyte will provide the core software platform, vendor-level technical support, and ongoing product roadmap development.
Business and Operational Value
The proposed DCIM solution delivers measurable operational and governance benefits, including:
• Improved infrastructure visibility and control
• Enhanced capacity planning and utilization
• Reduced operational risk during infrastructure changes
• Increased accountability through structured workflows
• Alignment with recognized data center best practices
The platform is recommended by the Uptime Institute and is deployed within CGI’s own operational environments, providing
additional assurance of its maturity, reliability, and operational suitability.

2.2 Elevated Support
2.2.1 Deployment Plan
Proponents should:
• Describe their approach to delivering a coordinated deployment plan that makes the client fully operational.
• Include timelines, milestones, and resource planning to achieve deployment of a single site with 6-10 racks.
• Identify a single point of contact who will oversee deployment activities as the project manager.
The timeline to deploy a single site with 6–10 racks, including all configuration items (CIs), single-line diagrams, and DC
infrastructure, is typically 18 to 20 weeks, depending on the accuracy and completeness of the initial data provided.
To ensure efficient implementation and minimize manual configuration, the recommended approach for data onboarding is
a mass data upload methodology. This approach enables rapid population of assets, connectivity, and infrastructure records
and is the standard method used for large-scale deployments.
Using mass data upload, full data implementation and validation can be completed within a 6–8 month timeframe, including
verification, reconciliation, and operational readiness. This method significantly reduces deployment risk, improves data
accuracy, and accelerates time to value.
CGI will work in conjunction with its implementation partner Nlyte to deliver a coordinated, milestone-driven deployment plan
resulting in a fully operational DCIM environment aligned to SNB’s priorities. CGI will serve as the prime contractor and
maintain full accountability for delivery execution, vendor coordination, and stakeholder alignment.
Account Management and Governance Structure During Deployment
CGI will provide a structured account governance model to ensure clear accountability, effective communication, and
coordinated delivery of services associated with the DCIM solution. CGI will serve as the prime contractor and single point of
accountability, managing all aspects of service delivery while coordinating directly with Nlyte for product-related matters and
maintaining direct engagement with SNB.
The governance structure is organized across executive oversight, account management, and operational delivery tiers:
• Executive Sponsor (CGI): Provides strategic accountability, contractual alignment, executive escalation
management, and participates in governance reviews.
• Account Manager (CPMO): Serves as the primary commercial contact responsible for contract performance, vendor
coordination, SLA monitoring, and escalation oversight.
• Service Delivery Manager: Oversees day-to-day delivery execution, incident and change governance, and
operational coordination.
• Technical Lead / Solution Architect: Provides architectural oversight, integration design, configuration governance,
and technical escalation support.
• Nlyte: Provides product-level support, defect resolution, roadmap coordination, and release management (managed
through CGI).
A formal escalation path will be established: Operational Support → Service Delivery Manager → Account Manager →
Executive Sponsor.

Professional Services Scope
The proposed Professional Services include project management, training, installation, and initial configuration services to

Project Management services will be delivered in accordance with established best practices for Nlyte deployments. A

of four (4) days of instruction covering Nlyte Asset Optimizer and Nlyte Energy Optimizer modules. The training program is

2.2.2 Support and Service Level Agreement (SLA)
Proponents should detail their ability to meet the following requirements for ongoing support and service delivery:
2.2.2.1 Support Access and Availability
Describe how users will access support (e.g., via telephone, email) and how support will be available five days a week,
eight hours per day. Include specifics such as time zones and available hours.
CGI will serve as the primary support interface and single point of accountability for all matters related to the DCIM solution.
System Access
The DCIM solution is delivered as a secure, web-based platform accessible via modern industry-standard browsers.
Access is governed through:
• Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
• Integration with enterprise directory services (LDAP/Active Directory)
• Granular permissions based on user roles
• Secure authentication and encrypted communication (TLS 1.3 compliant)
• Logical segmentation by site, tenant, or organizational group as required
Support Model

• Coordinated escalation with Nlyte product support
• Issue resolution management
• Configuration and integration guidance
• Upgrade planning support

• Defined response times
• Access to vendor knowledge base
Elevated / Priority Support (Optional)

• Acknowledging receipt of issues within one hour of contact.

Acknowledgement of receipt of issues can be measured by email response or incident-tracking mechanisms, as mutually

CGI will assign primary (Manager-level) and escalation (Director-level) roles for client engagement.

2.3 Risks and Mitigations
Solution Fit and Functional Coverage
Risk:
Some advanced capabilities (e.g., deep power simulation, physical security integration, or advanced virtualization telemetry)
may not be fully native within the DCIM platform.
Mitigation:
CGI conducts a structured requirements validation and gap assessment during onboarding to confirm scope alignment. Where
required, integrations with third-party systems or phased capability adoption can be planned to ensure operational needs are
met without custom development.
Integration Complexity
Risk:
Integration with enterprise systems (ITSM, CMDB, virtualization platforms, billing systems) can introduce complexity
depending on the client’s existing architecture and data quality.
Mitigation:
The solution provides native connectors and APIs to reduce integration effort. CGI’s systems integration expertise and proven
delivery methodology are used to design, test, and validate integrations prior to production deployment, minimizing risk to
existing systems.
Data Migration and Data Quality
Risk:
Incomplete, inconsistent, or outdated source data may impact migration accuracy and initial reporting quality.
Mitigation:
CGI supports structured data migration using Excel-based imports and APIs, supplemented by data validation and cleansing
activities. Optional physical audits and proof-of-concept exercises can be used to validate data accuracy before full

Users may initially underutilize advanced DCIM features if processes and roles are not clearly defined.

CGI provides role-based training, onboarding support, and configuration aligned to operational workflows. The solution’s
configuration-driven approach enables gradual adoption without disrupting existing operations.
Availability and Resilience Expectations
Risk:
Stakeholders may assume built-in high availability or disaster recovery capabilities beyond what is included in the standard
deployment.

CGI clearly defines deployment architecture, availability characteristics, and optional resilience configurations during solution
design. Where required, the solution can be aligned with the client’s existing infrastructure standards and resilience strategies.

Future feature availability is dependent on the vendor’s product roadmap.
Mitigation:
Nlyte maintains a documented product roadmap, and CGI’s long-standing partnership provides early visibility into planned
enhancements. CGI actively engages with the vendor to align roadmap priorities with client requirements.

CGI, in partnership with Nlyte, has reviewed the requirements outlined in this solicitation and confirms that the proposed DCIM
solution provides substantial compliance with the stated technical, functional, and operational requirements.
The solution delivers strong alignment with core DCIM capabilities, including centralized asset and capacity management,
visualization, power and environmental monitoring, workflow support, enterprise integration, and role-based access control.
The platform is recommended by the Uptime Institute and is actively used within CGI’s own operational environments,

Areas of Full Compliance
The solution fully meets requirements related to:
• Centralized DCIM management across data centers, colocation, and edge locations
• Asset, space, and power visualization and reporting
• Role-based access control and user management
• Workflow and change management support for IMAC activities
• Integration with enterprise platforms including ITSM, CMDB, virtualization, and billing systems
• API and integration capabilities for data exchange
• Reporting, dashboards, and export functionality
• Configuration-driven implementation without the need for custom code
• Security controls, including TLS 1.3 compliance
• Training, data migration, and proof-of-concept support.
Areas of Partial Compliance
Some requirements are partially met, typically where:

• Physical security access control (e.g., CAC/RFID door locks)

• Native project management tooling
• Deep virtualization telemetry beyond standard infrastructure visibility

2. CALL-UP PROCEUDRE FOR SERVICES
2.1 Purchase Orders. A separate Purchase Order (“PO”) must be executed by both parties for
each separate Service or group of Services that the Province determines, in its sole
discretion, to obtain from the Supplier during the Term of this Agreement.
2.2 Initiation of the Call-Up Procedure. The Province will issue a Statement of Work (SOW)
for each separate Service or group of Services that the Province determines to obtain from
the Supplier. Each such SOW will include or incorporate by reference the information
identified in the attached Schedule “A.3” (Statements of Work) and shall be in the form
determined by the Province. The delivery of a SOW by the Province to the Supplier will
initiate the Call-Up Procedure for Services under this Agreement.
2.3 Call-Up Process. Upon the delivery of a SOW by the Province to the Supplier as
contemplated under Section 2.2 (Initiation of the Call-Up Procedure), the following process
will apply:
(a) The Supplier shall prepare a response to the SOW describing how the Supplier
will perform the Services requested under the SOW (the “SOW Proposal”) within
five (5) Business Days (or such longer or shorter period of time as required by the
Province, acting reasonably and having regard to the nature and complexity of the
Services in question). For the purposes of this Agreement, “Business Day(s)”
means Monday to Friday, excluding statutory and civic holidays observed in Nova
Scotia and any other day on which the Province has elected to be closed for
business.
(b) The SOW Proposal will address all of the details requested by the Province under
the SOW, and will, unless otherwise instructed by the Province, address the
matters described in Schedule “A.3” (Statements of Work).
(c) The Province shall then assess the SOW Proposal based on criteria that are
identified in the SOW (if any), including, without limitation: (i) the Supplier’s
experience with the requested Services; (ii) the Supplier’s financial proposal to
perform the Services; and (iii) the project methodology, timing, and approach
proposed by the Supplier for performance of the Services.
(d) The Province shall then provide the Supplier with a written response to the SOW
Proposal within ten (10) Business Days (or such longer or shorter period of time
as required by the Province) of completion of the Province’s assessment of the
SOW Proposal, indicating the Province’s approval of the SOW Proposal, its
rejection of the SOW Proposal, or the terms of a counter proposal acceptable to
the Province. For greater certainty, the Province shall have no obligation to
approve a SOW Proposal and may, in its discretion, terminate the Call-Up
Procedure at any time.
(e) Each SOW Proposal accepted and approved by both parties in writing will
constitute a binding commitment between the parties for the performance of the

The schedule for payments owed by the Province to the Supplier for performance of the Services will be in
accordance with that described in Schedule A.2 (Supplier’s RFSQ Proposal) and each approved SOW, unless
otherwise authorized by the Province in writing.
3. C.3 Professional Services Per Diem Rates
The per diem rates for professional services, if any, will be in accordance with that described in Schedule A.2
(Supplier’s RFSQ Proposal), unless otherwise authorized by the Province in writing. If such rates are not
described in the Supplier’s RFSQ Proposal, the Province will not be liable to pay any such rates unless and
until such rates are first authorized by the Province in writing. Such rates will be effective for the Initial Term of
this Agreement.
4. C.4 Changes to Fees; Economic Change Adjustment
The Supplier shall not increase the fees payable under this Agreement during the Initial Term, including that no
fees will be subject to any adjustments for increases in cost of living or inflation or for any changes in foreign
exchange rates. At the beginning of each Renewal Term (if and to the extent exercised by the Province in
accordance with this Agreement), the Supplier may increase the fees chargeable to the Province to reflect
annual increases in consumer prices, if the Supplier can demonstrate, to the satisfaction of the Province, that
the Supplier’s costs have increased significantly from the Initial Term, and the Supplier’s cost increases can be
independently verified by the Province. This increase (if applicable) will not exceed the average increase in the
Consumer Price Index (CPI) over the prior 12 months preceding the effective contract renewal date. CPI as
used herein means the “Informatics Professional Services Prices Index” published by Statistics Canada. If this
index is no longer published, the Parties shall mutually agree on an alternative replacement index.

Description
This request for standing offer (RSO) is an invitation by the Nova Scotia Liquor Corporation
(the “NSLC”) to prospective proponents to submit proposals for Professional Information
Technology Services, as per the specifications. The term of this agreement will be 5 years.
Pricing must be firm for this period
-Year 1 and 2 to run from date of award to November 30, 2023
Optional Years
-Year 3 to run from December 1, 2023 to November 30, 2024
-Year 4 to run from December 1, 2024 to November 30, 2025
-Year 5 to run from December 1, 2025 to November 30, 2026
Optional Years:
NSLC reserves the right to request extensions for additional years (years three through five)
or to re-quote. If extension(s) are requested by NSLC, vendor will have the option to
submit an increase at the time of the extension requires for consideration by NSLC. NSLC
can accept the increase or re-quote.
Onboarding Note:
This IT Standing Offer (ITSO) list will be open to onboard new proponents, at the end of the
first two-year term of this RSO. Proponents chosen under this RSO will not need to reapply
at the end of the first two year term but will have an opportunity to provide a list of new
additional services, if applicable, that they did not have to offer under this current RSO.
Submission Closing Deadline / Delivery
The RSO submission must be signed and emailed to Tenders@mynslc.com. Submissions
must be received on or before the submission closing deadline of November 16, 2021 @
2:00 PM AST. (Halifax local time). Please indicate the NSLC Reference No. and Title on the
email’s subject line. Please ensure you receive an automatic reply that confirms your
message has been delivered to this general inbox. Reach out to the contact noted in section
4a for any issues.
NOTE: DO NOT SEND SUBMISSIONS TO THE CONTACT STATED IN ENQUIRIES
SECTION.
Submissions received after the closing date and time will be disqualified from competition.
NSLC will not make allowances for delays due to factors such as email server delays and
power outages. NSLC strongly encourages proponents to avoid waiting until the final
calendar day to submit responses to mitigate any unforeseen circumstances.

Contact below via email:

other representatives of the NSLC, other than the NSLC Contact, concerning matters

be included in the submitted price.

public body for the purposes of the Freedom of Information and Protection of Privacy Act
(FOIPOP). All records in the custody or control of the NSLC (including any proposals and
attachments submitted in response to this request for proposals) are subject to public
release to applicants under FOIPOP, subject to some limited exceptions. Confidential
materials related to a third party are addressed under s. 21 of FOIPOP. Any proponent that

satisfy the mandatory submission requirements within the Rectification Period of one
day, its proposal will be excluded from further consideration. The Rectification Period

will begin to run from the date that NSLC issues a rectification notice to the
proponent.

this information.

1. BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE
1.1. Business Context
The Nova Scotia Liquor Corporation (NSLC) is one of Nova Scotia’s largest
retailers and the fourth largest retailer of beverage alcohol in Canada. A crown
corporation, the NSLC operates 104 retail stores, supplies 60 Agency Stores,
and 2,100 licensees throughout the province. By providing superior customer
convenience and service, the NSLC returns substantial revenue to the
provincial government while ensuring the responsible enjoyment of beverage
alcohol in Nova Scotia.
The purpose of this RSO is to simplify the procurement of Information
Technology professional services on a Standing Offer basis from private sector
vendors (or consortia of vendors) to provide a broad range of professional
resources for consulting, design, analysis, technical support, training and
programming services for IT projects and support. The use of this Standing
Offer is to obtain professional services to address IT requirements on short
notice or on a short-term basis (typically engagements of six months or less,
not to be used to complete multi-phased larger projects) with a maximum
budget of $100,000 per project. Professional service requirements for multi-
phased larger projects (over $100,000) will be competitively sourced
separately in accordance the NSLC Procurement Policy.
IT professional services may include any work and/or consultation associated
with assessment, planning, design, development, installation, evaluation,
training, support, and other functions of IT-related applications and/or IT-
specialized technologies, methodologies, software, and hardware which require
the use of IT professionals.

renewal of three one- year extensions totaling a possible 5 years, unless at

2.3 Service Delivery Requirements
The following will prevail as enduring requirements for service delivery
throughout the effective period of the Standing Offer. Any Supplier who fails
to meet any one of these requirements may, at the discretion of the NSLC,
be removed from the Standing Offer:
 During the contract, the proposed resources will be required to
work either onsite and/or offsite, as requested by the NSLC.
 The successful supplier will be required to attend or
participate in regular project meetings.
 Suppliers must complete a Statement of Work provided by the
NSLC. The Statement of Work will detail the services to be
performed and will be used by NSLC departments to acquire quotes
for the work required.
 Suppliers must commence project work only after having received
a duly completed Purchase Order from a NSLC. Suppliers who
conduct work before having received a Purchase Order are subject
to immediate removal from the Standing Offer.
 Any invoices submitted for services rendered must include a detailed
breakdown of the work completed, the resource(s) being used to
support the amount that is invoiced, the per diem rate of the
resource and a reference to the Purchase Order provided by the NSLC.
 Suppliers who conduct work that exceeds the maximum dollar limit of
$100,000 per project are subject to immediate removal from the
Standing Offer.
 Upon request, the Supplier will provide a resource’s résumés in
electronic format within two business days of the request.
 If a resource is not available upon request the Supplier may provide
a substitute resource of similar qualifications if agreed upon by the
NSLC. The rate of the substitute shall not exceed the rate of the
original resource.
 The proposed rates that are accepted during the evaluation of this
Standing Offer will not increase during the contract period.
 If travel or living expenses are involved, they must be negotiated at
the time of call-up.

2.9 Definition of a Day
A day is defined as seven hours exclusive of meal breaks. ITSO suppliers will
be paid the agreed upon per diem rate for every seven hours of work done.
Fees payable will be calculated by dividing the total hours worked by
seven, and then multiplying the result by the rate agreed-to by the client
organization during call-up negotiations.
3. Administrative and Legal Requirements
3.1. Business Registration
NS law requires all businesses operating within the Province of Nova Scotia to
register with the NS ‘Registry of Joint Stock Companies’ (RJSC) with some
exceptions for New Brunswick (NB) suppliers who are registered with the NB
‘Corporate Affairs Registry’ (CAR). Fees are payable when first registering
and also annually to keep the registration active. Also, suppliers who
undergo name changes, mergers or acquisitions will need to update their
business registration accordingly.
The status of a respondent’s business registration does not preclude the
Submission issued in response to any tender. A Submission can be
accepted for evaluation while a tender is open, regardless of (i) whether the
company is registered, or (ii) whether its business registration is in good
standing (i.e.: status is ‘active’). However, a problem can arise at the time
of award if either of these conditions is not met.
NSLC will issue a Purchase Order for a Successful Respondent using the
same name as that reflected in its RJSC or CAR business registration. But
the award cannot be made (i) if the company is not registered with RJSC
or CAR or (ii) if its business registration is not in good standing (i.e.: any
status other than ‘active’).
Therefore, to facilitate the award if your Submission is successful, please address
one of the following as part of your Submission:
1. Include in your Submission your business registration profile, as can
be obtained in the public domain from the RJSC or CAR Web sites.
This profile should clearly state: (i) the company’s legal name as
appropriate for using in a potential contract, (ii) the business
registration number, and the (iii) the current status of
registration at the time of your Submission. If your registration is not
in good standing (status of ‘active’), describe your plan to correct
this should your firm be selected for the ITSO.
OR
2. If your company is currently not registered in NS or NB,
describe your plan to become registered in either of these
provinces should your firm be selected for the ITSO.
